Job Position: Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst
Role Summary
The Senior Cyber Threat Intelligence Analyst serves as a senior member of the Cyber Threat Intelligence program and is responsible for independently collecting, analyzing, enriching, and disseminating actionable intelligence on emerging cyber threats, adversary activity, and evolving attack trends. This role transforms complex technical and strategic threat information into actionable insights that support security operations, incident response, vulnerability management, and enterprise risk decisions.
The ideal candidate possesses deep expertise in cyber threat intelligence tradecraft, threat actor tracking, infrastructure analysis, and intelligence production. They operate with minimal supervision, lead complex intelligence investigations, provide authoritative threat assessments, and serve as a trusted advisor to technical teams and leadership. Success requires strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, technical curiosity, and the ability to communicate intelligence effectively across a broad range of stakeholders.
Your Opportunity
NXP is a global player in Semiconductor industry, and security is an essential and integral part of our business.
Job Responsibility
Monitor and assess emerging cyber threats, adversary activity, malware campaigns, and vulnerability exploitation trends.
Track threat actors and analyze their capabilities, targeting, infrastructure, and tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs).
Conduct technical investigations using threat intelligence, open-source intelligence (OSINT), and infrastructure analysis techniques.
Correlate intelligence from multiple sources and assess potential impact to the organization.
Lead indicator of compromise (IOC) collection, enrichment, validation, and lifecycle management activities.
Maintain intelligence records, indicators, and threat artifacts within the organization’s Threat Intelligence Platform (TIP).
Develop and disseminate actionable threat advisories, intelligence reports, and emerging threat notifications.
Support intelligence-sharing efforts with internal stakeholders and trusted external partners.
Produce tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence products for technical and business audiences.
Deliver intelligence briefings to security teams, leadership, and other stakeholders.
Provide threat-informed recommendations that improve organizational awareness and preparedness.
Serve as a subject matter expert on adversary activity, emerging threats, and cyber risk trends.
Provide intelligence support during cybersecurity investigations and incident response activities.
Perform adversary-focused analysis to support incident scoping, attribution, and impact assessments.
Partner with Security Operations, Vulnerability Management, and Risk teams to provide threat context and intelligence insights.
Identify intelligence gaps, emerging risks, and opportunities to strengthen defensive capabilities.
Job Qualification
Professional Experience
10+ years of experience in Cyber Threat Intelligence, Threat Research, Incident Response, Security Operations, or related cybersecurity disciplines.
Demonstrated experience tracking threat actors, malware campaigns, adversary infrastructure, and emerging cyber threats.
Experience producing tactical, operational, and strategic intelligence products for technical and executive audiences.
Proven ability to independently conduct investigations, develop actionable intelligence, and brief stakeholders.
Familiarity with nation-state actors, sophisticated cybercriminal groups, and supply chain threats.
Experience in intelligence-driven hunting to identify suspicious network activity and potential risks.
Technical Skills
Strong understanding of threat intelligence tradecraft, intelligence lifecycle methodologies, and frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.
Knowledge of cyber threat intelligence frameworks and methodologies including MITRE ATT&CK, ATT&CK Navigator, Diamond Model, Cyber Kill Chain, STIX/TAXII, Intelligence Lifecycle, and Structured Analytic Techniques.
Experience with Threat Intelligence Platforms such as Anomali, ThreatQ, ThreatConnect, OpenCTI, MISP, or similar platforms.
Proficiency with intelligence and OSINT tools such as Maltego, VirusTotal, Shodan, Censys, DomainTools, PassiveTotal, GreyNoise, URLScan, SecurityTrails, or similar investigative platforms.
Knowledge of threat actor clustering methodologies used to track adversary campaigns, intrusion sets, and threat group activity.
Experience conducting infrastructure analysis involving domains, DNS, passive DNS, IP addresses, ASNs, WHOIS records, certificates, hosting providers, and internet-facing assets.
Familiarity with STIX/TAXII, YARA, Sigma, Snort, Suricata, malware analysis concepts, and intelligence automation techniques.
Experience with Python, data mining, Elasticsearch, ELK Stack, Databricks, large-scale data analysis, and threat intelligence correlation workflows.
Soft Skills
Strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, and technical curiosity.
Strong communication and technical writing skills.
Ability to communicate intelligence effectively to technical, business, and leadership stakeholders.
Ability to operate with minimal supervision and lead complex intelligence investigations.
Certifications (Preferred)
Industry certifications such as GCTI, CTIA, GCIH, GCFA, CISSP, or equivalent cybersecurity and threat intelligence certifications.

Security Mindset: Deep understanding of automated threat mitigation, policy-as-code principles, and cloud-native security orchestration.
Hybrid Expertise: Proven ability to manage and automate security policies across complex hybrid or multi-cloud infrastructures (AWS, GCP, Azure).

Job Description
Position Overview
We are seeking a highly skilled and strategic Principal Observability & Event Management Engineer to champion enterprise-wide initiatives that improve monitoring effectiveness, reduce alert noise, and accelerate incident response.
In this dual-impact role, you will act as both a strategic leader and a hands-on technical expert. You will define the enterprise standards for multi-domain monitoring (infrastructure, cloud, application, network, batch, and mainframe) while actively designing and configuring our Event Management platforms—specifically Oracle Unified Assurance (Assure1) and IBM Netcool. The ideal candidate will leverage data insights, machine learning, and automation to transform massive "event storms" into high-fidelity, actionable signals.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership & Governance
Drive Enterprise Initiatives: Own and lead cross-functional, enterprise-wide initiatives focused on improving monitoring effectiveness, optimizing alert quality, and reducing incident volumes.
Define Standards: Establish corporate standards, approaches, and best practices for alert optimization across infrastructure, application, batch, network, and mainframe environments.
Culture & Mentorship: Mentor, guide, and evangelize a strong observability and optimization mindset across engineering and operations teams.
Continuous Improvement: Identify systemic gaps in monitoring design and lead long-term, architectural improvements to eliminate redundant or low-value alerts.
Platform Engineering & Administration
Infrastructure Design: Implement, maintain, and scale Oracle Assure1 / Unified Assurance servers and architectures for high-availability (HA) enterprise environments.
Event Correlation & Enrichment: Develop advanced Object-Server configurations, triggers, and correlation rules to distinguish isolated anomalies from critical root causes.
Multi-Vendor Integration: Integrate multi-vendor telemetry, logs, faults, and data from disparate monitoring domains into a single, unified Event Management UI.
Operations & Backend Support: Manage backend databases (e.g., MySQL, OpenSearch), maintain platform availability, and troubleshoot complex backend issues.
Automation, AIOps & Incident Response
Incident Automation: Write robust automation scripts and workflows to bridge monitoring tools with ITSM platforms (such as ServiceNow) to accelerate incident response times.
AIOps & Root Cause Analysis (RCA): Apply Machine Learning (ML) algorithms, topological discovery, and data-driven approaches to enhance event correlation, suppress noise, and automate self-healing or ticket generation.

Required Qualifications & Skills
Experience & Education
Total Experience: 5+ years of dedicated experience in enterprise Event Management, Fault Management, Service Level Management, or production environments.
Initiative Leadership: 3+ years of proven experience leading large-scale, cross-functional improvements in monitoring effectiveness, alert optimization, or incident reduction.
Technical Expertise
Platform Expertise: Hands-on, deep technical experience with Oracle Unified Assurance / Assure1 and/or IBM Netcool suites (OMNIbus, Netcool Impact, ITM).
OS & Scripting: Strong proficiency in Linux Administration (RHEL) and expert-level scripting skills (Python, Bash, Perl, or Shell) for building event parsers and API integrations.
Databases & APIs: Solid understanding of backend database management, SQL queries, REST APIs, and tool customization using rule files and OpenSearch.

Motorola Solutions designs its UC ecosystem so that frontline workers, field technicians, office supervisors, and public safety personnel can collaborate seamlessly regardless of the device they carry or the network they connect to.
Key principles include:
Any Network, Any Device: Connecting traditional two-way radios (such as MOTOTRBO or APX P25) directly to smartphones, tablets, laptops, and dedicated broadband push-to-talk (PTT) handhelds.
Instant Push-to-Talk (PTT): Expanding high-reliability, sub-second PTT audio from dedicated radio talkgroups to cellular and Wi-Fi networks.
Integration of Voice, Video, and Data: Unifying voice talkgroups with streaming video (body cameras, fixed surveillance), multimedia messaging, GPS location tracking, and telemetry.

WAVE PTX (Broadband Push-to-Talk)
A subscription-based carrier-independent cloud service that turns smartphones, tablets, and PCs into push-to-talk communication devices.

Bridges MOTOTRBO/TETRA/P25 radio systems with cellular networks.

Hybrid Smart Devices (e.g., MOTOTRBO Ion)
Ruggedized devices that combine the mission-critical audio and durability of a two-way radio with the multimedia and touchscreen capabilities of an Android smartphone.

AI Principal Architect
Mastercard's Business & Market Insights (B&MI) group empowers organizations to achieve growth and innovation goals by delivering unparalleled data-driven intelligence and cutting-edge AI solutions. By harnessing proprietary data, frontier generative AI, and global expertise, B&MI helps businesses make smarter, faster, and more impactful decisions. We transform complex, multi-modal data into agentic systems and generative applications that drive measurable business outcomes and sustained competitive advantage.
We're looking for a Principal Architect, Generative AI & ML Engineering, for the Operational Intelligence Program within B&MI. As a principal-level technical leader, you'll define the architecture vision and technical strategy for our agentic AI platform. On this platform, agents make extensive tool calls into enterprise services and APIs and must run securely, reliably, and at scale. You'll set the standards teams build on across tool calling, multi-agent orchestration, self-correcting agents, memory, retrieval, and LLMOps. You'll also make the key decisions on models, platforms, and trade-offs. Working closely with engineering, product, security, and business leaders, you'll shape the long-term direction of Gen AI across B&MI and mentor architects and senior engineers. You'll also stay hands-on with prototypes that de-risk big bets. The hardest problems in enterprise Gen AI are reliability, integration, security, and scale. If you've solved them as a backend or distributed systems architect and have started applying that experience to LLM systems, we'd love to hear from you.
Roles & Responsibilities
• Own the architecture and technical roadmap for the Operational Intelligence Gen AI platform, defining reference architectures and standards that teams across the program can reuse and scale.
• Architect the enterprise tool-calling layer, setting standards for how internal services, data platforms, and external APIs are exposed to agents as tools. This covers schemas, contracts, versioning, access control, and resilient execution (parallel and chained calls, retries, timeouts, idempotency, circuit breakers, and fallbacks).
• Set the architecture for multi-agent and skills-based agent systems (e.g., LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen), including when to use agents versus deterministic workflows and how agents coordinate, delegate, and share context.
• Design self-correcting agent patterns: tool critics and verifiers that check tool selection, arguments, and results, plus reflection and plan-and-execute loops that catch errors before agents act or respond.
• Architect agent memory and state for long-running, multi-step sessions, including short- and long-term memory (e.g., Mem0, Zep, LangGraph memory), session persistence, and memory scoping and retention.
• Define retrieval architecture for grounded reasoning, including Self-RAG, Corrective RAG (CRAG), adaptive retrieval, and Graph-RAG, built on vector databases (e.g., Pinecone, pgvector, OpenSearch) and knowledge graphs (e.g., Neo4j, AWS Neptune).
• Design the inference and orchestration layer for high throughput, covering async processing, streaming, caching, rate limiting, and model routing across OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini, and open-source models.
• Establish the LLMOps architecture on Databricks (AWS), including MLflow, CI/CD for prompts and agents, and model lineage. Set platform-wide evaluation and observability standards: end-to-end tracing of tool calls, tool-selection accuracy, task success rates, cost, and latency.
• Build security and Responsible AI into the architecture, including guardrails, prompt-injection defenses, hallucination mitigation, data privacy, and audit trails that meet Mastercard's data ethics and regulatory standards.
• Own key architecture decisions and trade-offs, such as build versus buy, model and vendor selection, and cost versus latency versus accuracy, documented through architecture decision records. Assess emerging models, frameworks, and standards such as MCP for production readiness.
• Lead design reviews and partner with engineering, product, security, and data teams to align on architecture and raise the engineering bar across the program.
• Stay hands-on, building prototypes and reference implementations that de-risk decisions and give teams a working starting point.

• Deep expertise in API design and systems integration, including contracts, security models, and reliability patterns for services consumed by many teams. You understand what changes when the consumer is an LLM.
• Hands-on experience designing and shipping LLM-powered systems in production, especially agents that use tool/function calling, memory, and retrieval, and a clear view of how they fail.
• Strong Python skills for hands-on prototyping (async programming, FastAPI or similar), plus SQL proficiency.
• Deep experience with at least one major cloud platform (AWS preferred; Azure or GCP welcome), including its AI services such as Bedrock, SageMaker, Azure OpenAI, or Vertex AI.
• A solid grounding in security, privacy, and compliance for enterprise systems, ideally in financial services or another regulated industry.

• Nice to have: hands-on experience with tool critics, Self-RAG, CRAG, reflection loops, memory frameworks such as Mem0 or Zep, MCP tool servers, or agent evaluation frameworks.

Title and Summary
Senior Data Scientist
Our Purpose
Mastercard powers economies and empowers people in 200+ countries and territories worldwide. Together with our customers, we’re helping build a sustainable economy where everyone can prosper. We support a wide range of digital payments choices, making transactions secure, simple, smart and accessible. Our technology and innovation, partnerships and networks combine to deliver a unique set of products and services that help people, businesses and governments realize their greatest potential.
Overview
The Security Solutions Data Science team develops AI and machine learning capabilities that help protect the global payments ecosystem from fraud and cyber threats. Supporting Mastercard’s fraud and risk product, the team builds and enhances models that analyze billions of transactions and enable real-time detection of fraudulent activity.
We are looking for a highly motivated Senior Data Scientist to help build the next generation of AI-powered fraud detection systems. This role offers an opportunity to work on challenging problems involving predictive modeling, AI agents, LLM-based solutions, real-time decisioning systems, and large-scale data engineering while contributing directly to Mastercard's mission of enabling secure and trusted commerce worldwide.
Role
As a Senior Data Scientist, you will design, develop, and deploy enterprise-scale AI solutions that enhance fraud detection and risk intelligence capabilities across Mastercard's Security Solutions portfolio.
This is not just a model development role; it is ideal for someone who enjoys working closely with complex data, exploring patterns, deeply understanding business and technical problems, experimenting through R&D, and translating practical solutions into scalable fraud and security capabilities.
Key responsibilities include:
Develop, deploy, and optimize machine learning models for fraud detection, risk scoring, anomaly detection, and related security applications.
Build scalable AI and ML pipelines supporting model training, validation, deployment, monitoring, and retraining.
Design and implement Generative AI and Agentic AI solutions leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs), retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), reasoning and planning workflows, Chain-of-Thought-style prompting techniques, tool/function calling, LLM-based modular systems, and multi-agent orchestration.
Partner with AI Engineers and Data Scientists to productionize advanced models and translate research into scalable business solutions.
Work with large-scale transactional datasets using distributed computing technologies such as Spark and Databricks.
Implement MLOps best practices, including CI/CD, model governance, observability, experimentation frameworks, and performance monitoring.
Contribute to the design of reusable AI platforms, libraries, and engineering frameworks that accelerate AI development across teams.
Evaluate emerging AI technologies and identify opportunities to apply them to fraud prevention and security challenges.
Contribute to Mastercard's innovation efforts by publishing top-tier research papers, filing patents, and translating applied AI research into scalable fraud and security solutions.
Ensure solutions meet Mastercard standards for scalability, reliability, explainability, security, and responsible AI.
All About You
Strong programming skills in Python and experience building production-quality software.
Solid understanding of machine learning fundamentals, including supervised learning, ensemble methods, feature engineering, model evaluation, and experimentation.
Hands-on experience developing and deploying machine learning solutions in production environments.
Experience working with LLMs, prompt engineering, reasoning and planning frameworks, RAG architectures, vector databases, AI agents, and Generative AI application development.
Experience with distributed computing platforms such as Spark, Databricks, or similar big data technologies.
Familiarity with cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or GCP and associated AI/ML services.
Understanding of MLOps principles, including model deployment, model monitoring, CI/CD, and ML lifecycle management.
Experience working with SQL and large-scale structured and unstructured datasets.
Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving abilities with a passion for solving complex real-world challenges.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.
Strong learning agility, intellectual curiosity, and desire to stay current with advances in AI and machine learning.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience developing fraud detection, risk management, trust & safety, cybersecurity, or financial crime solutions.
Hands-on experience with Hadoop, Spark, Databricks, MLflow, Agentic AI frameworks, reasoning and planning frameworks, LangChain, or similar AI engineering technologies.
Experience building Agentic AI solutions and multi-agent systems.
Exposure to graph learning, anomaly detection, network intelligence, or real-time decisioning systems.
Publications, patents, open-source contributions, Kaggle achievements, or demonstrated research experience in AI/ML.
Corporate Security Responsibility
All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:
Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;
Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;
Report any suspected information security violation or breach, and
Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

jobs.title: IP RTL Senior Design Engineer
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
The Role and Impact:
As an IP Logic Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in developing high-quality intellectual property (IP) for Unified Intel Chassis designs. This position is at the forefront of Intel's innovation, ensuring that our products consistently deliver world-class performance, power efficiency, and reliability. Work closely with architects to define and design complex protocol bridges. Define and implement range-based access control for secured memory and register paths across HBW and LBW. Own privilege qualification and policy propagation across AXI-Lite, APB, IOSF-SB, and HBW request paths. Design and validate parity/ECC generation and checking for request, response, and data channels. Define fault behavior for unauthorized accesses and corrupt transactions, including silent block semantics, RAZWI-style handling, poison propagation, and timeout cleanup. Build or integrate logging, interrupt, and firmware-visible error harvesting flows for local and global RAS handling. Support error injection, diagnostics, and post-silicon debug hooks for both security and reliability validation. Define and implement telemetry capture for fabric load, latency, congestion, error context, and other operational health indicators. Own debug and trace data paths for wrapper-level and fabric-level observability, including data capture, transport, formatting, and handoff to downstream debug infrastructure. Design counters, sticky status, snapshots, and firmware-visible CSRs that make performance and failure analysis practical. Integrate trigger, monitor, and logging hooks needed for bring-up, stress triage, and post-silicon correlation. Work with architecture, validation, firmware, and post-silicon teams to ensure telemetry and debug signals are useful, stable, and diagnosable. Balance observability depth against area, timing, bandwidth, and survivability constraints. Support root-cause analysis of bandwidth loss, latency outliers, protocol stalls, and intermittent field or lab issues using hardware observability features.
Key Responsibilities:
Develop logic designs, register transfer level (RTL) coding, and simulations required for IP blocks, functional units, and subsystems.
Define architecture and microarchitecture features for the IP block being designed.
Apply strategies, tools, and methods to optimize RTL design for power, performance, area, and timing targets.
Strong knowledge of AXI, AXI-Lite, APB, parity/ECC schemes, and transaction error handling.
Experience with secure MMIO, access-control/firewall logic, or privilege-based filtering.
Experience with RAS concepts such as fault containment, poison, interrupt generation, logging, and recovery-oriented design.
Support SoC customers with seamless integration and verification of IP blocks.
Telemetry and debug are both observability functions rather than primary Datapath functions.
Drive compliance with quality assurance standards to enable smooth IP handoff within the SoC development process.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, Computer Engineering, or related field.
A minimum of 8 years of experience in logic design and RTL development.
Proficiency in hardware description languages such as Verilog, System Verilog.
Strong understanding of digital design principles, including timing analysis, power optimization, and area trade-offs.
Experience with industry-standard EDA tools for design and simulation (e.g., Synopsys, Cadence, Mentor Graphics).
Knowledge of IP block integration workflows within SoC designs.
Expertise in RAS/debug/security/telemetry.

Job Details:
Job Description:
Performs physical design implementation of CPU designs from RTL to GDS to create a design database that is ready for manufacturing. Conducts all aspects of the CPU physical design flow including synthesis, place and route, clock tree synthesis, floor planning, static timing analysis, power/clock distribution, reliability, and power and noise analysis. Conducts verification and signoff including formal equivalence verification, static timing analysis, reliability verification, static and dynamic power integrity, layout verification, electrical rule checking, and structural design checking. Analyzes results and makes recommendations to improve current and future CPU microarchitectures closely collaborating with logic, circuit, architecture, and design automation teams. Possesses CPUspecific expertise in various aspects of structural and physical design, including physical clock design, timing closure, coverage analysis, multiple power domain analysis, structured placement, routing, synthesis, and DFT. Works intimately with industry EDA vendors to build and enhance tool capabilities to design a highspeed, lowpower synthesizable CPU. Optimizes CPU design to improve product level parameters such as power, frequency, and area. Participates in the development and improvement of physical design methodologies and flow automation.
Qualifications:
As a CPU Physical Design Engineer, you will play a pivotal role in implementing high-performance, low-power CPU designs from RTL to GDSII. You will focus on detailed processes such as synthesis, placement, routing, timing analysis, and power optimization, enabling designs that meet stringent performance and efficiency targets. Your work will directly influence the success of Intel's next-generation CPUs and their manufacturing readiness, contributing to innovative advancements in computing technology.
You will join a dynamic team dedicated to designing Intel's latest high-performance CPUs using cutting-edge technologies. The Role and Impact
As CPU Circuit Design Lead, you will lead the development of advanced digital circuits for custom blocks such as SRAM, register files, memory compilers, Custom Data path, and caches. You will be instrumental in designing floorplans, optimizing circuits for power, performance, area, timing, and yield goals, and ensuring functionality through rigorous simulation and verification processes. You will also help in build and lead a circuit design team to oversee design creation, testing, and performance analysis, ensuring that projects meet technical specifications and timelines.
Business group
The Silicon and Platform Engineering Group (SPE) is at the core of Intel's innovation, focusing on designing and building cutting-edge silicon and platform technologies that power Intel's products. With a commitment to excellence, the group drives advancements in circuit design, architecture, and performance optimization to enable transformative computing solutions. jobs.title: EDA Tools License Management
jobs.description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
Manages EDA license operations, governance, compliance, and optimization to ensure reliable access to critical design tools across hardware engineering teams. Defines and executes license management processes for major EDA suppliers, including entitlement tracking, usage analysis, cost optimization, audit readiness, and contract compliance. Addresses complex compliance challenges such as reconciling supplier entitlements against actual tool usage, preventing over-deployment or unauthorized access, validating geographic and business-unit usage restrictions, managing license transfers during reorganizations or divestitures, ensuring usage-reporting accuracy, and preparing defensible documentation for supplier audits. Required to migrate the license environment to SLES15, ensuring testing of end users' scripts and automation workflows to improve license visibility, reduce manual effort, and enable data-driven decision-making. Partners with design, contract manager, procurement, finance, legal, IT, and EDA vendors to support tool enablement, license planning, renewal strategy, and business continuity. Builds deep understanding of EDA tool usage, licensing models, supplier agreements, and operational controls to ensure scalable, compliant, and cost-effective license management across technology programs.

• 4-12 years of Experience managing EDA license operations, license servers, vendor daemons, or engineering tool infrastructure.
• Working knowledge of EDA licensing models, entitlement tracking, usage analysis, renewals, and supplier compliance.

We are seeking a skilled and motivated Layout Design Engineering Manager to lead a team of layout engineers in delivering best in class SRAM,RF,ROM,CAM Memory compiler designs across the Intel's bleeding FinFETs,GAA technologies. In this role, you will champion technical execution by overseeing compiler friendly and optimized floorplanning, high-density,performance based placement and routing template, and rigorous physical sign-off processes including DRC, LVS, Yield, DFM, Density, parasitic extraction, Noise Reliability i.e. EM, IR. You will provide technical guidance, set clear goals, and foster cross-functional collaboration with circuit design, Tilers, and foundry teams to meticulously optimize memory area, performance, power, and yield. Beyond daily execution, you will spearhead layout methodology innovations, establish advanced automation flows using SKILL, Python, or Tcl, and cultivate a culture of technical excellence by mentoring senior and staff-level engineers. The role requires a strong vision for leveraging AI and ML technologies (such as reinforcement learning for routing or predictive analytics for DRC debugging) to make execution significantly more efficient, robust, and high-quality.
Business group
The Intel Foundry group plays a pivotal role in enabling innovative semiconductor manufacturing solutions that power Intel's products and those of our partners worldwide. As part of the BA Memories organization, this position supports the development of advanced memory technologies and methodologies, empowering Intel's mission to shape the future of technology and create world-changing advancements.

- Lead and mentor a team of layout design engineers to developed world class memory compiler designs on FinFets/GAA technologies, ensuring alignment with organizational goals and timelines.
- Oversee the design, development, modification, analysis, and verification of memory compiler layout designs.
- Provide technical guidance for analog, digital, memory, and standard cell layout methodologies, compilers, tools, and flows.

- A track record of fostering innovation and driving a culture of excellence.

Senior Design Verification Engineer
About the Role
As a Senior Design Verification Engineer at Analog Devices, you will lead verification planning and execution for next-generation automotive connectivity SoCs based on E2B technology. Working independently with minimal supervision, you will develop advanced verification environments for complex SoCs incorporating embedded microprocessors, communication subsystems, firmware, security functions, and mixed-signal components.
You will collaborate closely with architecture, digital design, analog design, firmware, functional safety, and validation teams to ensure robust verification coverage and high-quality silicon. You will also contribute to verification methodology improvements, mentor junior engineers, and help resolve complex hardware, firmware, and system-level issues.
This career-level position provides the opportunity to contribute to technologies that enable reliable, high-performance communication within modern vehicles.
Key Responsibilities
Verification Strategy: Develop and implement comprehensive verification strategies and test plans for automotive connectivity SoCs and E2B-related functionality.
SoC Verification: Verify complex SoCs containing embedded processors, memories, interconnects, DMA controllers, interrupts, communication interfaces, security features, and mixed-signal subsystems.
UVM Environment Development: Architect, develop, and maintain scalable SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments, including agents, scoreboards, reference models, sequences, assertions, and functional coverage.
Processor and Firmware Verification: Develop firmware-driven verification scenarios for microprocessor-based SoCs, including processor initialization, interrupts, exceptions, memory accesses, peripheral control, and hardware-software interactions.
C DPI Development: Develop and integrate C/SystemVerilog DPI components, software models, and reference models into simulation environments.
E2B Protocol Verification: Verify E2B protocol functionality, including data transfers, control and configuration mechanisms, timing behavior, error handling, diagnostics, and recovery scenarios.
Coverage and Verification Closure: Define and track functional coverage, code coverage, assertion coverage, test status, and verification metrics through sign-off.
Debug and Issue Resolution: Analyze and resolve complex issues across RTL, UVM environments, embedded software, C models, and system-level use cases.
Functional Safety Verification: Support verification of safety mechanisms, fault injection campaigns, requirements traceability, and verification activities associated with ISO 26262-compliant automotive products.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work closely with architecture, design, firmware, functional safety, validation, and applications teams on verification planning, issue resolution, and product readiness.
Post-Silicon Support: Contribute to FPGA prototyping, silicon bring-up, post-silicon validation, and investigation of system or customer issues.
Technical Mentorship: Provide technical guidance to junior verification engineers and contribute to design and verification reviews.
Methodology and Automation: Improve verification productivity through reusable components, automation, regression infrastructure, and verification best practices.
Must-Have Skills
SystemVerilog and UVM: Expert-level knowledge of SystemVerilog and the Universal Verification Methodology, with experience developing reusable verification environments for complex digital designs.
SoC Verification: Strong experience verifying complex SoCs that include embedded microprocessors, memories, buses, peripherals, interrupts, and communication subsystems.
C DPI Development: Hands-on experience developing C/SystemVerilog DPI interfaces and integrating C models or reference models into verification environments.
Verification Planning: Proven ability to convert architecture, design, and product requirements into detailed verification plans, test scenarios, functional coverage, and sign-off criteria.
Coverage-Driven Verification: Strong experience with constrained-random verification, functional coverage, code coverage, and assertion-based verification.
Hardware-Software Integration: Experience developing firmware-driven tests and debugging interactions between embedded software and RTL.
Debugging Expertise: Strong analytical and debugging skills across SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches, RTL, embedded C code, and system-level environments.
Scripting and Automation: Proficiency in Python, TCL, Perl, shell scripting, or similar languages for regression management, result analysis, and workflow automation.
Communication and Collaboration: Ability to work effectively across architecture, design, firmware, functional safety, validation, and applications teams.
Technical Leadership: Ability to independently lead verification activities, conduct technical reviews, mentor less-experienced engineers, and influence verification methodology adoption.
Preferred Skills
Experience verifying SoCs incorporating RISC-V processors. Experience with ARM or other embedded processor architectures is also valuable.
Understanding of processor concepts such as privilege modes, exceptions, interrupts, memory protection, caches, debug infrastructure, and firmware boot sequences.
Experience with automotive communication technologies, in-vehicle networking, or E2B technology.
Experience verifying communication protocols, packet-based interfaces, control channels, diagnostics, and error-recovery mechanisms.
Knowledge of automotive functional safety development and ISO 26262 verification practices.
Experience with fault injection, safety-mechanism verification, requirements traceability, and functional safety evidence generation.
Experience with emulation, FPGA prototyping, virtual platforms, or pre-silicon firmware development.
Knowledge of formal verification, clock-domain crossing, reset-domain crossing, low-power verification, or gate-level simulation.
Experience working with analog behavioral models or mixed-signal verification environments.
Familiarity with automotive cybersecurity concepts and secure communication mechanisms.
Experience with continuous integration, regression automation, and verification dashboards.
Preferred Education and Experience
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
Master’s degree preferred.
4–8 years of relevant digital or mixed-signal IC verification experience.
Experience verifying processor-based SoCs and delivering designs through verification closure.
Experience with automotive semiconductor products or communication SoCs is preferred.
Why You Will Love Working Here
At Analog Devices, you will be part of a collaborative and innovative team developing next-generation automotive connectivity solutions. You will work with experienced architects, designers, firmware developers, functional safety engineers, and validation teams to solve challenging system-level problems and deliver robust semiconductor products.
We offer an environment focused on professional growth, technical innovation, collaboration, and continuous learning. Your work will contribute to technologies that enable reliable, efficient, and high-performance communication inside the vehicles of the future.

Automotive Connectivity SoCs and E2B Technology
About the Role
As a Design Verification Engineer at Analog Devices, you will develop verification environments and execute verification activities for next-generation automotive connectivity SoCs based on E2B technology.
You will work on complex devices incorporating embedded processors, digital communication subsystems, firmware, security functions, and mixed-signal components. Working with moderate supervision, you will collaborate with design, architecture, firmware, functional safety, and validation teams to ensure that designs meet their functional, quality, and reliability requirements before tape-out.
You will contribute to SystemVerilog/UVM testbench development, C DPI integration, coverage analysis, regression execution, and debugging of hardware-software interactions. This position provides an opportunity to develop expertise in automotive SoC verification while contributing to technologies that enable reliable, high-performance in-vehicle connectivity.
Key Responsibilities
Verification Environment Development: Develop and maintain SystemVerilog/UVM verification environments, including agents, sequences, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, assertions, and functional coverage.
SoC Verification: Verify SoC functionality involving embedded processors, memories, interconnects, interrupts, DMA controllers, peripherals, communication interfaces, and mixed-signal subsystems.
Verification Planning: Contribute to verification plans by translating design and product requirements into test scenarios, coverage items, and verification objectives.
Test Development: Develop directed and constrained-random tests for block-level, subsystem-level, and SoC-level verification.
Processor-Based Verification: Develop and execute verification scenarios for microprocessor-based SoCs, including processor initialization, register accesses, interrupts, exceptions, boot sequences, and basic firmware interactions.
C DPI Integration: Develop and maintain C/SystemVerilog DPI interfaces and integrate C-based models or reference functions into simulation environments.
E2B Functionality: Verify E2B communication functionality, including configuration, control, data transfer, timing behavior, error handling, diagnostics, and recovery scenarios.
Coverage and Metrics: Analyze functional, code, and assertion coverage; identify verification gaps; and develop additional tests to support verification closure.
Regression Execution: Execute and monitor verification regressions, analyze failures, classify issues, and communicate results to the project team.
Debugging: Analyze and resolve verification failures across testbenches, RTL, embedded C code, reference models, and system-level scenarios.
Functional Safety Support: Contribute to verification of automotive safety mechanisms, fault injection tests, requirements traceability, and verification evidence for ISO 26262-related activities.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with design, architecture, firmware, functional safety, validation, and applications teams to resolve technical issues and support project milestones.
Documentation: Create and maintain clear documentation covering verification plans, testcases, coverage results, known issues, and verification status.
Automation: Develop scripts to automate regression execution, results analysis, coverage reporting, and other verification workflows.
Technical Reviews: Participate in design, architecture, verification plan, and code reviews, providing verification-focused feedback.
Must-Have Skills
SystemVerilog and UVM: Proficiency in developing and maintaining verification environments using SystemVerilog and the Universal Verification Methodology.
Testbench Development: Experience developing coverage-driven verification components and testcases for complex digital designs.
Digital and SoC Verification: Understanding of digital verification concepts and experience verifying blocks, subsystems, or SoCs containing processors, memories, buses, interrupts, peripherals, or communication interfaces.
C and C DPI: Experience with C programming and familiarity with integrating C models or functions into SystemVerilog environments through DPI.
Verification Techniques: Experience with directed testing, constrained-random verification, functional coverage, code coverage, and assertion-based verification.
Verilog RTL: Strong understanding of RTL design concepts and the ability to read and debug Verilog or SystemVerilog RTL.
Debugging: Ability to analyze and resolve moderately complex verification problems with limited supervision.
Scripting and Automation: Ability to develop scripts using Python, Perl, TCL, shell, or similar languages to improve verification workflows.
EDA Tools: Experience using simulation, waveform-debug, regression, and coverage-analysis tools.
Communication Interfaces: Working knowledge of communication interfaces such as SPI, I2C, or UART and their verification requirements.
Collaboration: Effective communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to collaborate with design, firmware, validation, and other engineering groups.
Preferred Skills
Experience verifying SoCs incorporating RISC-V processors. Experience with ARM or other embedded processor architectures is also valuable.
Familiarity with processor concepts such as privilege modes, exceptions, interrupts, memory protection, debug infrastructure, and firmware boot sequences.
Experience with firmware-driven verification or hardware-software co-verification.
Experience developing C/SystemVerilog DPI components and integrating C-based reference models.
Familiarity with automotive connectivity technologies, in-vehicle networking, or E2B technology.
Experience verifying packet-based communication protocols, control channels, error handling, diagnostics, or recovery mechanisms.
Understanding of automotive functional safety and ISO 26262 development processes.
Familiarity with fault injection, safety-mechanism verification, or requirements traceability.
Experience with emulation, FPGA prototyping, virtual platforms, or pre-silicon firmware development.
Familiarity with mixed-signal verification or analog behavioral models.
Knowledge of formal verification, clock-domain crossing, reset-domain crossing, low-power verification, or gate-level simulation.
Familiarity with continuous integration and automated regression infrastructure.
Preferred Education and Experience
Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics and Communications Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field.
2–4 years of relevant experience in digital design verification.
Experience developing SystemVerilog/UVM testbenches and coverage-driven verification environments.
Experience with processor-based designs, communication SoCs, or automotive semiconductor products is preferred.
Why You’ll Love Working Here
At Analog Devices, you will be part of a collaborative and innovative team developing next-generation automotive connectivity solutions. You will work alongside experienced verification engineers, architects, designers, firmware developers, safety engineers, and validation teams while building expertise in complex SoC and automotive verification.

jobs.title: Soft Skills Trainer – CRT
jobs.description:
Soft Skills Trainer – CRT
Description -
Job Description: Soft Skills Trainer – CRT
Location: Bangalore, India
Level: Intermediate
Function: Training Centre of Excellence (Training COE)
Program: Customer Resolution Training (CRT)
Role Overview
We are seeking a passionate and learner-focused Soft Skills Trainer to support the Customer Resolution Training (CRT) program, with a focus on strengthening customer-facing communication, service excellence, and effective resolution skills among customer support agents.
The ideal candidate will have experience delivering soft skills training in a customer service or contact centre environment and be confident in facilitating interactive learning sessions, conducting role-plays, providing individual coaching, and translating customer experience expectations into observable agent behaviours.
This is a hands-on training role that requires strong facilitation skills, a customer-first mindset, and the ability to collaborate with Training, Quality, and Operations teams to improve agent confidence, communication effectiveness, and customer resolution outcomes.
Key Responsibilities
1. CRT Soft Skills Training & Facilitation
Deliver structured soft skills training interventions aligned with CRT program objectives and customer experience expectations.
Facilitate interactive sessions on:
Customer-centric communication and active listening.
Empathy, rapport building, and acknowledging customer concerns.
Ownership, accountability, and end-to-end resolution.
Probing, questioning, and identifying customer needs.
Managing difficult conversations, objections, and escalations.
De-escalation techniques and emotional intelligence.
Clear explanations, expectation setting, and professional communication.
Positive language, call control, and effective closing.
Use role-plays, case studies, simulations, group activities, and real-world customer scenarios to reinforce learning.
Adapt facilitation methods to suit different learner profiles, experience levels, and capability gaps.
Reinforce the application of soft skills during customer interactions, rather than focusing solely on theoretical concepts.
2. Agent Coaching & Performance Improvement
Conduct individual and group coaching based on call observations, Quality feedback, assessment results, and identified skill gaps.
Review customer interaction examples to identify behavioural opportunities and recommend targeted interventions.
Provide actionable feedback on communication, empathy, listening, ownership, and resolution behaviours.
Conduct mock calls, practice conversations, and behavioural assessments to evaluate agent readiness.
Track coaching actions and conduct follow-up validations to ensure feedback is translated into improved performance.
Support agents who require additional intervention through structured improvement plans and targeted practice.
3. CRT Program Execution
Support the implementation and ongoing delivery of CRT learning interventions across relevant agent groups.
Partner with the CRT program team to understand learning objectives, customer pain points, performance trends, and priority capability gaps.
Prepare session plans, facilitator guides, participant activities, practice scenarios, and assessment materials.
Maintain training attendance, assessment results, coaching records, and program progress reports.
Ensure consistent delivery of approved content and alignment with CRT standards.
Incorporate feedback and emerging customer interaction trends into future training interventions.
4. Quality & Business Collaboration
Partner with Quality and Operations teams to identify recurring communication and customer experience gaps.
Participate in call calibrations and feedback discussions to understand performance expectations and align coaching approaches.
Analyse available quality insights, customer feedback, repeat contacts, and escalation trends to identify relevant learning needs.
Support pre- and post-training assessments to evaluate skill development and learning transfer.
Recommend targeted refreshers or coaching interventions based on observed performance gaps.
Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving customer experience and resolution effectiveness.
5. Learning Effectiveness & Reporting
Measure learning effectiveness through assessments, mock-call evaluations, facilitator observations, and post-training feedback.
Maintain accurate records of training delivery, learner progress, and follow-up coaching.
Prepare regular updates on training completion, learner performance, key behavioural gaps, and improvement opportunities.
Share insights and recommendations with the CRT program, Quality, and Operations stakeholders.
Demonstrate the impact of training through observable improvements in agent communication and customer interaction quality.
Qualifications & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in any discipline; relevant training certifications are an advantage.
Typically 3–6 years of experience in soft skills training, customer service training, communication coaching, or learning and development.
Experience in a customer support, BPO, contact centre, or customer experience environment is preferred.
Demonstrated ability to facilitate soft skills sessions and coach customer-facing employees.
Experience with call listening, mock-call assessments, Quality feedback, or behavioural coaching is desirable.
Strong verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to influence and engage diverse audiences.
Proficiency in PowerPoint, Excel, and standard virtual training tools.
Ability to manage multiple training activities, maintain documentation, and collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
Core Competencies
Facilitation excellence: Creates engaging, interactive, learner-centred sessions.
Customer empathy: Demonstrates a strong understanding of customer emotions, expectations, and service recovery.
Coaching effectiveness: Provides specific, constructive, behaviour-based feedback.
Communication: Communicates with clarity, confidence, and professionalism.
Adaptability: Adjusts delivery based on learner needs and performance gaps.
Analytical thinking: Uses call observations and Quality insights to identify capability needs.
Collaboration: Works effectively with Training, Quality, and Operations teams.
Execution discipline: Manages schedules, records, assessments, and follow-up actions consistently.
Success Measures
Training delivery completion and adherence to the CRT learning plan.
Improvement in soft skills assessment and mock-call scores.
Observable improvement in empathy, active listening, probing, ownership, and expectation setting.
Reduction in recurring behavioural gaps identified through call monitoring, where applicable.
Completion and effectiveness of targeted coaching and refresher interventions.
Positive stakeholder feedback and demonstrated application of learning on the job.
What We Are Looking For
We are looking for a practical, energetic, and learner-focused trainer who can connect with frontline agents, simplify behavioural concepts, and translate them into effective customer conversations.
The right candidate will combine strong facilitation and coaching skills with an understanding of contact centre realities. They should be comfortable working closely with Quality and Operations, using real customer scenarios to address capability gaps, and contributing to measurable improvements in the CRT program.
This is an intermediate-level opportunity for a trainer who is ready to take ownership of soft skills learning delivery and grow their impact through structured coaching, stakeholder collaboration, and continuous improvement.

jobs.title: Workplace Experience & Real Estate Portfolio Lead
jobs.description:
Workplace Experience & Real Estate Portfolio Lead
Description -
Workplace Experience & Real Estate Portfolio Lead
Bengaluru, India
About the Role
India is one of HP Inc.’s strategically important and operationally complex markets. The CREWS India is the accountable workplace experience and real estate leader for India, shaping environments that enable business performance, strengthen employee engagement, and help teams, peers, and partners thrive across multiple sites.
Based in Bengaluru and reporting to the Director, CREWS — APJ, CREWS India will serve as a trusted country leader and partner to India business and site leaders, Finance, HR, Legal, Procurement, Security, EHS, and global CREWS stakeholders. The role requires executive presence, sound judgment, and the ability to align diverse stakeholders, lead enterprise-scale change, and translate business, workforce, and employee needs into an integrated India workplace strategy.
The successful candidate will lead through others, influence without authority, and connect workplace decisions to HP’s business priorities. Success will be measured through business continuity, productivity and collaboration, employee experience, cost and capital discipline, risk and compliance, partner performance, and delivery of complex transformation priorities.
Key Responsibilities
Own workplace experience, facilities, and site services across India, creating safe, compliant, reliable environments that enable employees and teams to perform at their best.
Bring a hospitality-led mindset to workplace delivery, creating responsive, thoughtful, high-quality experiences for employees, leaders, visitors, and partners.
Set India’s real estate and workplace strategy, translating business and workforce priorities into portfolio plans, space optimization, investment choices, and executive-ready recommendations.
Partner with senior business and site leaders to anticipate growth, workforce, cultural, operational, and regulatory needs and convert them into workplace solutions that improve productivity, collaboration, talent experience, and resilience.
Establish strong governance through clear KPIs, SLAs, reporting rhythms, accountability, and recovery plans for service providers and internal delivery teams.
Create operating and capital budgets, optimize total workplace cost, and build compelling business cases that balance financial return, employee experience, risk, and long-term value.
Provide strategic oversight of construction, fit-out, renovation, consolidation, expansion and facilities related issues
Build, coach, and develop India CREWS team and partner ecosystem, fostering an inclusive, positive environment where people take ownership, collaborate, and thrive.
Represent HP Inc. with landlords, developers, service partners, consultants, and senior governmental or regulatory representatives where required.
Drive EHS, security, procurement, financial, sustainability, and statutory compliance across the India portfolio.
Ensure disciplined follow-through on issues, escalations, and service gaps, with clear ownership, urgency, transparency, and closure.
Foster collaboration, ownership, continuous improvement, and One HP problem-solving across regional, global, and local teams.
Lead India’s employee transportation program, ensuring compliance, service reliability, and adoption of innovative, industry-standard technologies.
Education & Experience
Bachelor’s degree required in Business Administration, Engineering, Architecture, Real Estate, Facilities Management, or a related discipline; equivalent demonstrated experience will be considered.
Graduate degree, MBA, or postgraduate qualification preferred.
Typically 12+ years of progressive experience in facilities services, corporate real estate, workplace operations, portfolio management, or related fields.
Experience leading large, complex, multi-site operations in India, preferably within a multinational, technology, engineering, R&D, or shared-services environment.
Demonstrated track record of influencing senior executives, leading enterprise-scale change, and delivering measurable outcomes across workplace experience, cost, risk, and business performance.
Preferred certifications include Certified Facility Manager, PMP, RICS, MCR/CORENET, LEED, GRIHA, or equivalent credentials.
Required Knowledge & Skills
Facilities management, workplace services, preventive maintenance, EHS, sustainability, security coordination, and business continuity.
Construction, fit-out, renovation, HVAC, plumbing, property management, supplier management, and project governance.
Finance, procurement, financial analysis, budget ownership, forecasting, invoicing, and executive reporting.
KPIs, service provider governance, root-cause analysis, continuous improvement, and recovery planning.
Ability to navigate statutory requirements, government interfaces, landlord/developer relationships, and India market dynamics.
Leadership Competencies
Strategic thinking, results orientation, and the ability to convert ambiguity into clear priorities, decisions, and execution plans.
Executive presence and effective communication with senior leaders, employee councils, government representatives, landlords, developers, vendors, and internal teams.
Customer centricity, digital fluency, learning agility, and data-driven decision-making, with the ability to translate business, workforce, and employee needs into strategies that improve productivity, collaboration, engagement, and organizational performance.
Collaborative leadership across matrixed global, regional, and local teams, creating trust, shared accountability, and a positive environment where colleagues and partners can thrive.
Ability to influence outcomes without direct authority by building trust, aligning stakeholders, creating shared ownership, and following through on commitments.
Constructive, resilient leadership under pressure, maintaining clarity, inclusion, accountability, and momentum through ambiguity and escalation.
People leadership capability, including coaching, performance management, talent development, team building, and succession readiness.
Enterprise leadership potential to lead large cross-functional programs, influence long-term direction, and represent the function at senior forums.
Impact, Scope & Complexity
Shapes outcomes for large functions and leads complex, cross-division initiatives across India, with visibility and influence at country, regional, and global leadership levels.
Delivers innovative, practical solutions to complex real estate and workplace challenges, using data and stakeholder insight to improve employee experience, productivity, resilience, cost, and risk outcomes.
Balances day-to-day service reliability with long-term transformation, portfolio optimization, sustainability goals, and workforce experience outcomes.
Requires sound judgment, resilience, collaboration, and the ability to make trade-offs across cost, risk, service quality, compliance, employee experience, and business growth.
Preferred Leadership Differentiators
Experience with smart building technologies, workplace analytics, and sustainability frameworks such as LEED, GRIHA, or equivalent.
Track record leading workplace transformations or portfolio expansions in complex, high-growth organizations.
Natural ability to influence, align, and collaborate across global, regional, and local teams without relying on formal authority.
Passion for operational excellence and belief that the workplace can drive culture, performance, collaboration, and talent experience.
Travel
Travel within India and occasional regional travel may be required based on business, site, project, and stakeholder needs.
Why HP Inc. India
At HP Inc., CREWS creates workplace experiences that enable business outcomes, support our people, and advance the well-being of our communities and planet. This role offers the opportunity to shape one of HP’s most important country portfolios, lead through meaningful complexity, and strengthen India CREWS capability. The right candidate will help make HP’s workplace a competitive advantage while developing the breadth, judgment, and enterprise leadership capability to take on expanded scope as opportunities arise.
HP Inc. is an equal opportunity employer committed to building a diverse, inclusive, and equitable workplace.

Communications & People Engagement Lead
Description -
The Communications & People Engagement Lead is a strategic partner responsible for shaping organizational culture, driving employee engagement, strengthening leadership communications, and enabling successful change adoption across the Global Customer Care Centers (CCC) organization.
This role serves as the connective tissue between leadership, employees, and business priorities assuring that communication is not merely informational, but transformational. The individual will design and execute integrated communication, engagement, culture, recognition, and change management strategies that foster connection, transparency, inclusion, and organizational effectiveness across a globally distributed workforce.
The role requires a highly creative, customer-centric, and influential communications professional capable of translating business priorities into meaningful employee experiences that build trust, drive alignment, accelerate adoption of change, and strengthen employee commitment to organizational goals.
Working closely with Customer Care Center leadership, Operations, Quality, Training, HR, Communications, and other business stakeholders, the Communications & People Engagement Lead will help build a connected, resilient, engaged, and future-ready workforce while elevating employee experience across all care center locations.
Key Responsibilities
1. Strategic Communications
Organizational Communications Strategy
Develop and execute integrated communications strategies aligned to CCC business priorities, transformation initiatives, and organizational objectives.
Serve as the primary communications advisor to CCC leadership, shaping messaging that drives clarity, engagement, and alignment.
Build annual communication roadmaps and engagement calendars supporting strategic priorities.
Ensure consistent, timely, and effective communication across global teams, sites, and functions.
Establish communication standards, governance, and best practices across the organization.
Executive & Leadership Communications
Develop executive-level messaging, presentations, speeches, town halls, leadership updates, and employee communications.
Support leadership engagement sessions, all-employee meetings, fireside chats, podcasts, and interactive forums.
Partner with leaders to strengthen visibility, accessibility, and connection with employees.
Coach leaders on communication effectiveness, storytelling, and employee engagement approaches.
Communication Content Management
Own and manage end-to-end communication channels and content strategies.
Create and distribute:
Newsletters
Leadership updates
Internal campaigns
Employee stories
Organizational announcements
Transformation communications
Recognition communications
Ensuring content reflects organizational values, culture, and customer-focused priorities.
2. Storytelling, Branding & Employee Advocacy
Strategic Storytelling
Develop compelling narratives that connect employees to purpose, customers, business outcomes, and organizational strategy.
Translate complex business concepts into engaging, relatable, and actionable content.
Create storytelling frameworks that highlight innovation, customer impact, quality, transformation, and employee success.
Employee & Customer Impact Stories

Creative Content Development
Lead innovative communication approaches leveraging:
Visual storytelling
Infographics

Digital campaigns
Podcasts
Interactive experiences
Executive narratives

Social and collaboration platforms
3. Employee Engagement & Culture
Employee Experience Strategy
Design and implement programs that strengthen employee engagement, belonging, motivation, and connection.
Partner with HR and leadership teams to improve employee experience across the employee lifecycle.
Develop initiatives that align employee sentiment with organizational goals and values.
Recognition & Appreciation Programs
Lead enterprise recognition strategies that celebrate performance, innovation, customer obsession, teamwork, and cultural excellence.
Establish scalable global recognition programs and engagement events.
Drive employee appreciation initiatives that reinforce desired organizational behaviors.
Inclusion, Belonging & Community
Champion an inclusive culture where all employees feel valued, respected, and empowered.
Build engagement initiatives that foster collaboration across countries, cultures, functions, and teams.
Partner with employee resource groups and community networks to create meaningful employee experiences.
Employee Listening Programs
Design and manage employee listening strategies including:
Pulse surveys
Focus groups
Listening sessions
Engagement assessments
Sentiment analysis
Translate employee feedback into actionable recommendations.
Ensure leadership accountability through continuous feedback loops and action planning.
4. Change Management & Organizational Adoption
Management of Change (MoC)
Lead communication and engagement workstreams supporting organizational transformation programs.
Develop comprehensive change communication strategies and adoption plans.
Ensure employees understand the rationale, benefits, risks, and impacts of transformation initiatives.
Change Communications
Create and implement communication plans covering:
Business rationale for change
Strategic objectives
Employee impacts
New ways of working
Adoption expectations
Success outcomes
Ongoing progress updates
Change Champion Network
Build and manage global networks of change champions.
Enable champions with training, messaging, communication assets, and engagement tools.
Drive local advocacy and adoption across regions and teams.
Adoption & Readiness Management
Measure awareness, readiness, engagement, and adoption of key initiatives.
Identify resistance points and engagement risks.
Develop mitigation strategies and targeted interventions.
Track organizational readiness and communication effectiveness.
5. Leadership Engagement & Organizational Effectiveness
Leadership Partnership
Act as a trusted advisor to senior leaders on employee engagement, communications, culture, and change initiatives.
Provide insights and recommendations that improve organizational effectiveness and employee connection.
Employee Engagement Events
Lead planning and execution of:
Global All Employee Meetings
Leadership forums
Town halls
Engagement weeks
Recognition ceremonies
Cultural celebrations
Volunteer and community activities
Learning and development events
Global Collaboration
Foster collaboration across sites, partners, suppliers, and functional organizations.
Encourage sharing of best practices, knowledge, and organizational success stories.

Employee Advocacy
Champion employee concerns, perspectives, and ideas.
Promote transparent communication and trust across the organization.
Active Listening & Empathy
Create environments where employees feel heard, respected, and supported.
Strengthen leadership understanding of employee needs and experiences.

Enhanced employee experience outcomes.

Description -
Job Summary
• This role is responsible for managing a diverse team supporting large and complex business units for internal and external audits, including Human Rights and Reasonable Business Alliance. The role shapes labor relations policy, negotiates, and advises on disciplinary matters. The role collaborates with HR in grievance investigations, serving as spokesperson and providing insights.
Responsibilities
• Manages a small team of HR compliance managers in the delivery of internal and external audit activity on behalf of the human resource function, including human rights and reasonable business alliance.
• Assists in the formulation of labor relations policy and represents the business in labor relations, including negotiations, interpretation, and administration of the collective bargaining agreements.

jobs.title: Senior Data Scientist– Pricing
jobs.description:
Senior Data Scientist– Pricing
Description -
About the role
HP's B2B Pricing Data Science team builds the analytics and ML systems that set and negotiate prices for commercial PC and Print products, sold both through channel partners and directly to business customers worldwide. Our pricing engine combines machine learning price and win-rate models, causal price elasticity estimation, and constrained optimization, and is deployed in live A/B pilots across multiple markets. We are expanding the team's global footprint to better support a global product.
You will work at the intersection of econometrics and production data science: improving the causal inference core of our pricing algorithm, designing experiments to measure the impact of pricing and process interventions, and shipping your work as production-quality Python code. You will report directly to the team's manager, partner closely with our senior applied data scientist on methodology, and operate with a high degree of autonomy.
What you will do
Advance the causal inference components of our pricing system: price elasticity estimation (double/debiased ML, heterogeneous treatment effects), uncertainty quantification, and optimization logic.
Design, run, and analyze experiments and quasi-experiments (A/B tests, diff-in-diff, synthetic control) to measure the impact of pricing and process interventions, including where clean randomization isn't possible.
Translate methodological improvements into production-ready Python code, with tests, documentation, and adherence to team engineering standards.
Contribute to the operational health of our production systems: incident support, model monitoring, and periodic retraining and validation cycles.
Communicate findings and recommendations to technical and business stakeholders across time zones.
What you bring
4–5+ years of professional experience in data science, econometrics, or quantitative research, ideally with exposure to pricing, revenue management, or marketplaces.
Strong grounding in causal inference and experimental design: potential outcomes framework, DML/orthogonalization, CATE estimation, instrumental variables, panel methods.
Solid applied ML skills (gradient boosting, regularized regression) and the statistical judgment to know when a predictive model answers a causal question — and when it doesn't.
Proficient Python for production: clean, testable, maintainable code; comfortable with the scikit-learn ecosystem, Git-based workflows, and code review.
Hands-on experience with Databricks (or comparable cloud data platforms) for development and deployment.
Proactive, self-directed working style: you reach out early when blocked, over-communicate in a distributed team, and don't wait for co-location to collaborate.
Fluent English; comfortable working with predominantly CET-based colleagues.
Nice to have
Experience with EconML, DoWhy, or similar causal ML libraries; conformal prediction.
Effective use of GenAI tools for coding and research — our team works extensively with AI coding assistants (e.g., Codex, GitHub Copilot) as part of daily development.
B2B pricing domain knowledge (quotes, deal negotiation, discounting, channel dynamics).
Advanced degree (MSc/PhD) in economics, statistics, or a quantitative field.
Education
Full time Master's degree, PhD/Doctorate will be added advantage (not mandatory)

Work directly with FreeWheel and external vendors on technical investigations, product capabilities, new integrations, and resolution of complex issues.

Ad Tech Integration & Connectivity

Stay current with developments in programmatic advertising, ad-server capabilities, oRTB standards, and emerging ad-tech solutions.

Monitor the health and performance of integrations and identify trends, recurring issues, and potential risks.
Use data and technical analysis to identify opportunities for improving ad delivery, integration performance, and operational processes.
Support the rollout of new markets, partners, products, and monetization capabilities from a technical integration perspective.

Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Advertising, or a related field.
Relevant certifications in ad tech or programmatic operations are a plus.
Experience
5+ years of experience in programmatic advertising, ad-tech integrations, ad operations, or a related technical role, with significant hands-on experience with FreeWheel Ad Server and FreeWheel Marketplace.
Strong hands-on experience working across FreeWheel Ad Server, FreeWheel Marketplace, SSPs, DSPs, exchanges, and other programmatic platforms.
Experience owning or supporting end-to-end integrations and troubleshooting complex ad-serving and programmatic issues.
Strong understanding of oRTB, VAST/VPAID, APIs, XML, ad-request/response flows, and programmatic data flows.
Hands-on experience with debugging tools such as Charles Proxy, Wireshark, browser developer tools, logs, or similar tools.
Experience working directly with technology vendors and external programmatic partners on technical integrations and issue resolution.

Strong ownership mindset with a focus on continuous improvement, scalability, and operational excellence.
Preferred Qualifications

Advanced FreeWheel expertise, including FreeWheel Marketplace; experience with other major ad-server platforms such as Google Ad Manager or Xandr is a plus.
Experience working with CTV/OTT programmatic advertising and video ad delivery.
Understanding of privacy frameworks and their impact on programmatic advertising and ad-tech integrations.

Drive medium-sized software releases from initial development through production release and beyond. You will lead cross-functional release core teams across Product Management, Engineering (Development, Test), Marketing, Operations, and Global Services; set your own priorities; recommend release tradeoffs; and influence stakeholders up to the Senior Director level. Technical competency ranging from moderate to subject matter expert
