Advanced Path Planning & OLP: Execute complex path planning and Offline Programming (OLP) to ensure collision-free and efficient robotic motion. Perception & AI: Implement computer vision algorithms and sensor fusion (LiDAR, 3D cameras) to enable real-time object recognition, part localization, and obstacle avoidance. Virtual Commissioning: Lead the virtual commissioning of robotic systems to validate PLC logic and HMI interfaces before physical deployment, reducing lead times and risks. Robotic Control & Systems Engineering: Programming & Logic: Demonstrate competency in programming languages (C++, Python) to develop custom robotic applications and troubleshoot complex system behaviours. Modelling & Simulation: Use specialized software (Matlab-Simulink, Open Modelica, Control Build) to model electro-mechanical devices and simulate dynamic system responses. Industrial Communication: Implement PLC and HMI solutions, establishing robust communication protocols (TIA Portal, Simatic Manager) between robotic controllers and factory systems. Hardware-in-the-Loop: Integrate real-time simulation with physical control hardware to ensure seamless vertical integration of the robotic stack. Industrial Architecture & Project Leadership: Technical Deliverables: Take ownership of work packages and lead technical reviews, ensuring robotic solutions meet the highest industrial standards. Stakeholder Management: Coordinate the exchange of technical data between internal and global stakeholders to drive architecture projects toward best performance. Documentation & Best Practices: Maintain rigorous documentation of robotic application developments, version controls, and changes to ensure traceability and scalability. Strategic Alignment: Align the robotics roadmap with the organization’s long-term business goals, capturing stakeholder needs to define architectural solutions that exceed expectations. TOOL SKILLS: DELMIA / 3DX (3DEXPERIENCE), MATLAB / Simulink, TIA Portal, Simatic Manager, OpenModelica, ControlBuild, C++, Python, iDMU (Industrial Digital Mockup), ROS / ROS2, OpenCV While the above mentioned represents our current technical stack, we prioritize a growth mindset and a curious mind over mastery of any single tool. jobs.description: Job Description: Description of the job Airbus India is looking for a senior Full-Stack Developer to join our team in Bengaluru. You will join the Airline Sciences team within the Digital department. Join our Product team that will design and build specialized products, utilizing the core capabilities of our simulation/data models. This role is like that of a Solutions Engineer to solve real-world aerospace challenges through rapid digital innovation. Acting as the Product Manager’s technical co-pilot, you will be involved in scoping business needs, build interactive prototypes, and deliver scalable web solutions integrated with the core simulation models and data pipelines. This role offers end to end development accountability, combining airline operations problem-solving with hands-on full-stack development. Also, there may be a need to create an application prototype using Python, as part of a Proof-Of-concept. You will also be responsible for the database, AWS Cloud and DevOps tasks specific to the product delivery aligned to you. It is not an embedded systems, avionics firmware, or DO-178C certification position. Collaborates with other developers and provides significant contributions to develop specifications, to resolve business client questions, problems solving, bug fixing, testing, and investigating platform issues. Ensure all bespoke solutions comply with global cloud architecture, cyber security, and data governance standards. Potential partnership with the Product Manager/Lead during client discovery workshops to assess business needs Evaluate customer IT ecosystems, data feeds, and API capabilities to define technical feasibility and architecture blueprints Rapidly build interactive prototypes, data flows, and build APIs to demonstrate feasibility and secure stakeholder buy-in This role may involve some travel for business in Europe and as such you must be able to travel accordingly. Required skills We are looking for candidates with the following skills and experience: The skills you bring Bachelor or Master degree in Aeronautical Engineering, Computer Science, Software Engineering or other related discipline preferred 5-7 years of experience in Software Development and especially working hands-on in a fast-paced discovery to design to prototype and industrialize specialized applications, predominantly in the Aerospace/Airline Operations scope Knowledge / hands-on experience in handling aviation data and digital application needs (real-life aviation/airline operations products, possibly simulation platforms) is mandatory Hands-on experience with frontend development of UI components for ADT applications using ReactJS / Redux technologies Experience in Python coding Java development (including experience with JDK 8+ preferred) and a strong experience using Spring Framework Experience developing multithreaded application in Java to build high performing applications Expertize in memory management while doing application design and development and experience of building scalable applications Experience in following an agile methodology (SCRUM, KABAN) Knowledge of all phases of software development including design, coding, testing, debugging, implementation, and support Knowledge and strong experience with GIT Ability to thoroughly understand the business issues surrounding each project Knowledge and experience in at least one of the following technologies: MySQL, Maven, Spring Framework, Jenkins, JIRA Direct interaction with business teams for requirement analysis, issue troubleshooting and resolution, first line support to the users for their business needs. Familiarity with version control systems and CI/CD pipelines. Good knowledge on designing and implementing APIs, RESTful web-services and SOAP-based Web-services Knowledge of AWS Cloud and Microservices architecture English: advanced level both verbal and written Along with the above mandatory skillsets, highly preferable candidates will showcase: Experience with client discovery workshops to understand airline operational bottlenecks and solution scoping AND/OR Experience with digital product development within the aerospace / aviation domain AND/OR Hands-on experience with aerospace/aviation data and its usage AND Demonstrated experience integrating AI coding assistants and modern productivity tools into the end-to-end software development lifecycle (ideation, development, automated test generation, and code review). We're seeking an innovative AI Agent Designer to join our high-impact Methods and Tools team. You'll be the crucial link, translating intricate business logic and engineering workflows into autonomous, high-performing AI agents and multi-agent systems on our cutting-edge, Engineering Knowledge Framework [EKF] AI platform. This isn't just about prompt engineering; it's about shaping the future of digital continuity and AI augmented Aircraft Engineering across Airbus. You'll dive deep into dynamic data integration, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and agentic workflows—turning complex engineering requirements into seamless, secure, and compliant AI solutions. If you're a proactive leader, eager to drive AI innovation from concept to deployment in a large, complex engineering ecosystem, this is your opportunity to shine! Key Responsibilities: Agent Architecture & Analysis: Understand complex business and engineering workflows, identify augmentation opportunities, and document detailed functional requirements for AI agent personas, tools, and guardrails. Feasibility & Risk Assessment: Proactively evaluate AI automation suitability for use cases. Analyze engineering requirements to determine appropriateness, identifying potential failure modes, data gaps, or regulatory risks before development. Hands-on Agent Configuration: Directly design, configure, and fine-tune AI agents, prompting strategies, agent body of knowledge (databases and graphs) within our internal EKF platform. Stakeholder Engagement: Act as the primary liaison between engineering business teams and core EKF development teams, managing expectations and ensuring alignment on agent capabilities and limitations. Agile Execution: Collaborate closely with EKF development teams to refine, clarify, and prioritize user stories for EKF capabilities, agent tools, APIs, and data pipelines. Testing & Evaluation: Develop test plans specifically for AI behavior (including accuracy, hallucination mitigation, and regression testing), lead User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and ensure agents meet rigorous quality and safety standards. Documentation & Governance: Create comprehensive documentation (agent specifications, prompt catalogs, configuration guides) and train end-users on interacting with and auditing AI agents. Continuous Optimization: Monitor agent performance in production, analyze user feedback loops, and iteratively improve agent reasoning, context retrieval, and efficiency. Experience: 5+ years of progressive experience as a Business Analyst, Systems Designer, or Solution Architect, with a minimum of 2 years explicitly focused on designing decision support systems, AI agents, or advanced LLM implementations. Experience in the aerospace engineering field would be a plus. Required Skills Proprietary Tool Mastery: The ability to quickly learn and master internal, proprietary agent-building platforms and orchestration frameworks with provided training. AI & Data Literacy: Strong understanding of LLM capabilities, agentic design patterns (e.g., reflection, planning, tool-use), RAG patterns, semantic data handling and LLM as judge. jobs.title: Lead ML Engineer
jobs.description: Responsibilities: Build, validate, and ship applied ML models that require real ML judgment, including channel rankers using learning-to-rank and gradient-boosted approaches, peer-network embeddings and similarity, statistical normalization of noisy LLM outputs, and confidence calibration; deploy them into production behind clean, maintainable contracts Integrate ML models and LLM-based components into decoupled, asynchronous pipelines and multi-agent graphs, ensuring they are reliable, observable, and safe under real concurrent production load Stand up evaluation, monitoring, and data-quality discipline that confirms whether a model is actually working in production, including offline metrics that predict online behavior, drift detection, and reconciliation of projected vs. real impact Build fast, reproducible data pipelines in the cloud by reflex, reaching for managed cloud services over one-off scripts, automating data movement, cleaning, and preparation so that the data layer never becomes the bottleneck to ML delivery velocity Decide when not to use ML and defend the simpler answer; jobs.title: LLM & Agentic AI Performance Engineer
jobs.description: Job Details: Job Description: The Role and Impact: Join Intel's Data Center AI organization and help shape how LLM and Agentic AI workloads perform on Intel platforms. Our team operates at a unique intersection of core performance optimization, AI frameworks, and customer-facing AI solutions. We bridge the gap between teams that deeply understand silicon and benchmarking and teams building real-world AI solutions, turning performance insights into software optimizations that developers and customers can use. In this role, you will own end-to-end performance characterization and optimization of LLM and Agentic AI workloads, from Python-level frameworks and inference runtimes down to Linux, system architecture, and hardware performance counters. This is not simply a benchmarking role. Benchmarking tells us what the number is. Your job is to understand why the number is what it is, identify the hardware or software bottleneck, and determine what needs to change to remove it. Your work will translate into code contributions, framework optimizations, best-known configurations (BKCs), customer-ready solutions, and insights that help influence future Intel hardware and software. If you enjoy working across the complete AI stack, from agent frameworks and LLM serving engines to NUMA, memory bandwidth, cache behavior, and silicon counters, this role provides an opportunity to work at that intersection. About the Team: The AI Solutions and Toolkit Engineering team is part of Intel's Data Center organization, focused on enabling modern AI workloads and solutions on Intel platforms. We work across the AI ecosystem, collaborating with AI framework and runtime developers, performance and optimization teams, hardware architects, open-source communities, and solution engineering teams. Our goal is to take deep platform capabilities and performance insights and translate them into practical, optimized AI solutions that developers and customers can deploy. The team works across areas including LLM inference, Agentic AI, AI frameworks and runtimes, workload optimization, open-source software, and datacenter AI systems. Key Responsibilities: · Characterize and optimize LLM and Agentic AI workloads across the complete software and hardware stack. · Identify performance bottlenecks across AI frameworks, inference runtimes, operating systems, memory, compute, and platform architecture. · Design and develop hardware-aware and hardware-agnostic optimizations for AI frameworks and runtimes. · Optimize LLM inference techniques including KV-cache management, attention, continuous batching, and quantization. · Work hands-on with serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, or equivalent technologies. · Analyze host and accelerator performance using tools such as VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, and roofline modeling. · Debug complex performance issues spanning Python frameworks, native code, Linux, runtime libraries, and hardware. · Convert performance findings into software changes, upstream contributions, BKCs, and reusable optimization guidance. · Collaborate with open-source communities to upstream and integrate performance improvements. Translate silicon-level findings into actionable recommendations for framework developers, while bringing application and framework insights back to Intel platform and silicon teams. Qualifications: Minimum Qualifications: · BE +10 years / M.Tech +8 years in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related discipline. · Significant hands-on experience in performance engineering, systems optimization, or workload characterization on server-class platforms. · Demonstrated ability to identify complex performance bottlenecks and deliver measurable performance improvements. · Strong programming skills in Python and C++, or equivalent systems programming experience in C/Rust. · Strong understanding of server architecture including cache hierarchy, memory bandwidth, NUMA, interconnects, and system-level performance behavior. · Hands-on experience with Linux performance and system technologies such as affinity, huge pages, cgroups, eBPF, ftrace, perf, or equivalent tools. Preferred Qualifications: · Deep understanding of LLM inference, including KV-cache, paged attention, continuous batching and quantization such as INT8, INT4, or FP8. · Hands-on experience modifying or optimizing AI serving stacks such as vLLM, SGLang, TGI, OpenVINO, or equivalent. · Experience building, profiling, or optimizing Agentic AI systems using technologies such as LangGraph, CrewAI, AutoGen, MCP-based frameworks, or similar platforms. · Experience with hardware counter-level performance analysis using VTune, EMON/PMU, perf, top-down analysis, or roofline modeling. · Contributions to significant open-source projects, including upstream code contributions. · Ability to communicate across abstraction layers, translating silicon-level findings for software developers and application-level requirements for hardware architects. Why Join This Team? This role gives you the opportunity to work across boundaries that few engineering positions span: Agentic AI & LLMs → AI frameworks → inference runtimes Linux → server architecture → silicon You won't be limited to measuring performance or optimizing an isolated component. You'll help connect the entire stack, identify where the real bottlenecks are, implement improvements, and make those optimizations available to developers and customers. The result is tangible: better AI performance today, stronger software solutions for customers, and insights that can influence tomorrow's Intel platforms. jobs.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer
jobs.description: Senior Machine Learning Engineer Description - We are looking for a Senior MLOps Engineer to design, build, and operate the infrastructure that enables machine learning models and large language models to be deployed safely, reliably, and at scale. In this role, you will create the end-to-end capabilities required to move models from experimentation into production, expose them through secure and highly available endpoints, and enable users and applications to interact with AI-powered services. You will work across AWS and Databricks to establish robust CI/CD pipelines, model-serving infrastructure, observability, governance, rollback mechanisms, and operational standards. You will partner closely with data scientists, machine learning engineers, software engineers, security teams, and platform engineers. The ideal candidate combines strong cloud and DevOps engineering skills with a practical understanding of machine learning systems, LLM deployment patterns, and production reliability. Key Responsibilities MLOps Platform and Architecture Design and implement a scalable MLOps platform using AWS and Databricks. Define reference architectures and reusable deployment patterns for traditional machine learning models, deep learning models, and large language models. Build standardized workflows that move models from development and validation into staging and production. Develop self-service capabilities that allow data scientists and ML engineers to deploy models without manually managing infrastructure. Establish clear separation between development, testing, staging, and production environments. Design multi-region or multi-availability-zone architectures where required by business continuity and availability objectives. CI/CD and Model Deployment Build automated CI/CD pipelines for model code, inference services, infrastructure, configuration, and model artifacts. Implement automated testing across the deployment lifecycle, including: Unit testing Integration testing Model validation Data contract validation API and endpoint testing Security testing Performance and load testing Regression testing Automate model packaging, containerization, versioning, approval, promotion, and deployment. Support deployment strategies such as blue-green deployments, canary releases, shadow deployments, and controlled traffic shifting. Implement reliable rollback and roll-forward mechanisms for application code, infrastructure, model versions, prompts, and configuration. Ensure deployments are reproducible, auditable, and recoverable. Model and LLM Serving Design and operate secure, scalable, low-latency inference endpoints. Deploy models using appropriate services and patterns across AWS and Databricks, such as: Databricks Model Serving MLflow Model Registry Amazon SageMaker Amazon ECS or EKS AWS Lambda, where appropriate API Gateway Application Load Balancers Build synchronous, asynchronous, batch, and streaming inference capabilities. Design serving architectures for LLM-powered applications, including: Hosted foundation models Open-source models Fine-tuned models Retrieval-augmented generation Embedding services Vector search Prompt and response orchestration Tool-calling and agentic workflows Optimize inference performance, scalability, GPU utilization, concurrency, throughput, latency, and cost. Implement autoscaling, request throttling, queuing, caching, timeout handling, and graceful degradation. Reliability, Recovery, and Business Continuity Build recoverable model-serving endpoints with clearly defined recovery time and recovery point objectives. Implement automated health checks, failover mechanisms, retry policies, circuit breakers, and service recovery procedures. Design backup and recovery processes for: Model artifacts Model registry metadata Feature definitions Deployment configurations Infrastructure state Prompts and application configuration Vector indexes and knowledge-base assets Create disaster recovery procedures and regularly test restoration and failover capabilities. Ensure production services can recover from failed deployments, infrastructure outages, model errors, and upstream dependency failures. Develop operational runbooks and incident response procedures. Monitoring and Observability Implement end-to-end observability for infrastructure, applications, models, data, and user interactions. Monitor: Availability Request volume Latency Error rates Resource utilization Model performance Data quality Data drift Concept drift Prediction distributions LLM response quality Hallucination and safety indicators Token consumption Cost per request Establish dashboards, alerts, service-level indicators, and service-level objectives. Integrate monitoring with incident management and on-call processes. Enable traceability from user requests through model inference, retrieval, orchestration, and downstream services. Support root-cause analysis by maintaining structured logs, metrics, traces, model lineage, and deployment history. Security and Governance Implement security controls for model-serving environments, APIs, data access, and deployment pipelines. Apply least-privilege access using AWS IAM, Databricks permissions, service principals, and role-based access control. Secure secrets, credentials, API keys, certificates, and tokens using approved secrets-management solutions. Implement encryption in transit and at rest. Design private networking, endpoint controls, firewall rules, and secure connectivity patterns. Support authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and tenant isolation for AI services. Ensure models and LLM applications comply with organizational requirements for privacy, security, auditability, and responsible AI. Maintain model lineage, approval records, version history, and deployment audit trails. Implement controls for sensitive data, personally identifiable information, prompt injection, unsafe outputs, and unauthorized model access. Infrastructure as Code and Automation Build and maintain cloud infrastructure using Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform or AWS CloudFormation. Automate environment provisioning, policy enforcement, deployment configuration, and platform upgrades. Create reusable modules, templates, libraries, and deployment frameworks. Implement configuration management and environment-specific parameterization. Ensure infrastructure changes are peer-reviewed, tested, version-controlled, and traceable. Collaboration and Engineering Standards Partner with data scientists and ML engineers to productionize models and define deployment requirements. Work with software engineering teams to integrate model endpoints into user-facing products and internal applications. Collaborate with cybersecurity, architecture, legal, privacy, and governance teams. Define MLOps engineering standards, design principles, coding practices, and operational requirements. Conduct architecture reviews, code reviews, and production-readiness assessments. Machine Learning Experience : Significant experience in MLOps, platform engineering, DevOps, site reliability engineering, cloud engineering, or production machine learning. Proven experience deploying and operating machine learning models in production. Strong hands-on experience with AWS services and cloud architecture. Strong hands-on experience with Databricks, including MLflow, model registries, jobs, clusters, permissions, and model-serving capabilities. Experience building CI/CD pipelines using tools such as GitHub Actions, GitLab CI/CD, Jenkins, Azure DevOps, or AWS CodePipeline, Docker and containerized application deployment. Experience with Kubernetes and managed container platforms such as Amazon EKS or ECS. Proficiency in Python and experience building production-quality APIs and inference services. Experience with REST APIs, asynchronous processing, event-driven architectures, and distributed systems. Strong knowledge of Infrastructure as Code, preferably Terraform. Experience with model versioning, artifact management, experiment tracking, and deployment promotion workflows. Experience implementing monitoring, logging, tracing, alerting, and production support processes. Strong understanding of high availability, disaster recovery, fault tolerance, and rollback strategies. Knowledge of cloud networking, IAM, secrets management, encryption, and secure software delivery. Training and inference workflows Online and batch inference Model serialization and packaging Feature engineering and feature consistency Model validation and evaluation,l drift and data drift Model explainability and reproducibility GPU-based model serving Embeddings and vector databases Retrieval-augmented generation Prompt management and versioning LLM evaluation and guardrails Token limits, context management, and inference cost optimization Responsible AI, content safety, and human-in-the-loop controls This role does not necessarily require the candidate to develop new machine learning algorithms. jobs.title: Senior Privacy Engineer – Automation & Data Mapping
jobs.description: Job Description The Senior Privacy Operations Engineer bridges privacy compliance and technical implementation, architecting, building, and maintaining the tooling, automation, and data infrastructure that powers the company’s global privacy program across UK/EU, US, APAC, and other regions. This role works closely with engineering and product teams to operationalize privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default requirements, and owns the technical backbone connecting privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust), work-management systems (e.g., Azure DevOps, Jira), and the organization’s broader data and cloud infrastructure. This is a senior, hands-on engineering role requiring both strong technical depth and working knowledge of global privacy regulatory concepts. Key Responsibilities Privacy Automation Engineering Design, build, and maintain automation for privacy operations workflows, including data subject rights fulfillment, data discovery, data mapping, and privacy assessment triggering. Build and maintain API and Power Automate integrations between privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust) and internal systems (ticketing/ADO/Jira, identity, data stores), including field mapping, assignment logic, bi-directional status sync, and error handling/logging so systems do not drift apart. Implement risk-based conditional logic and trigger workflows for privacy assessments (PIAs/DPIAs/TIAs) tied to intake or procurement systems, including escalation paths for high-risk triggers and governance/audit trails over the trigger rules themselves. Design and maintain automated redaction and exception-flagging pipelines (e.g., keyword/pattern matching, ML classifiers) for DSAR fulfillment, ensuring a mandatory human-review checkpoint before release and maintaining an audit log of redaction decisions. Data Mapping & ROPA Infrastructure Build and maintain an automated, event-driven data flow inventory and data mapping pipeline, tied to system/vendor intake and procurement processes rather than periodic manual surveys. Build and maintain integrations with data discovery and classification tooling (e.g., OneTrust Data Discovery, BigID, Collibra, AWS Macie, Azure Purview, database crawlers) to automatically feed classifications and data flows into ROPA records. Implement drift-detection mechanisms that reconcile ROPA records against discovery/mapping tool outputs, and support metrics such as percentage of ROPA records reviewed within a defined window. Support technical aspects of privacy impact assessments, including data flow diagrams and system/architecture review. Privacy-by-Design Engineering & Product Collaboration Partner with engineering and product teams to implement privacy-by-design and privacy-by-default controls within products and internal systems. Assist in the technical implementation of data retention and deletion requirements across structured and unstructured data sources. Advise engineering teams on technical architecture considerations for new products and features from a privacy and data protection perspective. Program Tooling, Reporting & Observability Build and maintain KPI dashboards and reporting pipelines (e.g., ADO Analytics, Power BI) that translate raw work-item and automation data into executive-ready privacy program metrics (DSAR SLA compliance, assessment backlog, incident response times). Monitor and report on the health of privacy tooling and automated processes, troubleshooting integration or data-quality issues as they arise. Maintain governance over report definitions and automation/trigger rule changes so metrics and workflows remain consistent and trustworthy over time. DSAR & Assessment Automation at Scale Design and maintain automated routing of DSAR tasks with data-owner mapping across multiple systems, SLA tracking tied to statutory deadlines, and tiered escalation as deadlines approach. Build scalable automation and surge-capacity mechanisms (triage automation, templated responses) to support DSAR volume spikes, incorporating lessons learned into ongoing process improvements. Support automation of assessment intake quality, including conditional required fields, real-time validation, and automated reminders to reduce incomplete submissions. Required Qualifications 5-7 years of experience in a data engineering, software engineering, or technical privacy/compliance engineering role, ideally supporting privacy or compliance operations at a global or multinational organization. Strong proficiency in at least one programming/scripting language (e.g., Python, SQL) and demonstrated experience building and maintaining API integrations and automated workflows (e.g., Power Automate, custom scripts, middleware). Hands-on experience building integrations between privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust, BigID, Collibra) and internal systems (ticketing/ADO/Jira, identity, data stores), including field mapping, assignment logic, and bi-directional status sync with error handling. Experience designing and maintaining automated data discovery and data mapping pipelines across structured and unstructured data sources (e.g., AWS Macie, Azure Purview, database crawlers) that feed ROPA records. Experience implementing risk-based conditional logic and trigger workflows for privacy assessments (PIA/DPIA/TIA) tied to intake or procurement systems. Experience building reporting/analytics pipelines (e.g., ADO Analytics, Power BI) that translate raw operational data into KPI dashboards for privacy program leadership. Solid understanding of core privacy concepts (data minimization, purpose limitation, data subject rights, retention) and global privacy regulations (UK GDPR/EU GDPR, CCPA/CPRA, PIPEDA, or similar) as applied to technical system design. Experience working with structured and unstructured data across multiple systems and cloud environments. Preferred Qualifications Experience with privacy management platforms (e.g., OneTrust, BigID, Collibra) and their APIs/connector frameworks. CIPT certification. Experience with cloud data infrastructure (AWS, Azure, or GCP), including native discovery/classification services (e.g., Macie, Purview). Experience building automated redaction/exception-flagging pipelines with tuned accuracy and governed human-review checkpoints. Experience supporting DSAR automation at scale, including SLA tracking/escalation design and volume-spike scaling strategies. Experience designing event-driven data mapping architectures integrated with CMDB/asset inventory or cloud discovery tooling. Skills & Competencies Strong systems-design thinking with the ability to balance automation against defensibility and risk Ability to work independently and collaboratively across global engineering, legal, and privacy teams Strong troubleshooting and debugging skills across integrated systems Adaptability to evolving regulatory and technical requirements Clear communication skills to translate technical architecture into terms non-technical privacy and legal stakeholders can act on #LI-KP1 What’s in it For You? observability dashboards • Serve as L1/L2 production support, providing first response monitoring, triage, and escalation to tech teams as new agentic services go live • Identify and diagnose issues by monitoring eval scores and drift alerts, inspecting failing traces and patterns, and classifying root causes such as intent, tool, parameter, or hallucination errors • Evaluate whether the agent’s production reliability, including API and authentication failures and issues originating from external AI endpoints, to protect revenue generating, client facing agents • Partner with AI Engineering This is a hands-on engineering leadership role: you will manage the vendor technical leads and drive a multi-disciplinary DevOps team of SAP Commerce Cloud, Composable Storefront, UI, and QA engineers. The role demands deep technical expertise in SAP Commerce Cloud, headless commerce architecture, along with the ability to partner with the Business Product Owner, enterprise architecture, and business stakeholders to deliver secure, scalable, and high-impact customer experiences. Key Responsibilities: 1. Engineering Leadership & Platform Ownership Own the technical health, roadmap execution, and engineering quality of the GSKDirect-US and GSKDirect-Global eCommerce platforms built on SAP Commerce Cloud and SAP Composable Storefront. Serve as the design authority for commerce solutions, approving designs across OCC APIs, B2B commerce (company accounts, customer-specific catalogs and pricing, approvals, checkout), SSO, ERP integrations and Backoffice. Make build-vs-configure decisions that favor out-of-the-box SAP capabilities, reduce technical debt, and keep the platform upgrade-ready. Implement and enforce ITMS (IT Management System) controls, ensuring compliance, audit readiness, and operational excellence in a regulated environment. 2. Vendor Management & Delivery Oversight Manage and direct the vendor technical leads, DevOps scrum teams of SAP Commerce, Composable Storefront, UI, and QA engineers. Own sprint delivery across 3–4 week agile cycles: backlog grooming, story analysis, estimation, sprint planning, reviews, and retrospectives, and hold vendor teams accountable for quality, velocity, and commitments. Lead daily scrum with GSK leads and business stakeholders, removing blockers and making timely technical decisions. Track vendor performance against SLAs and KPIs (velocity, defect leakage, cycle time, incident resolution), and drive corrective actions and resourcing decisions with the supplier. Foster a “One Team” culture across GSK, onshore, and offshore team members built on collaboration, support, and accountability. 3. Hands-on SAP Commerce Cloud & Headless Commerce Expertise Provide technical direction on SAP Commerce Cloud environment management and deployments. Guide the headless storefront architecture on SAP Composable Storefront (Spartacus) and Angular, including SSR, lazy loading, performance optimization, accessibility, and reusable component and design-system patterns. Lead code quality through GitHub pull request reviews, coding standards, unit testing expectations, and secure development practices. Drive root cause analysis of complex production issues. 4. Strategic Partnerships & Business Alignment Partner with the GSK Business Product Owner and business stakeholders in the US and global markets to translate commercial needs into scalable technical solutions and a prioritized roadmap. Align with enterprise architecture, security, and integration teams (ERP, identity, data) within a federated architecture model. Influence roadmap and investment decisions by providing technical insights, feasibility assessments, and effort estimates, and explain technical trade-offs in clear, non-technical language. 5. Innovation & Continuous Improvement Modernize engineering practices: CI/CD pipelines (GitHub, Jenkins, Azure DevOps), test automation, release management, and environment strategy on CCv2. Drive AI-assisted engineering across the vendor DevOps team. That means GitHub Copilot for coding, unit tests and pull request reviews; AI help with story grooming and writing acceptance criteria; and tracking the impact on velocity and quality. jobs.title: Associate Software Engineer
jobs.description: ROLE SUMMARY Are you an early-career software engineer who cares about writing good code and wants to learn from experienced engineers while building systems that matter? Join us at FTSE Russell! We’re building a team of engineers passionate about software craftsmanship, quality, and continuous improvement. As an Associate Software Engineer, you’ll contribute to the software that powers indices trusted by financial institutions worldwide, working alongside experienced engineers who will help you develop your technical skills and engineering judgement. We build primarily in Python, so experience with Python is valuable — but we’re equally interested in strong programming fundamentals and your ability to learn. If you’ve worked with Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, Rust, or another modern programming language and are motivated to develop your Python skills, we’d like to hear from you. This is a hands-on engineering role. You’ll write, test, review, and improve production software as part of an experienced engineering team. You’ll learn how well-designed software is built and operated in practice — from clean code and automated testing to APIs, databases, cloud services, observability, and production support. You won’t be expected to know everything from day one. We’re looking for engineers with solid foundations, curiosity, and the willingness to learn, ask questions, take feedback, and gradually take ownership of increasingly complex work. If you’re excited about developing as a software engineer while building systems used in global financial markets, we’d love to meet you. WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING We’re building the next-generation index data platform at FTSE Russell — and you’ll help us build it: Writing clean, maintainable production code, primarily in Python, with guidance and support from more experienced engineers Building and enhancing software components, services, APIs, and shared libraries as part of a collaborative engineering team Writing automated tests and learning how to build software that is reliable, secure, and easy to maintain Participating in code reviews — learning from feedback on your own code and gradually developing the skills to review the work of others Investigating bugs and production issues, understanding root causes, and implementing well-tested fixes Working with relational databases such as Aurora PostgreSQL, learning good practices around data modelling, queries, and schema evolution Developing software running on AWS using technologies such as Lambda, containerised services, object storage, and other managed AWS services Contributing to data-intensive applications that process significant volumes of financial and index data Using CI/CD pipelines and development tooling to build, test, and deploy software safely Learning how observability, logging, monitoring, and quality controls help us operate reliable production systems Working closely with engineers, product colleagues, and other stakeholders to understand requirements and deliver useful solutions Taking part in design discussions and learning how experienced engineers evaluate technical options and trade-offs Building knowledge of financial indices and understanding how the software you develop supports our customers Continuously developing your engineering skills through hands-on work, feedback, pairing, and knowledge sharing WHAT YOU’LL BRING Essential — we’re looking for strong foundations and potential: A foundation in software development gained through professional experience, internships, graduate programmes, university projects, open-source contributions, or substantial personal projects Programming experience in Python or another modern language such as Java, C#, C, C++, Scala, Go, or Rust, together with a willingness to develop strong Python skills Understanding of core software engineering concepts such as functions, classes, data structures, APIs, error handling, and automated testing An interest in writing readable, maintainable code rather than simply making something work Basic understanding of software development practices such as version control, code review, testing, and debugging Familiarity with Git or another source control system Basic knowledge of relational databases and SQL An analytical approach to problem solving and the ability to break problems into smaller, manageable pieces Curiosity and willingness to learn new technologies, tools, and engineering practices Openness to feedback and an interest in learning from more experienced engineers Good communication skills and the confidence to ask questions when something is unclear A collaborative mindset — you enjoy solving problems with others and contributing to a supportive engineering environment We don’t expect Associate Engineers to arrive knowing our entire technology stack. Strong programming fundamentals, evidence that you enjoy building software, and the ability to learn are more important than having used every technology listed in this description. NICE TO HAVES Beneficial, but definitely not required: Experience building applications, APIs, services, or libraries in Python Familiarity with Python development practices such as type hints, pytest, linters, and dependency management Exposure to AWS or another public cloud platform Experience with PostgreSQL or another relational database Understanding of REST APIs and distributed or service-based architectures Experience with Docker or containerised applications Familiarity with CI/CD tooling such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, or GitHub Actions Exposure to infrastructure as code such as Terraform or AWS CDK Experience with data processing, ETL, or data-intensive applications Exposure to Pandas, Apache Spark / PySpark, or similar data-processing technologies Familiarity with object storage, data lakes, or technologies such as Apache Iceberg Contributions to open-source projects or personal software projects you can talk us through Experience in financial markets, financial data, or investment analytics An interest in financial markets and a willingness to learn the index domain Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, collaboration, and continuous improvement. This role is an opportunity to build strong software engineering foundations, learn from experienced engineers, and gradually take on greater technical responsibility while contributing to software used across global financial markets. We're proud to have been recognised as a Great Place to Work® in India ‘25 Career Stage: Associate London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) Information: Join us and be part of a team that values innovation, quality, and continuous improvement. If you're ready to take your career to the next level and make a significant impact, we'd love to hear from you. LSEG is a leading global financial markets infrastructure and data provider. Our purpose is driving financial stability, empowering economies and enabling customers to create sustainable growth. Our purpose is the foundation on which our culture is built. Our values of Integrity, Partnership , Excellence and Change underpin our purpose and set the standard for everything we do, every day. They go to the heart of who we are and guide our decision making and everyday actions. Working with us means that you will be part of a dynamic organisation of 25,000 people across 65 countries. However, we will value your individuality and enable you to bring your true self to work so you can help enrich our diverse workforce. We are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. This means that we do not discriminate on the basis of anyone’s race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, age, marital status, veteran status, pregnancy or disability, or any other basis protected under applicable law. Conforming with applicable law, we can reasonably accommodate applicants' and employees' religious practices and beliefs, as well as mental health or physical disability needs. You will be part of a collaborative and creative culture where we encourage new ideas. We are committed to sustainability across our global business and we are proud to partner with our customers to help them meet their sustainability objectives. Our charity, the LSEG Foundation provides charitable grants to community groups that help people access economic opportunities and build a secure future with financial independence. Colleagues can get involved through fundraising and volunteering. LSEG offers a range of tailored benefits and support, including healthcare, retirement planning, paid volunteering days and wellbeing initiatives. jobs.title: Senior Product Engineer - STA
jobs.description: Company Overview Siemens EDA is a global technology leader in Electronic Design Automation software. Our software tools enable companies around the world to develop highly innovative electronic products faster and more cost-effectively. Our customers use our tools to push the boundaries of technology and physics to deliver better products in the increasingly complex world of chip, board, and system design. Position Overview We are seeking a talented Product Engineer – STA to join our team in Bangalore and Noida. In this role, you will work on cutting-edge 7nm and 5nm designs with various customers for the deployment of Aprisa place and route tools. You will be an expert in solving critical design challenges to achieve desired performance, area, and power targets. You will develop flows and methodologies for placement, CTS, and routing while providing training and technical support to customers using Aprisa tools. This is a hybrid role offering flexibility while enabling you to travel across India and globally to support our customers and teams shaping the future of semiconductor design. Key Responsibilities • Develop and optimize placement, CTS, and routing flows and methodologies for complex block and full-chip designs using Aprisa tools. • Provide expert technical support and training to customers deploying Aprisa place and route tools for 7nm and 5nm designs. • Solve critical design problems to achieve desired performance, area, and power targets for complex semiconductor designs. • Identify and resolve timing, power, and area trade-offs using deep domain expertise and optimization techniques. • Collaborate with R&D teams to develop signoff-ready ECO flows and drive correlation improvements. • Proactively triage and resolve customer issues and JIRAs, driving solutions through to completion with ownership mentality. • Leverage AI tools (e.g., Copilot, AI-assisted scripting) to optimize workflows, automate repetitive tasks, and accelerate debugging. • Provide clear cross-functional communication between customers, R&D, and internal teams to ensure project success. Qualifications • 4–8 years of hands-on experience in Physical Design (floorplan, placement, CTS, routing) and timing closure of complex blocks and/or full-chip designs. • Proven experience with commercial place and route tools such as Synopsys-ICC2, Cadence-Innovus, or Aprisa. • Tapeout experience on 2 or more projects. • Strong understanding of timing, power, and area trade-offs in semiconductor design. • Highly skilled in leveraging AI tools (e.g., Copilot, AI-assisted scripting) to optimize workflows, debug, and automate repetitive tasks. • Excellent verbal and written communication abilities with strong presentation and problem-solving skills. • Experience with Static Timing Analysis (STA) tools such as PrimeTime and Tempus is preferred. Additional Preferred Qualifications • Experience with multiple voltage islands and top-level floor-planning and chip-assembly. • BE/B.Tech in Electronics and Communication (E&C), Electrical, or Telecom Engineering; ME/M.Tech in VLSI or Microelectronics is a plus. • Ability to pick up new flows, learn on the job, and drive quality of results improvements. Why Us We are Siemens: At Siemens Software, flexibility is how we work—hybrid by default, built on trust and autonomy. Together, 30,000 people across more than 200 countries build technology that shapes the real world. You'll grow through real projects, strong technical peers, and global mobility, backed by the scale and benefits of an industrial software leader. We're committed to equality and inclusion, and we hire based on merit, skills, and impact. Bring your curiosity and creativity and help us shape tomorrow! Diversity & Inclusion We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, sex, gender, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. We are committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce and welcome applications from all qualified candidates. Siemens Software. Transform the Everyday #LI-Hybrid #LI-EDA

jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Manager
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own Emerging Tech and AI Tooling, the front edge of GSK’s AI platform estate. You will run structured evaluation of new AI tools and platforms, decide what graduates into a standing tower and what gets retired, and own the AI developer tooling GSK engineers use every day. It suits someone who can hold an evaluation to a decision date and retire tools the organisation is attached to. You will lead a small engineering squad and set direction a far larger estate inherits. Why This Role Exists : Every week brings a new AI tool and a stakeholder who wants it. Without a disciplined front door, evaluations never close and nothing is ever retired. This role runs that front door, and owns the developer tooling estate so the tools engineers depend on daily have a named owner rather than a shared inbox. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the evaluation portfolio for new AI tools and platforms across Enterprise AI. Decides what graduates into a standing platform tower, what holds, and what gets retired. Owns the AI developer tooling estate end to end. Hands graduated platforms over with a working operating model. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management: This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Evaluation & Graduation: Run every evaluation to a decision. Set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the kill date up front. Keep a live view of what is in flight, on hold, or retired. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible adoption and retirement cases that survive finance and architecture scrutiny — engineering hours saved, licence cost avoided, capability gained, duplication removed. Tell new capability from repackaging so overlap with what GSK already runs is caught before it becomes duplicate spend. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping: Shape the emerging tech portfolio. Keep a living view of in-flight, queued, and retired evaluations with the rationale for each call, and feed it into the AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make the graduate, retire, or hold call. Decide which tower receives a graduating platform, and hold the decision date when the organisation would rather extend it. Protect the estate from sprawl. Say no, with evidence, to tools that look attractive but do not change what the organisation can actually do. Engineering Partnership & Enablement: Lead the Emerging Tech and AI Tooling squad. Set direction for a small full-stack team across evaluation builds and the tooling estate, and stay close enough to review the work. Own the graduation handover. Hand the receiving tower an operating model, support path, and entitlement design. Own the AI developer tooling estate. Run access, entitlement, support, and adoption for the coding and desktop tools engineers depend on daily. Stay hands on. Prototype alongside the team and form your own judgment on a tool by using it. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication: Operate fluently with VP-level technology and business leaders. Run conversations that turn vendor enthusiasm into a testable hypothesis with a decision date. Build sponsor coalitions that secure evaluation funding, pilot cohorts, and the air cover to retire tools people are attached to. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects tooling investment to engineering throughput and enterprise outcomes. Measurement, Learning & Iteration: Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every evaluation and graduation and improve it with what you learn. Run honest post-mortems on evaluations that failed, and feed lessons back into how the front door selects what to test. Required skil ls: 16+ years of progressive experience spanning some combination of pharma/life sciences, AI/ML product strategy, and senior product management or strategy roles in technology-led organisations. Demonstrated track record of identifying, scoping, prototyping, and shepherding high-value technology or AI initiatives from problem framing through funding into delivery. Strong working knowledge of enterprise AI platforms and developer tooling — how they are licensed, entitled, supported, and adopted at scale — and of at least one part of the pharma value chain. Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML — LLMs, agentic systems, AI agents and workers, ML lifecycle, data and evaluation patterns — sufficient to leverage evidence from rapid prototyping to challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices. Experience leading a small engineering team while operating with a span of influence far wider than the headcount — leading through frameworks, evidence, and quality of thinking. A product management or product-strategy heritage: discovery, opportunity sizing, roadmap shaping, prototyping, and stakeholder alignment — ideally on products whose core behaviour is AI rather than conventional software. Preferred skills: Hands on with the AI platform ecosystem as a daily practitioner: fluent in how the landscape is categorised, where the category boundaries actually fall, and which capabilities are genuinely distinct from each other. Able to evaluate from first principles and to design the evaluation itself: set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the decision date, and defend the method to engineers and vendors alike. A proven record of retiring and consolidating technology, including at least one tool killed on evidence. #AGTech Skills AI Platforms, Artificial Intelligence, Change Management, Data Analysis, Feature Prioritization, Machine Learning (ML), Machine Learning Model Management, ML Platforms, Model Evaluation, Performance Analysis, Product Delivery, Product Design, Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Product Roadmapping, Product Strategies, Roadmap Development, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis Why GSK? jobs.title: Senior Solution Support Engineer
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team is expanding its ability to architect, build, and run complex AI solutions across the enterprise. Senior Solutions Engineers sit at the intersection of technical architecture, hands-on AI engineering, and production operations — ensuring that AI capabilities translate reliably into production value and keep delivering it after go-live. As a Senior Solutions Engineer you will own the technical solution design for complex AI integrations and personally build and operate them, working across EAI engineering, business technology teams, external partners, and strategic suppliers to ensure that what gets built can be deployed, integrated, maintained, and operated at enterprise scale. This is a hands-on role: you will design, build, and review AI systems yourself — including LLM, agentic, and retrieval-based solutions — working within the architectural standards, engineering practices, and lifecycle framework set by the Staff Solutions Engineer, and contributing to how they evolve. You bring both the architectural depth to make the right design choices and the communication skills to earn confidence across technical and business audiences. The role carries direct accountability for the AI products and integrations you deliver. Expect to spend roughly 40% of your time on production operations and support — keeping the lights on (KTLO), meeting SLAs and service metrics, and day-to-day coordination with strategic suppliers — and roughly 60% on engineering, with a deliberate focus on using that engineering to automate operations and steadily reduce the operational load. You will use AI agents as part of your engineering and operations toolkit, supervising their output, to keep lowering the cost at which value is delivered for the solutions you own. As those solutions scale in deployment, you are responsible for identifying when the current engineered solution needs to be refactored and/or optimised, and for recommending and delivering that change — escalating portfolio-level cases to the Staff Solutions Engineer. Why This Role Exists: As the Enterprise AI portfolio matures, the complexity of integration, deployment, and operations grows. Many of the most valuable AI opportunities require deep technical solutioning before engineering can begin, hands-on engineering to build them, and disciplined operation once they are live. In this role you will be the person who: Closes the gap between AI capability and enterprise deployment readiness through rigorous technical solutioning. Enables faster delivery by resolving integration complexity early, before it becomes a production blocker. Builds and ships production AI solutions hands-on, so that architectural decisions are grounded in working code rather than slideware. Keeps products healthy in production by owning KTLO, SLAs, and service metrics for the solutions you deliver. Automates the run through monitoring, AIOps, and AI agents, so reliability improves and the cost to operate falls as the portfolio grows. Governs the lifecycle by applying Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) discipline — stage gates, versioning, change control, and traceability — to every AI product you deliver. Raises the bar on solution quality by applying and contributing to architectural standards across complex engagements. Builds trust with business technology partners and enterprise architects through credible, well-grounded technical guidance. Key Responsibilities: Solution Architecture & Technical Design Own technical solution design for complex AI integrations — from requirements through to detailed architecture, component selection, and integration specification. Define integration patterns for connecting AI capabilities with enterprise systems: SAP, Veeva, Salesforce, clinical data platforms, and GSK’s data infrastructure. Design for operability so that observability, SLOs, runbooks, and support requirements are built into the solution from the start rather than added after go-live. Produce solution architecture documentation that enables downstream engineering teams to build with confidence and minimises ambiguity at handoff. Hands-On AI Engineering (approx. 60% of role) Build and ship production AI solutions — including LLM-based applications, agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and ML model serving — integrated with GSK enterprise systems. Write production-quality code and reference implementations, with tests, evaluation harnesses, guardrails, and CI/CD for the AI systems you deliver. Apply the function’s AI engineering standards — prompt and model versioning, evaluation, secure deployment — and contribute improvements back to them. jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Management (Global Functions)
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and digital workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager (Director level equivalent role) to own a major slice of our Global Functions portfolio and act as the strategic counterpart to the engineers and digital workers in your pod, setting the forward deployed strategy they execute against. This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can identify and shape high-value AI opportunities across the key areas of Global Functions - HR, Legal, Compliance, Procurement, or Finance, build the case to fund and deploy against them, and ensure FDEs are working on what matters most. You will not manage engineers; you will shape what they build in your domain and how we measure whether it worked. Why This Role Exists: Forward deployed teams are most powerful when paired with sharp opportunity selection. Enterprise AI has no separate strategy layer: the AI Product Manager sets the forward deployed strategy, and the pod executes it. This role closes that gap at this level by ensuring the engineers we deploy are working on the right things. In this role you will be the person who: Owns a clear domain or capability area within the Enterprise AI opportunity portfolio. Identifies, sizes, and shapes the highest-value AI opportunities in that domain. Partners daily with forward deployed, full-stack, and data engineering leads to scope and steer engagements end-to-end. Builds the business and executive alignment the pod needs to land and scale. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management: This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems rather than evolving an established platform. Work with probabilistic systems — defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight instead of fixed functional requirements. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to digital workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes, not features shipped or system uptime. Key Responsibilities: Opportunity Identification & Value Sizing: Hunt for high-value AI opportunities within your assigned domain at GSK; develop a structured pipeline of opportunities ranked by impact, feasibility, and time-to-value. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible business cases that survive finance and senior business unit scrutiny — cycle time saved, decisions accelerated, revenue uplift, cost avoided, scientific productivity gained. Develop deep domain pattern recognition so you can spot AI-shaped problems in workflows the business itself hasn’t yet articulated. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping: Shape the opportunity portfolio in your domain. Maintain a living view of in-flight, queued, and de-prioritized opportunities, with the rationale for each decision, and feed it into the broader Enterprise AI portfolio. Make trade-off recommendations. When two business sponsors both want an FDE pod, defines the success metrics, run the analysis and recommend where engineers go. Protect engineering focus. Push back — with evidence — on opportunities that won’t move scalable outcomes. Engineering Partnership & Enablement Be the strategic counterpart to forward deployed, full-stack, and data engineering leads in your domain. Translate ambiguous business problems into crisp problem statements, prototypes, success metrics, and decision frameworks engineers can build against. Shape engagements end-to-end. Define scope, success criteria, exit conditions, and scaling pathways before kick-off, then stay close as engineers execute. Surface re-use and platform leverage when a one-off solution should become a reusable capability. Design the human–digital split. Decide which tasks the pod’s digital workers own, where engineers and business users stay in the loop, and how evaluation and oversight make that safe. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication Operate fluently with VP-level business and scientific leaders. Run conversations that turn fuzzy ambitions into concrete, fundable AI engagements. Build sponsor coalitions that secure data access, change-management commitment, and air cover for your engagements. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects AI work to patients, science, and enterprise outcomes. Measurement, Learning & Iteration Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every engagement in your domain and improve it with what you learn. Run honest post-mortems and feed lessons back into how your domain selects opportunities. Required Functional Experience: 18+ years of progressive experience spanning some combination of pharma/life sciences, AI/ML product strategy, and senior product management or strategy roles in technology-led organisations. Demonstrated track record of identifying, scoping, prototyping, and shepherding high-value technology or AI initiatives from problem framing through funding into delivery. Strong working knowledge of at least one part of the pharma value chain — R&D, clinical, medical, manufacturing, commercial, or an enterprise function — including the data, decisions, and constraints inside it. Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML — LLMs, agentic systems, and digital workers, ML lifecycle, data and evaluation patterns — sufficient to leverage evidence from rapid prototyping to challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices. Experience operating as a senior individual contributor — leading through influence, frameworks, and quality of thinking rather than headcount. jobs.title: Engineer II, Full Stack Engineer
jobs.description: Job Purpose: Enterprise AI (EAI) builds AI products that combine real modelling work with user-facing applications, and ships them to production. Full Stack Engineers move across data, models, platforms, APIs and interfaces in a single workflow. In our operating model, digital workers do much of the hands-on build. They generate services, APIs, interface components and tests, run evaluations and monitor what is in production. Our engineers set the architecture and standards that work is built to, and own the quality of what ships. EAI products and agents draw on a governed context layer that makes data, meaning, permissions and history retrievable at the moment they are needed. Full Stack Engineers build the products and agents that consume it, and decide how that context reaches users. The Full Stack Engineer II independently builds and ships AI-integrated features, working closely with GSK business teams to prototype against real data and workflows at a days-to-weeks cadence. The role owns the quality of what digital workers deliver in those features, makes evidence-based calls on what to continue or stop, and contributes reusable components others adopt. Responsibilities: Own use cases from problem framing through working prototype and first production version, at a days-to-weeks cadence and without close supervision. Qualify incoming asks: challenge underspecified problems, assess feasibility and define scope before committing to work. At the end of each piece of work, form and defend an evidence-based recommendation to continue or stop, presented clearly to business and EAI leadership. Work closely with business teams, prototyping against real data and workflows and building trusted relationships with product owners and engineering leads. Required skills: 6+ years of full-stack or AI/ML engineering experience, including production deployments. Demonstrated ability to take ideas from sketch to working software at speed, independently and under time pressure. A startup, lab or innovation-team background is an advantage. Strong proficiency in Python and at least one of TypeScript, JavaScript, Go or similar, with experience designing and shipping backend services and complete UI features. Hands-on experience with GenAI patterns: agents, multi-agent orchestration, RAG, tool use, prompt engineering and evaluation, including evaluation pipelines and LLM-specific monitoring in production. Daily use of AI coding agents as the primary mode of development, with sound judgement on what to accept, change or reject. A track record of raising team standards through code review and documentation, and of contributing reusable engineering patterns that others adopted. Education : Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Preferred skills: Prior experience as a Full Stack Engineer, Customer Engineer or Solutions Architect, ideally at an AI-native company or hyperscaler. Experience in regulated industries, such as life sciences, healthcare or financial services, and familiarity with GxP, GDPR and SOX. Working knowledge of fine-tuning fundamentals and Model Context Protocol (MCP) integrations. #AGTech Skills Amazon Web Services (AWS), Artificial Intelligence (AI), Full Stack Development, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Machine Learning (ML) Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. Inclusion at GSK: As an employer committed to Inclusion, we encourage you to reach out if you need any adjustments during the recruitment process. Please contact our Recruitment Team at IN.recruitment-adjustments@gsk.com to discuss your needs. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Your Role We are seeking a Platform Security Architect to serve as a trusted advisor, shaping how security is embedded into modern private cloud and platform engineering environments. This role sits at the intersection of platform engineering, DevSecOps, and developer experience, with a strong emphasis on advisory, architecture definition, and governance. You will bring deep real-world delivery experience to ensure that recommendations are practical, scalable, and proven in production. You will support Consult-led opportunities across the full lifecycle (pre- and post-sale), working with clients on first-of-a-kind private cloud migration and modernization initiatives, including navigating sovereignty requirements and evolving regulatory landscapes. To our clients, you are the subject matter expert—engaging early, shaping the solution, defining architecture, and ultimately leading technical delivery. What you will do The Platform Security Architect is responsible for advising clients on the design and security of modern private cloud and platform engineering environments by defining target-state architectures, enforceable standards, and non-bypassable security guardrails. This includes shaping secure Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs), embedding policy-as-code governance, and establishing repeatable "golden paths" that enforce secure-by-default patterns across applications, Kubernetes, and infrastructure. The role also addresses the emerging threat of AI-accelerated vulnerability exploitation (informed by frameworks such as Mythos / Project Glasswing), defining architecture and controls that close the gaps adversaries can find and weaponize faster using AI — including accelerated vulnerability discovery, automated exploit chaining, and compressed attack timelines — so that platform defenses are hardened against machine-speed threats rather than human-speed ones. A key focus is reducing configuration variability, minimizing attack surfaces, and ensuring that security is inherently built into platform design rather than applied reactively. In addition, the role drives end-to-end DevSecOps and runtime security transformation by integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines, identity and access architectures, secrets management, and software and AI/ML supply chains. This includes architecting developer-facing tooling and testing capabilities that keep pace with today's AI-accelerated vulnerability landscape — enabling developers to identify, validate, and remediate exploitable weaknesses at the speed adversaries now operate at, rather than relying on traditional review cycles that assume human-speed attack timelines. The role further defines control frameworks, embeds continuous compliance, enables behavior-based runtime detection, and integrates real-time security feedback into developer workflows to maintain velocity without compromising governance. The architect also leads client engagements across pre- and post-sale phases—shaping solutions, guiding large-scale private cloud modernization programs (including sovereignty and regulatory requirements), and supporting go-to-market efforts through workshops, pilots, and thought leadership that advance Kyndryl's platform security and AI-risk mitigation capabilities. Whatever you see for yourself, you’ll find the opportunity here. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred!
