A core focus of the role is the development of Digital Twin computational models - including discrete event and optimization-based representations - that provide online modeling capabilities to manufacturing facilities, in alignment with the Engineering Digital Strategy for Manufacturing and Quality within Lilly. This is a global role, supporting functional initiatives and all Lilly Manufacturing sites globally. The primary focus of the role is to develop and deploy discrete event simulation and optimization models that increase manufacturing capacity, resilience, compliance, and inspection readiness, and that support operational excellence goals for safety, quality, and supply. The engineer will also serve as an internal advocate for simulation-based and model-based methods, fostering the use of discrete modeling tools by colleagues outside DME through instruction, consultation, and the development of internal collaborations. Key Objectives / Deliverables Develop and deploy discrete event simulation and optimization models to drive decisions that help design new and/or improve existing manufacturing and logistics processes. Develop capacity, throughput, line-balancing, and bottleneck-analysis models for parenteral fill/finish, device assembly, packaging, and material handling operations. Develop Digital Twin computational models of discrete manufacturing lines and logistics networks to provide online modeling capabilities to Lilly manufacturing facilities. Deliver sound interpretation of modeling results by maintaining in-depth knowledge of the underlying first-principles concepts (queueing theory, stochastic processes, scheduling theory) and numerical methods from which discrete event and optimization models are formulated and solved. Complement model-based solutions with empirical validation against site operating data and, when appropriate, time studies or shop-floor investigation. Prepare internal technical reports to document work and to contribute to the product or process body of knowledge, and when appropriate, publish and/or present work externally. Maintain and grow the functional value of discrete manufacturing modeling within Lilly by developing appropriate internal collaborations and sharing key learnings broadly at appropriate internal forums so colleagues can identify projects that may benefit from model-based analysis. Foster the use of discrete simulation and optimization tools by colleagues outside DME by providing instruction, consultation, and continuously advocating the use of simulation-based and model-based methods. Identify and implement modeling advances that bring value to Lilly by maintaining awareness of new developments in the external discrete event simulation and optimization landscape. Develop collaborations with appropriate external partners to help manage workload and to gain additional expertise. Partner with data leads within DME to provide data requirements that support discrete manufacturing models and Digital Twin solutions. Basic Qualifications PhD with 4-8 years of experience or MS degree with 8-15 years of experience in Industrial Engineering, Operations Research, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. Minimum of 4 years of related work experience (graduate research included). Experience developing models in one or more of the following: discrete event simulation, nonlinear programming, mixed-integer linear programming, or dynamic simulation of discrete systems. Demonstrated working knowledge of queueing theory, stochastic processes, and the numerical/optimization methods from which discrete event and optimization models are formulated and solved. Additional Skills / Preferences Strong technical writing and presentation skills. Capability to solve complex issues with minimal supervision. Experience with capacity analysis, line balancing, scheduling, and logistics optimization in a manufacturing environment. Experience developing simulation and optimization models leveraging commercial software tools such as ExtendSim, Frontline Solver, aspenONE, or equivalent discrete event simulation platforms. Experience with statistical analysis and data/model fitting leveraging commercial software tools such as JMP or similar. Experience developing digital twins of discrete manufacturing lines (e.g., parenteral fill/finish, device assembly, packaging). Experience working with validated systems and in a GMP/pharmaceutical industry environment. Ability to work well across different cultures and global manufacturing sites. jobs.title: Senior Manager - Total Rewards - Reward Reporting & Analytics
jobs.description:
Experience range: 8-13 Yrs
1. About EXL EXL (NASDAQ: EXLS) is a global data and AI company. We help the worlds leading organisations — across insurance, healthcare and life sciences, banking and capital markets, retail, communications and media, and energy and infrastructure — reinvent their business models, improve outcomes and unlock growth at speed. Founded in 1999 and headquartered in New York, EXL today employs approximately 68,000 colleagues across six continents and is a constituent of the S&P MidCap 400. 2. Where This Role Sits Corporate Rewards is the global centre of expertise for compensation, benefits, incentives and reward governance at EXL. The function designs the frameworks that determine how 68,000 people are paid, and works with business leadership, HR Business Partners, Talent Acquisition, Finance and Controllership to apply them consistently across a highly diverse geographic footprint. This role sits within the Reward Reporting & Analytics team and reports to the Senior Assistant Vice President – Reward Analytics & Reporting. It is a global, non-country-specific role: the postholder supports corporate reward initiatives, contributes to regional programmes and responds to employee and stakeholder compensation queries across geographies. Why this role matters now EXL is scaling quickly, changing its skill mix, and operating in an environment of rising pay transparency regulation. Reward decisions are increasingly expected to be evidenced, modelled and defensible before they are made. This role is where that evidence is built — the analytical engine behind pay decisions, budget conversations and governance reporting for the enterprise. 3. Role Overview The Senior Manager – Total Rewards (Reward Reporting & Analytics) delivers analytical, operational and advisory reward support to the Corporate Rewards function and its stakeholders. The role converts compensation, benefits and workforce data into decision-grade insight: dashboards leadership actually uses, benchmarking that stands up to challenge, cost models that Finance recognises, and pay equity analysis that withstands regulatory scrutiny. This is a hands-on, senior individual contributor role. Success depends less on managing people and more on technical depth, judgement, accuracy under pressure, and the ability to explain a complicated number simply to a busy executive. 4. Key Responsibilities The role is organized around eight areas of accountability. Weighting will flex with the reward calendar — benchmarking and budget work peaks in the planning cycle, pay equity and disclosure work peaks around statutory reporting deadlines. 4.1 Reward Analytics, Reporting & Insight Build, maintain and continuously improve the monthly and quarterly reward dashboards used for leadership and governance review — covering pay positioning, compensation cost, incentive funding, attrition-linked pay signals and reward programme utilisation. Design reporting that answers a question rather than simply displaying data: define the metric set, the comparison basis and the narrative before building the visual. Translate complex, multi-country reward and workforce datasets into concise, executive-ready insight and recommendations for HR and business stakeholders. Automate recurring reporting so that analyst time shifts from assembling data to interpreting it; maintain documented, repeatable and auditable production processes. Undertake ad-hoc modelling and scenario analysis — cost of change, sensitivity, what-if — to support live reward decisions. 4.2 Compensation & Incentive Programme Support Support the administration and governance of short-term incentive (STI) programmes, including annual bonus, pay-for-performance and sales commission frameworks: eligibility, funding, accrual tracking, modelling, payout calculation, validation and post-cycle analysis. Support the annual compensation review cycle — budget modelling, distribution guidelines, manager reporting, moderation analytics, exception tracking and post-cycle effectiveness review. Provide compensation analysis and recommendations for promotions, market adjustments, retention cases, geographic mobility and other ad-hoc requests, applying consistent internal equity and market logic. Interpret and apply global reward principles across regions, ensuring consistency, documented rationale and compliance with local requirements. 4.3 Job Pricing & Market Intelligence Work closely with the other leaders on the Market Benchmarking and support with participation in salary and benefits surveys — job matching, data submission, quality assurance and results interpretation — across major survey houses and industry forums (for example Mercer, WTW, Aon, Korn Ferry, Radford). Analyse market data to produce reliable pay positioning views by geography, job family and level, including compa-ratio and range penetration analysis. Support job pricing, job evaluation and levelling activity in partnership with Corporate Rewards and Finance, maintaining the integrity of the job-code to survey-benchmark mapping. 4.4 Pay Equity, Transparency & DEI Analytics Support pay equity, gender pay gap and wider DEI reward analyses — data preparation, cohort construction, statistical testing, remediation modelling and insight development. Prepare data and supporting analysis for statutory and voluntary disclosures, including UK and IR gender pay gap reporting and emerging pay transparency obligations across EU and other markets. Maintain the analytical audit trail so that any published or internally circulated figure can be traced to source and reproduced on request. 4.5 HR Budget, Cost & Workforce Financials Support monthly HR budget tracking, including headcount analysis, compensation cost movement and expense monitoring against plan. Review cost allocations, identify and explain variances, and help stakeholders understand what is actually driving spend patterns. Contribute to the annual HR budget planning process — collating inputs, preparing analyses and partnering with Finance and Controllership on alignment and assumptions. Support ongoing forecasting, tracking expenditure against budget and highlighting variances and emerging risks early enough to act on them. 4.6 Employee Value Proposition, Benefits & Reward Projects Contribute to reward projects spanning benefits, incentives, recognition and wider EVP initiatives — typically owning the analytical and cost-modelling workstream. Review benefit competitiveness, utilisation and cost-effectiveness as part of broader reward reviews, renewals or country-level initiatives. Provide the evidence base for reward design choices: what it costs, what it buys, who it affects and what the alternatives are. 4.7 Reward Data, Systems & Automation Own the accuracy, consistency and governance of compensation and benefits data across internal and external systems; investigate and resolve discrepancies in partnership with HR Shared Services and HRIS. Build and maintain reusable data pipelines, structured data models and reporting layers that make reward data dependable rather than repeatedly reconstructed. Collaborate with HRIS and HR Shared Services on the effective configuration and administration of reward systems, including compensation cycle tooling and downstream reporting. Apply data privacy, confidentiality and access-control discipline appropriate to sensitive personal and pay data across multiple jurisdictions. 4.8 Stakeholder Partnership & Advisory Act as a trusted analytical partner to HR Business Partners, Recruiters, Finance and business stakeholders on compensation-related queries, requests and escalations. Respond to general employee compensation queries with accuracy, discretion and clarity. Support cross-functional collaboration on reward initiatives, and influence outcomes through evidence rather than authority — this role carries no formal reporting line into the stakeholders it advises. 5. AI-Enabled Ways of Working EXL is a data and AI company, and we expect our own functions to work the way our clients aspire to. Practical fluency with enterprise AI tooling is a meaningful differentiator for this role, not an optional extra. Expected Confident, everyday use of Microsoft 365 Copilot across Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams to accelerate analysis, drafting, summarisation and meeting follow-through. Use of large language model assistants — such as Claude and Copilot Chat — to structure analysis, draft policy and communication content, interrogate documents, and produce first-cut code for data preparation and reporting. Sound judgement on what may and may not be shared with an AI tool: employee-level pay data, personal data and confidential business information are handled strictly within approved enterprise tooling and EXL data-handling policy. Verification discipline — AI output is treated as a draft to be checked, never as a source of truth. Every number that leaves this team is traceable to a system of record. Strongly Advantageous Prompt design skill sufficient to get reliable, repeatable output from AI tools on recurring reward tasks — benchmarking summaries, policy comparison, variance commentary, survey job-matching support. Experience building lightweight AI-assisted automations or agents (for example Copilot Studio, Power Automate, or scripted LLM workflows) that remove manual effort from reward reporting. A demonstrable record of having made a reward process measurably faster or more accurate using AI — we will ask for a specific example. Interest in helping the wider Rewards team raise its own AI capability, including sharing reusable prompts, templates and working patterns. What we are looking for Not a prompt enthusiast, and not an AI sceptic. Someone who uses these tools daily, knows exactly where they add value and where they do not, and can show the difference it has made to real work. 6. Skills & Technical Capability Advanced Excel & Data Modelling - Complex models built to be understood by others — structured, documented, version-controlled; Power Query, advanced formula logic, robust reconciliation. Data Visualization & BI - Power BI (or Tableau/Qlik) dashboards with a defined metric layer, clean data model and design that supports a decision rather than decorating a dataset. Compensation Analytics - Compa-ratio, range penetration, quartile positioning, market movement, incentive funding and cost-of-change modelling applied fluently across geographies. HR Systems & Data Structures - Working command of a major HCM platform (Workday, SuccessFactors, Oracle HCM or similar), its compensation module and its underlying data model. Pay Equity & Regulatory Analysis - Cohort design, gap decomposition, remediation modelling; working knowledge of UK gender pay gap reporting and pay transparency requirements in EU and other markets. Budgeting & Cost Analysis - Comfortable in the language of Finance — accrual, variance, phasing, forecast — and able to reconcile HR numbers to the ledger. AI Tooling - Daily, judicious use of Copilot and Claude for analysis, drafting and automation, within enterprise data-handling policy. Automation Platforms - Power Automate, Power Apps or equivalent applied to remove manual steps from the reward reporting cycle. Job Architecture & Levelling - Familiarity with job families, levelling frameworks and survey-house crosswalk maintenance. 7. Capabilities & Behaviors Analytical Rigor - Interrogates the data before presenting it. Knows the limitations of the dataset and states them. Never presents a number they cannot reproduce. Precision Under Pressure - Reward work is unforgiving of error — payout files, disclosures and board reporting must be right the first time, on a deadline. Commercial Judgement - Understands that reward decisions are business decisions. Frames analysis in terms of cost, risk and retention rather than methodology. Communication & Storytelling - Explains a complex model to a non-technical executive in three sentences and one chart. Writes clearly and without jargon. Stakeholder Influence - Builds credibility across HR, Finance and the business without formal authority; pushes back constructively when the data does not support the request. Confidentiality & Integrity - Handles individual pay, personal and sensitive data with absolute discretion across multiple regulatory regimes. Ownership & Pace - Works comfortably in a fast-moving, matrixed, multi-time-zone organization; manages competing priorities without dropping quality. Curiosity & Improvement - Actively looks for the manual process that should not exist any more, and fixes it. 8. Experience & Qualifications Essential Approximately 8–12 years of professional experience, with a minimum of 5 years in compensation (recent), total rewards or HR/people analytics. Demonstrable experience of reward analytics and reporting in a large, multinational, matrixed organization — including multi-country datasets and multi-currency analysis. Hands-on ownership of compensation cycle analytics and/or incentive modelling, not solely oversight of others doing it. Experience partnering with Finance on budget, headcount cost or forecasting activity. Graduate degree in a numerate, business or HR-related discipline (for example Business, Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Finance or HR), is preferred. Fluent written and spoken English, with the ability to work effectively across time zones and cultures. Desirable Postgraduate qualification (MBA / Master’s) in HR, Business, Economics or a quantitative discipline. Professional certification — CCP (WorldatWork), GRP, CIPD or equivalent. Experience in professional services, technology, BPM, analytics or another high-growth, people-intensive industry. Prior consulting experience with a reward or human capital advisory practice. Exposure to UK, Ireland, EMEA or South Africa reward practice and regulation.

jobs.description:
Experience range: 9-14 Yrs
Role Purpose The HR Partner will support the Analytics & AI business and act as a strategic HR advisor to business and operations leadership , combining strong HR fundamentals with commercial understanding, data-driven decision-making, technology orientation and an understanding of the evolving Analytics and AI ecosystem. The role requires an HR professional who is curious about AI, digital technologies and analytics , is comfortable working with data, and has the ability to translate business and people challenges into pragmatic HR solutions. The incumbent should have a strong interest in leveraging AI, automation, dashboards and analytics to improve HR processes, employee experience, workforce insights and business outcomes. Key Responsibilities 1. Strategic HR Business Partnering & Analytics Domain Knowledge Partner closely with Analytics & AI business leaders as a strategic HR advisor and provide solutions to people-related business challenges. Develop a strong understanding of the Analytics, Data, Digital and AI business , including business models, talent segments, critical skills, workforce priorities and emerging capability requirements. Build business and commercial knowledge within the HR team to strengthen its ability to operate as a strategic partner to business and operations. Understand business challenges and proactively identify opportunities where HR process redesign, analytics, AI or automation can improve business outcomes. Identify emerging people risks, capability gaps and organizational issues early and appropriately escalate and resolve them. Ensure consistent implementation of organizational policies, processes and values while fostering a professional, collaborative and high-performance work environment. 2. HR Analytics, Dashboards & Data-Driven Decision Making Build and manage HR dashboards and people analytics covering key metrics such as attrition, retention, diversity, hiring, employee engagement, talent movement, compensation and workforce trends. Translate people data into actionable business insights , rather than limiting reporting to traditional HR metrics. Build a strong reporting framework for people metrics and provide leadership with meaningful analysis of trends, potential risks and opportunities. Leverage data and technology to develop insights from skip-level discussions, employee feedback, attrition analysis, exit information and other employee listening mechanisms . Design and strengthen Early Warning Systems to proactively identify potential attrition and employee concerns using appropriate data, analytics and technology. Bring together multiple sources of people data to enable more informed and proactive workforce decisions. 3. AI, Digital & HR Process Automation Demonstrate a strong interest in AI solutions, digital transformation, data management and emerging technologies , particularly their application within HR. Continuously identify HR processes that can be simplified, digitized or automated and take ownership for converting those opportunities into practical solutions. Understand business and HR challenges and develop technology-enabled solutions to address them. Explore and implement appropriate use cases for tools such as Microsoft Copilot and Claude across HR activities, including employee insights, exit management, reporting, analysis and productivity improvement. Partner with relevant stakeholders to automate repetitive HR activities and improve process efficiency, accuracy and employee experience. Bring a digital-first and automation mindset to HR rather than relying solely on conventional manual HR processes. 4. AI Events, Hackathons & Innovation Culture Drive employee engagement initiatives relevant to an Analytics & AI workforce, including AI events, hackathons, innovation forums, knowledge-sharing sessions and capability-building events . Have an understanding of how to design and launch hackathons for Data Scientists and Analytics/AI talent , including developing themes, engaging relevant stakeholders, driving employee participation and showcasing innovative ideas. Manage and strengthen AI forums across Analytics business areas and create platforms that encourage experimentation, innovation, knowledge sharing and collaboration. Stay curious and informed about developments across the AI industry and Analytics ecosystem and use these insights to strengthen employee engagement and talent initiatives. Develop new engagement interventions that harness employees' passion for data, analytics, AI, innovation and emerging technologies . 5. AI Academy, Learning & Future Skills Develop a strong understanding of Digital, Data, Analytics and AI learning curricula , including the organization's AI skill repository and emerging capability areas. Partner with business and Learning & Development teams to support AI Academy and digital capability-building initiatives . Understand evolving skills across Analytics and AI and help identify learning priorities that support future business requirements. Promote continuous learning, certification, experimentation and application of new AI and digital capabilities across the workforce. 6. Advanced Analytics & Technology Skills Possess advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel , power point presentation including the ability to undertake complex data analysis and prepare management-level reports and dashboards. Should have working knowledge of Python and an understanding of how it can be applied to data analysis, HR analytics and process automation. Should have practical exposure to Microsoft Copilot and Claude , with the curiosity and capability to explore new AI tools and their application to HR. Demonstrate comfort working with structured datasets, HR dashboards, analytical outputs and visualization/reporting tools. Continuously explore new technology and automation opportunities that can strengthen HR effectiveness and decision-making. 7. Employee Engagement & Experience Build upon existing employee engagement initiatives and introduce interventions relevant to the Analytics & AI workforce. Create differentiated engagement opportunities for employees across Data Science, Analytics, Digital and AI disciplines . Use employee listening data and analytics to move from reactive engagement interventions toward targeted and proactive employee experience strategies. Ensure consistent communication of people initiatives to foster a positive, collaborative and engaged work environment. 8. Employee Relations, Grievance Management & Governance Manage, investigate and report employee relations cases and ensure fair, consistent and timely resolution in accordance with company policies, procedures and values. Work closely with Legal, Compliance and Ethics teams on employee grievances, sensitive matters and leadership escalations. Identify recurring employee-relations themes through data and recommend systemic interventions where required. Support the definition and refinement of HR policies and processes to appropriately balance employee and organizational requirements. Maintain appropriate confidentiality, governance and responsible use of employee data when deploying analytics, AI or automation solutions. 9. Compensation, Workforce Economics & Business Impact Develop a strong understanding of market compa-ratios, internal compa-ratios, salary grids and compensation benchmarks , particularly for Analytics, Data Science, Digital and AI roles. Partner with business leaders on people metrics across retention, diversity, CSR, talent and people financial metrics . Identify sustainable cost-efficiency opportunities while balancing employee experience, business needs and talent-market realities. Analyze employee costs and workforce trends and identify opportunities to improve productivity, workforce effectiveness and gross margin . Provide data-backed recommendations rather than relying only on transactional HR reporting. Desired Profile The ideal candidate should be a business-oriented, digitally curious and analytics-driven HR professional who: Understands the Analytics, Data, Digital and AI talent ecosystem . Has strong HR Business Partnering and stakeholder management capabilities. Is comfortable discussing business challenges with Analytics and AI leadership. Has hands-on experience with HR analytics, dashboards and people metrics . Has advanced Microsoft Excel, presentation capability and working knowledge of Python . Has experience or practical exposure to Microsoft Copilot, Claude and other AI-enabled productivity solutions . Has a strong interest in emerging AI solutions, technologies and industry developments . Understands the fundamentals of data management, digital transformation and AI capability development . Can identify opportunities for process automation and technology-led HR transformation and translate ideas into implementable solutions. Understands AI/digital learning ecosystems, AI Academies and skill repositories . Has experience in, or strong knowledge of, designing Data Science/AI hackathons, innovation forums and AI events . Demonstrates strong analytical thinking, problem-solving and executive communication skills. Can convert large amounts of people data into clear insights, recommendations and action plans for leadership . Combines employee centricity with a strong understanding of commercial and business outcomes . This is not a conventional HR Business Partner role. We are looking for an HR professional who is passionate about Analytics, Data and AI and wants to apply technology to solve real people and business challenges. The individual should combine strong HR fundamentals with data fluency, digital curiosity and an automation mindset, and be motivated to experiment with AI-enabled solutions to build the next generation of HR practices for an Analytics & AI workforce

Strategic Planning & Infrastructure Quality Achieve SLAs: Ensure network activities align with corporate target KPIs, including Time to Detect (TTD) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR). Optimize Budgets: Recommend budget allocations and capacity planning strategies to ensure a cost-effective infrastructure. Plan Disruptions: Partner with cross-functional IT groups to execute robust Disaster Recovery (DR) simulations. Refine Systems: Constantly research and implement state-of-the-art software monitoring tools. Required Qualifications & Skills Educational Background Degree: Bachelors Degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Network Engineering, or a related field. Work Experience: Minimum of 8-10 years of experience in a dedicated NOC environment, with at least 3-5 years in a supervisory or management capacity. Monitoring Platforms: Hand-on familiarity with Enterprise Monitoring Systems (e.g., SolarWinds, Manage Engine, Datadog, Splunk, BMC, or Nagios). Operating Systems: Practical knowledge working with Linux/Unix distributions and Windows Server architectures. Voice Protocols: Familiarity with voice and telecom services like SIP trunking, CAS, and PRI. Core Certifications (Preferred) ITSM/Process: ITIL v4 Foundation or Managing Professional certification. Networking: Cisco Certified Network Professional (CCNP) or Juniper Networks Certified Enterprise Routing and Switching Professional (JNCIP-ENT). Desired Behavioral Competencies Crisis Management: Exceptional situational awareness and calm under pressure during major high-severity outages. Effective Communication: Strong verbal and written skills to translate technical concepts into scannable briefs for senior leadership. Customer Focus: Intense dedication to customer satisfaction, maintaining transparent external and client communication during disruptions. NLP Model Development: - Develop and implement NLP models for various applications, including text classification, sentiment analysis, entity recognition, and language translation. - Utilize machine learning and deep learning techniques to extract valuable information from unstructured text. 2. Text Preprocessing: - Preprocess and clean large volumes of text data to prepare it for analysis. - Implement techniques such as tokenization, stemming, and lemmatization. 3. Feature Engineering: - Identify and engineer relevant features from text data to improve model performance. - Implement techniques to capture semantic relationships within the data. 4. Model Training and Evaluation: - Train, fine-tune, and validate NLP models using appropriate algorithms. - Evaluate model performance using metrics such as precision, recall, F1 score, and accuracy. 5. Data Analysis: - Conduct exploratory data analysis on textual datasets to uncover patterns, trends, and anomalies. - Use statistical methods to gain insights into the underlying structure of the data. 6. Collaboration with Cross-Functional Teams: - Work closely with data engineers, software developers, and domain experts to integrate NLP solutions into broader systems and applications. - Collaborate in defining project goals, requirements, and deliverables. 7. Algorithm Optimization: - Optimize and fine-tune NLP algorithms for improved efficiency and accuracy. - Implement parallel processing and distributed computing techniques for large-scale data analysis. 8. Stay Updated with NLP Trends: - Stay informed about the latest advancements and trends in NLP and machine learning. - Apply cutting-edge techniques to solve complex business problems. 9. Documentation: - Document methodologies, algorithms, and code for reproducibility and knowledge transfer. - Prepare clear and concise project reports and documentation. Experience range: 6-11 Yrs
Job Description As a GSI Solution Architect, you will be the technical and solution engine behind our Global Systems Integrator ecosystem, with a dedicated focus on Employee Experience and Freshservice. You will help GSI partners find, shape, and progress new business and expansion opportunities - bringing solution credibility to early conversations, turning employee service challenges into structured opportunities, and building the assets and capability that let partners eventually run these motions themselves. You will work day-to-day with two Business Development colleagues and our GSI Partner Managers, and partner closely with Sales, Solution Engineering, Product, and Professional Services. This is a commercially aligned role - you will be measured on partner-sourced ARR - but it is not a pure sales role. Solution leadership, partner enablement, and technical credibility are the core of the job. Key Responsibilities Work with GSI partners to identify and shape new Freshservice opportunities linked to employee service transformation. Support early-stage discovery with partner teams and end customers, translating service challenges into structured solution opportunities. Build solution narratives across ITSM modernisation, employee self-service, workflow automation, knowledge management, and legacy ITSM migration. Identify where existing EX or ITSM footprints can expand into broader Enterprise Service Management - HR, Finance, Facilities, Legal, Procurement, Security, and Operations. Position AI as a practical accelerator: self-service, ticket deflection, agent assist, knowledge discovery, and automation. Equip our two Business Development colleagues with messaging, discovery questions, and qualification guides, and join calls where solution credibility is needed. Deliver enablement sessions for GSI sales, consulting, architecture, and delivery teams, and support their certification and readiness. Create reusable assets - demo flows, reference architectures, discovery guides, and partner playbooks - that scale beyond any single deal. Support partner account planning and contribute to the quality and conversion of partner-sourced pipeline. Qualifications Required Experience in solution architecture, presales, consulting, or partner solution engineering. Strong understanding of Employee Experience, ITSM, ESM, service desk modernisation, and internal service delivery. Experience working with GSIs, systems integrators, consulting firms, or other partner-led business models. Ability to build EX, ESM, and AI solution narratives, and to support both new business and expansion motions. Understanding of AI use cases in service management - self-service, agent assist, automation, knowledge, and ticket deflection. Experience creating demos, discovery guides, enablement content, and reference architectures. Comfortable being commercially aligned to partner-sourced ARR. Strong stakeholder management across partner, sales, product, and technical teams, with excellent communication and presentation skills. Based in or able to work from Chennai. Preferred Experience with Freshservice, ServiceNow, Jira Service Management, BMC, Ivanti, ManageEngine, or similar ITSM/ESM platforms. Experience supporting partner-sourced or partner-influenced revenue motions, or GSI-led transformation programmes. Experience working with Indian or global GSI partners. Familiarity with ITIL, workflow automation, and internal service operations. Ability to build business cases, value propositions, and repeatable go-to-market plays. Experience supporting migrations from legacy ITSM platforms. Disclaimer: This job posting has been aggregated from external source. Role details, content, and availability are subject to change. Applicants are advised to confirm the latest information directly on the company website before applying.

jobs.title: Lead - Product Marketing
jobs.description:
Experience range: 7-9 Yrs
Job Description Freshworks is hiring a Lead Product Marketer to drive go-to-market strategies, positioning, and adoption across the Freshdesk portfolio. As customer service software rapidly evolves alongside advances in AI and modern CX capabilities, proactive automation, and shifting buyer expectations, staying ahead of market alternatives is critical. We re looking for a seasoned SaaS product marketer who can bridge product capabilities with business value, enjoys translating complex AI technology into clear messaging, and thrives working cross-functionally in a fast-moving SaaS environment. What youll do Develop crisp product positioning and value-driven messaging that differentiates Freshworks solutions in the customer service market. Frame technical capabilities into clear, compelling narratives tailored to buyer personas, CX leaders, and executives. Lead cross-functional product launches in close collaboration with Product Management, Sales, Marketing, and Enablement teams. Lead competitive intelligence across the CX landscape, tracking competitor feature launches, pricing, and GTM moves. Develop, scale, and maintain actionable competitive enablement assets, including battlecards, competitive matrices, demos, FAQs, displacement pitch decks, and win/loss analysis. Serve as an SME on direct sales calls, executive briefing centers, and competitive deal desks. Create high-impact sales tools, pitch decks, FAQs, demos, and collateral to equip GTM teams with targeted strategies for handling competitor objections, feature gaps, and displacement throughout the buyer journey. Partner with Product Management to feed real-time competitive gap insights back into the product roadmap. Partner with Demand Generation, Lifecycle Marketing teams, and other PMMs to inject product and competitive positioning into field campaigns, web, content, webinars, and any customer-facing collateral and campaigns. Integrate modern AI tools into daily marketing workflows to automate content creation, market research, competitive intelligence, and win/loss data analysis, thereby accelerating output and asset development. Stay current on emerging AI technologies and competitive offerings to help shape Freshworks AI narrative. Qualifications Any graduate degree (MBA preferred) with 7 to 9 years of prior experience in a similar position. Excellent English written, verbal, and presentation skills, with an eye for quality and attention to detail. An ability to understand AI, tech, and the customer service domain, including buyer behavior and ideal customer profiles, and translate tech content into marketing material Proven track record of planning and executing end-to-end marketing strategies, product launches, customer research, and messaging frameworks. Strong messaging and positioning skills, with the ability to simplify technical concepts for both business and technical audiences, complemented by a customer-first mindset supported by strong market research and storytelling abilities. Strong expertise in integrating AI into product marketing processes, with hands-on experience using modern AI tools to enhance marketing tasks, content creation, and research workflows. Strength in collaborating with cross-functional teams, across geographies, including executive management, product management, operations, sales, and marketing Disclaimer: This job posting has been aggregated from external source. jobs.title: Lead - Solution Engineer
jobs.description:
Experience range: 8-13 Yrs
Job Description Freshservice is expanding what AI-driven ITSM means for our customers - from Freddy AI Copilot and Freddy AI Agent, to Agent Studio for building custom agentic workflows, to MCP Gateway connecting Freshservice to the broader AI stack. Were creating a new kind of Solutions Engineering role to match: the Lead AI Solution Engineer. This is a specialist presales role for someone who can do three things at once: speak credibly to technical and business buyers about AI value, architect and demo AI solutions on top of Freshservice, and stay hands-on enough to help customers get those solutions live post-sale. Youll be the AI subject-matter expert embedded in SMB and Commercial deals, partnering with Account Executives, core SEs, Product, and Professional Services to win competitive deals and make sure the AI value we sell is the AI value customers actually realize. Youll report into the Solutions Engineering leadership team and act as a force multiplier for the broader SE org - enabling peers, building reusable AI demo assets, and representing the voice of the customer back to Product on where our AI roadmap needs to go next. What Youll Do Own the technical narrative for AI/Freddy across strategic and competitive deals - positioning Freddy AI Copilot, Freddy AI Agent, Agent Studio, and MCP Gateway against how prospects actually work today, not a generic AI pitch. Design and deliver tailored AI proofs-of-concept and demos: configuring agentic workflows, custom skills, and automations in Agent Studio, and connecting Freshservice to customer data and tools via MCP Gateway and APIs. Lead technical discovery specifically for AI use cases - ticket deflection, agent-assist, workflow automation, knowledge management - quantifying expected impact (deflection rate, resolution time, agent productivity) with the customer, not just for them. Lead internal projects that improve Solution Engineering efficiency and productivity, identifying repetitive processes and building AI driven workflows to simplify or automate them. Partner with Account Executives and core Solution Engineers as the AI overlay specialist on SMB, Commercial and competitive pursuits, joining deals at the point where AI differentiation matters most. Support deal-winning activities end to end: RFP/RFI responses, executive briefings, proof-of-value engagements, and security/architecture reviews for AI components (data handling, model governance, integration security). Bridge presales to delivery: work with Professional Services and Customer Success to help scope and de-risk the implementation of AI solutions sold, so what was demoed is what gets deployed. Build and maintain a library of reusable AI demo environments, reference architectures, and ROI/business-case models that the wider SE team can self-serve. Track competitive AI positioning versus ServiceNow (Now Assist), SysAid, Quest KACE, and other ITSM/ITAM players - including where competitors are genuinely ahead, so the teams positioning stays credible rather than one-sided. Represent customer and field feedback on AI features and gaps directly to Product and Engineering, influencing roadmap prioritization. Mentor and enable other SEs on AI positioning, demo technique, and objection handling as the internal go-to expert. Qualifications What Youll Bring 8+ years in Solutions Engineering, Sales Engineering, Solution Consulting, or Technical Presales, ideally within ITSM, ITOM, ITAM, or broader enterprise SaaS. Strong AI fundamentals. You deeply understand how LLMs and agents work in production: context engineering, memory, RAG, tool use, structured outputs, and the failure modes that actually show up at scale. Youve worked with agentic frameworks (LangGraph, LlamaIndex, Google ADK, or equivalent) and with both open and closed source models. Hands-on experience deploying or configuring AI/LLM-based solutions in a customer-facing context - this can be conversational AI/copilots, RAG-based knowledge assistants, or agentic workflow automation; deep AI/ML research experience is required. Hands on expectations around building internal agents and automations. For example, creating agents that can interact with multiple internal systems, collect and consolidate information from different sources, reason across that context, and provide actionable recommendations or trigger downstream workflows. A track record of selling and positioning AI or automation value to both business stakeholders (ROI, productivity, risk) and technical stakeholders (architecture, security, integration). Experience building production-grade machine learning deployments on AWS, Azure, or GCP Experience running competitive deals and building honest, differentiated positioning rather than one-size-fits-all pitches. Comfort operating across the full deal lifecycle - from discovery and demo through proof-of-value and into implementation handoff. Excellent executive presence and communication skills; able to flex a technical AI conversation up to a CIO/CX-leader audience or down to a hands-on admin audience in the same week. Freshservice, Freshdesk, or comparable ITSM/CX platform experience (ServiceNow, SysAid, Zendesk, Jira Service Management) is a strong plus. Nice to Have Prior experience with Freddy AI, Agent Studio, or Freshworks products specifically. Experience with ITAM/discovery tooling (e.g., Device42) and how it feeds AI-driven automation. Exposure to AI governance conversations (data residency, model risk, responsible AI) in regulated industries. A builders instinct - youd rather stand up a working demo than a slide. Disclaimer: This job posting and Location has been aggregated from external source. Role details, content, and availability are subject to change. Applicants are advised to confirm the latest information directly on the company website before applying.

jobs.title: Lead - Solution Engineer
jobs.description:
Experience range: 5-8 Yrs
Job Description We are looking for a passionate and technically skilled Solution Engineer to be part of our SMBC Sales Support team for Freshservice. You will be instrumental in solving complex customer problems, designing tailored solutions - including AI-driven use cases built on Freddy AI and Agent Studio - and delivering impactful demonstrations of the Freshworks platform. This role suits individuals with strong pre-sales experience who thrive on customer interaction, solutioning, and collaborating with internal teams to drive business outcomes, and who are genuinely curious about applying AI to real customer problems rather than just talking about it. Pre-Sales Engagement Customer Solutions: Engage with SMB, mid-market customers to understand their business and technical challenges. Conduct discovery sessions, architect solutions, and deliver tailored product demonstrations and Proofs of Concept (POCs). Address technical objections and ensure alignment with customer needs. AI Solutioning Positioning: Understand and clearly explain core AI/LLM concepts (prompting, agents, model context/tooling) to both technical and business audiences without over-selling or over-simplifying. Position Freddy AI Copilot, Freddy AI Agent, and Agent Studio within customer discovery, tying AI capabilities to concrete outcomes (ticket deflection, resolution time, agent productivity) rather than generic AI messaging. Build and configure simple AI agents and automated workflows in Agent Studio (or comparable agent-builder tools) to bring AI use cases to life in demos and POCs. Field technical AI questions on integration, data handling, and governance, looping in specialists for deeper architecture discussions when needed. Solution Design Documentation: Participate in gathering requirements and scoping complex engagements. Create technical documentation including solution proposals, SoWs, and RFP/RFI responses. Evaluate opportunities from a technical feasibility standpoint and proactively mitigate risks. Collaboration Execution: Collaborate closely with Sales, Product, Engineering, and Implementation teams. Align technical strategies with sales initiatives to accelerate deal closures. Continuously improve pre-sales tools, processes, and enablement assets. Customer Advocacy Product Evangelism: Articulate the value and capabilities of the Freshworks platform to both technical and business audiences. Represent Freshworks at customer meetings, events, and forums as a trusted technical advisor. Keep abreast of product developments and industry trends to provide relevant, up-to-date guidance. Qualifications 5-8 years of experience in pre-sales/solution engineering, technical consulting, or a similar customer-facing technical role. Strong background in SaaS, cloud technologies, APIs, and enterprise software environments. Proven experience designing and delivering technical demonstrations and POCs. Ability to work with mid-market and enterprise customers, understand their pain points, and craft effective solutions. Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and verbal. Bachelor s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience). Familiarity with ITSM products and market is a must. Solid conceptual understanding of AI/LLM technology - prompting, RAG, agentic workflows, and how AI features are typically integrated into SaaS products; hands-on experience configuring or building AI agents/copilots (e.g., Agent Studio, similar low-code agent builders, or LLM APIs) is strongly preferred. Ability to credibly position and sell AI value to both business and technical stakeholders, including addressing common AI concerns (accuracy, data privacy, change management). This is a Night Shift role only, prior North America Market experience is a must Key Skills: Pre-sales consulting technical storytelling Solution architecture demo delivery API, integrations, SaaS product understanding Discovery, qualification objection handling RFP/RFI response and technical documentation Stakeholder collaboration (Sales/Product/Engineering) Strong communication relationship-building AI/LLM concepts (prompting, RAG, agentic workflows) positioning Hands-on AI agent/copilot building (Agent Studio or equivalent) Disclaimer: This job posting has been aggregated from external source. Role details, content, and availability are subject to change. Applicants are advised to confirm the latest information directly on the company website before applying.

jobs.title: Solution Architect
jobs.description:
Experience range: 10-15 Yrs
Job Description Solution Architect (SA) role is a critical internally and externally-facing role within Freshworks Professional Services (FPS) which acts the senior technical SME heavily involved in Sales, Delivery and Expansion phases of the customer lifecycle. FPS SA is a trusted advisor internally and externally working with the highest level functional and technical resources within Freshworks and the customer organizations to translate business outcome requirements into scalable solutions. Your role and responsibilities: During the Sales cycle, FPS SA will work closely with the Freshworks Presales team to understand a prospects pain points and solutions discussed to address them, and then directly interacts with the prospects leadership and functional owners to devise the best implementation approach for the identified solutions in line with industry and FPS best practices. During the Delivery phase, FPS SA will be the key resource who translates the high-level solution provided during the sales cycle into detailed design information to meet the customer s objectives and also for the FPS technical resources to implement the final solution. In the Expansion phase, FPS SA will work with the customer to adjust or expand their deployed capabilities by adjusting their implemented solutions to the customer s updated needs and organizational changes. Some of the specific SA deliverables and activities are: Product Champion: Act as a product leader in the region, instilling confidence in prospects during the sales cycle, devising innovative solutions during implementation, assessing existing enterprise customer health for improvement suggestions, and providing valuable customer feedback to the product team. Solution Design: Collaborate with stakeholders to gather requirements and develop custom Freshworks product solutions in line with business goals and industry standards. Create architecture diagrams for proposed designs and deliver presentations. Technical Implementation: Configure, customize, and deploy Freshworks products, encompassing workflows, automation, integrations, and reporting. AI and Automation Solutioning: Identify opportunities for prospects and customers to leverage AI, automation, and agentic capabilities to achieve measurable business outcomes. Advise customers on the data readiness, governance, security, accuracy, adoption, and operational ownership required to successfully deploy and manage AI-enabled solutions. Process Optimization: Identify areas for enhancement, proposing efficient solutions to improve operational efficiency. Training and Support: Provide training to customers support agents, administrators, and relevant teams, ensuring the proficient use of Freshworks products during deployments. Issue Resolution: Liaise with the Product and Engineering teams to troubleshoot and resolve technical challenges and implementation issues related to Freshworks products. Integrations Design: Create and integrate Freshworks products with other systems and third-party applications to streamline 3rd-party integrations and facilitate data flow. Documentation: Develop and maintain comprehensive technical and architectural documentation, covering system configurations, integrations, and customizations. Stay Informed: Stay updated on industry trends, Freshworks product updates, and best practices to continually enhance the capabilities of the customer support ecosystem. What success in this role looks like: Success in this role means opportunities are accurately scoped, proposed solutions are technically feasible and supportable, delivery teams receive clear and actionable designs, architecture decisions are made quickly, risks are surfaced early, and customers have confidence in you and that the solution will meet their intended business outcomes. Qualifications 10+ years of professional experience in ITSM, ESM, ITOM, ITAM Strong technical background with custom script development and presales experience Ability to read complex situations with several competing constraints and identify solutions that benefit both the customers and Freshworks Excellent listening and presentation skills 5+ years working directly with Functional and organizational leaders internally and externally Proficient in handling ambiguity and objections Skilled in negotiation and objection handling Experience with guiding customers in organization change management (OCM) to improve technology adoption is highly desirable. Produce reproducible research assets, including well-engineered code, experiment documentation, datasets, and robot demonstrations. 3. End-to-End Physical AI Systems Integrate perception, state estimation, semantic understanding, task planning, motion planning, learning, control, and safety mechanisms into complete robotic systems. The job holder coordinates AI-related engineering activities, guides and coaches developers, promotes common AI engineering practices and remains hands-on in prototyping, scripting, integration and solution development. The MES Automation Manager retains accountability for AI/automation strategy, governance and value realization, while the Principal AI Engineer provides the technical leadership and engineering capability required to implement and scale AI within MES Development Team. Key Responsibilities: Design, develop, test and implement AI-enabled solutions, agents and automation capabilities supporting the MES Development Team. Work with the MES Automation Manager to translate the MES AI and automation strategy into prototypes, (Minimum Viable Product) MVPs and scalable production solutions. Lead the technical implementation and adoption of AI within the development team, coordinating AI engineering activities and coaching developers in AI-enabled ways of working. Develop reusable AI agents, services, integrations, (Application Programming Interfaces) APIs, automation components and AI-ready knowledge solutions applicable across MES development. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Responsibilities and Tasks Understand Business Problems and Define Intelligent Solutions Develop a strong understanding of Micron’s business priorities, operational processes, enterprise systems, and strategic objectives. Partner with product owners, domain experts, data scientists, engineers, and business stakeholders to translate complex business problems into scalable technical solutions. Convert functional and non-functional requirements into solution architectures, technical designs, data requirements, and executable delivery plans. Identify opportunities where advanced analytics, machine learning, Generative AI, intelligent automation, or agentic capabilities can deliver measurable business value. Communicate technical options, dependencies, risks, and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Architect Scalable and Intelligent Enterprise Solutions Design secure, reliable, maintainable, and scalable solutions that integrate enterprise data, cloud platforms, applications, services, and AI capabilities. Define end-to-end architecture covering data ingestion, transformation, storage, retrieval, processing, APIs, user experiences, model integration, and production operations. Select appropriate architectural patterns, cloud services, data platforms, models, frameworks, and integration approaches based on performance, security, operability, cost, and business fit. Design modular services, APIs, event-driven components, intelligent workflows, and reusable platform capabilities. Contribute to architecture and design reviews while establishing reusable engineering patterns, technical standards, and quality gates. Build Reliable Data and Knowledge Foundations Identify and integrate relevant structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data from enterprise systems, databases, APIs, files, events, and streaming sources. Design and develop scalable ingestion, transformation, orchestration, and processing workflows for varying data volumes and latency requirements. Implement suitable data models, storage structures, contracts, metadata, lineage, retention, archival, and deletion strategies. Establish and monitor data-quality objectives, including completeness, accuracy, consistency, freshness, traceability, and fitness for purpose. Prepare trusted datasets and knowledge sources for reporting, analytics, machine learning, and AI-enabled applications. Develop retrieval pipelines that include document ingestion, parsing, chunking, metadata enrichment, embeddings, indexing, vector search, relevance evaluation, grounding, and citation strategies. Develop Production-Ready Applications and Services Lead the end-to-end design, development, testing, deployment, enhancement, and support of cloud-native and AI-enabled applications. Develop secure, maintainable, and high-performing backend services, APIs, microservices, integration components, and intelligent workflows. Build responsive, accessible, and reusable user experiences using suitable modern application frameworks. Apply sound object-oriented design, domain-driven design, asynchronous processing, dependency injection, and distributed-system principles where appropriate. Integrate relational, non-relational, analytical, streaming, and vector data stores into enterprise applications. Modernize existing solutions and progressively evolve legacy systems toward modular, cloud-native, and AI-enabled architectures. Engineer AI-Enabled Capabilities Design and implement solutions using machine learning, Large Language Models, Generative AI, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, tool calling, copilots, and AI agents. Develop prompt orchestration, context-management, memory, reasoning, workflow, and multi-agent patterns appropriate to the business use case. Enable governed connectivity between intelligent agents, enterprise tools, APIs, applications, and data sources using Model Context Protocol or similar integration patterns. Establish systematic evaluation approaches for model quality, retrieval relevance, groundedness, response accuracy, latency, safety, and user experience. Implement safeguards to reduce hallucinations, unsupported responses, prompt injection, sensitive-data exposure, and unintended system actions. Design appropriate human-in-the-loop mechanisms, fallback behaviors, approval controls, and escalation paths for higher-risk scenarios. Evaluate models, frameworks, and emerging technologies through structured prototypes and recommend adoption based on measurable technical and business outcomes. Ensure Security, Responsible AI, and Governance Apply security-by-design and responsible AI principles throughout solution architecture, implementation, and operation. Implement appropriate authentication, authorization, role-based access controls, secrets management, encryption, network controls, and secure coding practices. Protect confidential and sensitive information through data classification, access restrictions, privacy controls, filtering, masking, and secure handling practices. Incorporate content safety, prompt-injection defenses, auditability, traceability, explainability, and human oversight based on the use case. Ensure that solutions comply with applicable enterprise architecture, security, privacy, data-governance, software-development, and AI-governance standards. Assess third-party libraries, models, dependencies, and services for security, licensing, operational, and supply-chain risks. Own Engineering Quality and Production Readiness Build automated unit, integration, system, regression, performance, security, and AI evaluation tests. Establish continuous integration and delivery pipelines with appropriate code-quality checks, automated validation, deployment controls, and rollback mechanisms. Implement logging, metrics, distributed tracing, alerting, health monitoring, and operational dashboards across solution components. Optimize solutions for reliability, scalability, availability, performance, latency, throughput, and cost. Participate in production support, incident response, troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, corrective actions, and continuous service improvement. Define and monitor service-level indicators, operational thresholds, capacity requirements, and production-readiness criteria. Create and maintain technical documentation, architecture decisions, data contracts, API specifications, support procedures, and operational runbooks. Provide Technical Leadership and Collaboration Lead technical discussions, architecture reviews, code reviews, design reviews, and engineering-quality assessments. Mentor associate and mid-level engineers through technical guidance, pairing, constructive feedback, and knowledge sharing. Promote reusable solutions, coding standards, automation, documentation, and engineering best practices across teams. Coordinate with globally distributed and cross-functional teams to manage dependencies, resolve technical challenges, and deliver incremental business value. Help teams make informed decisions by clearly articulating technical risks, alternatives, constraints, and long-term implications. Use AI-assisted engineering tools responsibly for analysis, coding, testing, documentation, and developer productivity while maintaining human review, accountability, and compliance. Experience working in global, cross-functional environments and collaborating with technical and business stakeholders. Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, written communication, verbal communication, and presentation skills. Ability to manage ambiguity, evaluate technical trade-offs, and independently drive complex engineering work to completion. Ability to travel as needed. Required Technical Expertise Advanced proficiency in at least one general-purpose programming language such as Python, C#, Java, or C++, including object-oriented design, asynchronous programming, error handling, testing, debugging, and performance optimization. Experience developing secure RESTful APIs, backend services, microservices, integration components, and distributed applications. Practical experience with a modern frontend framework such as Angular, React, or Blazor, along with HTML, CSS, TypeScript, or JavaScript. Hands-on experience integrating Large Language Models or machine-learning capabilities into production applications. Experience with prompt design, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, embeddings, vector search, tool or function calling, AI agents, evaluation methods, grounding, and production safeguards. Strong SQL skills and experience with relational databases such as Microsoft SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Oracle, or MySQL. jobs.title: Staff, AI Product Manager
jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own the Orchestration and Automation platform tower: the low and medium code platforms where GSK builds agents and automations, and the enablement model that lets thousands of non-engineers use them safely. The estate spans workflow and agent builders such as Power Platform, Copilot Studio and n8n, alongside the adjacent orchestration tooling that sits with them. You will own the roadmap and the governance model, and act as the platform consultant business teams come to when they need to turn demand into working automations. Why This Role Exists GSK runs various low and medium code platforms, and demand from business teams outpaces any central delivery team. This role exists to take consolidation decisions, and to build the self-enablement layer — guardrails, templates, training, support — that lets citizen developers build safely without engineering review on every change. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the Orchestration and Automation platform tower and its roadmap. Takes consolidation decisions across the low and medium code platform estate. Acts as the platform consultant for business teams building on the estate. Owns the governance model that defines what a citizen developer may build unsupervised. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities Platform Portfolio & Consolidation Map capability against actual usage across the whole low and medium code estate, and recommend what consolidates, what stays, and what retires. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible business cases that survive finance and senior business unit scrutiny — cycle time saved, manual effort removed, licence cost avoided, automations running in production. Develop deep automation pattern recognition so you can spot the workflows worth automating and the ones that should be fixed at source instead. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping Shape the platform roadmap. Maintain a living view of in-flight, queued, and de-prioritized platform work, with the rationale for each decision, and feed it into the broader AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make trade-off recommendations. When two business sponsors both want platform investment, define the success metrics, run the analysis, and recommend where effort goes. Protect engineering focus. Push back — with evidence — on opportunities that won’t move scalable outcomes. Engineering Partnership & Enablement Consult on platform fit and design. Advise business teams and delivery squads on which platform fits, how to structure the build, and what it takes to reach production. Translate ambiguous requests into crisp problem statements and success metrics. Shape engagements end-to-end. Define scope, success criteria, exit conditions, and scaling pathways before kick-off, then stay close as engineers execute. Surface re-use and platform leverage when a one-off solution should become a reusable capability. Design the human and agent split. Decide which tasks the pod’s AI agents and workers own, where engineers and business users stay in the loop, and how evaluation and oversight make that safe. Stakeholder Alignment & Communication Operate fluently with VP-level business and scientific leaders. Run conversations that turn fuzzy ambitions into concrete, fundable AI engagements. Build sponsor coalitions that secure data access, change-management commitment, and air cover for your engagements. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects AI work to patients, science, and enterprise outcomes. Measurement, Learning & Iteration Apply Enterprise AI’s value-realization framework to every engagement and platform in the tower, and improve it with what you learn. Run honest post-mortems and feed lessons back into how the tower selects platforms and prioritizes demand Required Skills: 16+ years of progressive experience in enterprise platform leadership, with a meaningful part of it spent owning a platform or platform estate end to end: roadmap, architecture direction, operations, and lifecycle. Demonstrated track record of taking a platform from fragmented or underused to well run: consolidation calls made, adoption grown, and the operating model that sustained it. Experience running a platform in a regulated enterprise, with working knowledge of at least one part of the pharma value chain and the data, decisions, and constraints inside it. Solid technical fluency in modern AI/ML, covering LLMs, agentic systems, AI agents and workers, data and evaluation patterns, sufficient to set architecture direction, challenge engineers, scope realistically, and avoid hype-driven choices. Experience leading engineers directly while also leading a far larger citizen developer community through influence, frameworks, and quality of thinking. A platform product heritage: roadmap shaping, lifecycle and version management, vendor and licensing ownership, service levels, and stakeholder alignment across a large and varied user base. Preferred skills : Deep, hands-on Microsoft Power Platform experience is mandatory: Power Apps, Power Automate and Dataverse at enterprise scale, including environment strategy, ALM, licensing, and the governance model around them. Has owned a low or medium code automation platform at enterprise scale and run a citizen developer or self-service programme covering thousands of users, with guardrails that held under pressure. Fluent with the wider low and medium code agent and workflow stacks that sit alongside Power Platform, such as Copilot Studio, n8n, and the equivalents from the major cloud vendors. Skills AI Platforms, Change Management, Data Analysis, Microsoft ALM, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Power Automate, Microsoft Power Platform, Roadmap Development, Statistical Analysis, User Needs Analysis Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. jobs.title: SDE II, EE Experiences, Everyday Essentials Experiences
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION Everyday Essentials (EE) is a $100B+ business and one of the fastest-growing categories at Amazon — the household staples, health and personal care, grocery, and beauty products hundreds of millions of customers reorder. We're reinventing how customers discover, buy, and get more value from them, and we're looking for Software Development Engineers who want to build that future. The EE Experiences organization builds the shopping experience for the products customers come back for most. Our charter is Progressive Discovery and Monetization: helping customers find better products for their needs, complete their baskets, and get more value on every essentials purchase — and giving the world's largest consumer brands new and effective ways to reach those customers and grow with Amazon. We build a durable, profitable business at the intersection of the two, on the surfaces customers use every day. This is a space where the hardest problems don't have off-the-shelf answers. We're not polishing a solved product — we're inventing experiences that don't exist yet, and the decisions we make now shape a business with room to grow for years. You'll have the freedom to propose new ideas, prototype them, and ship them worldwide. Your work moves from whiteboard to production in front of a very large customer base, with visibility all the way to senior leadership. We're an AI-first team, and that shows up in two ways. We use AI throughout how we build software, and we expect our engineers to keep learning and applying the latest tools to move faster and raise the quality bar. AI is also at the core of what we build — the intelligence that helps customers find the right product is a modeling and engineering problem we work on hand in hand with scientists. If you're curious about AI, learn quickly, and like using it to solve real customer problems while keeping a clear head about where it helps and where it doesn't, you'll fit right in. Key job responsibilities Design, build, and own software end to end — working backwards from the customer through design, code, testing, deployment, and operations. Take on ambiguous problems where the goal is clear but the path is not, bring clarity, and deliver simple solutions to hard problems. Partner closely with scientists, product managers, and designers to turn customer problems into products that ship worldwide. Use AI tools and modern engineering practices to build faster and at a higher bar of quality, and help the team level up how it uses them. Own operational excellence for what you build — monitor it, respond when issues arise, and keep improving the customer and partner experience. Raise the technical bar through code reviews, mentoring, and hiring for the best talent. A day in the life Most days start with the customer problem in front of you: how to help someone find a better everyday-essentials product, or fill their basket faster. You dig into data, sketch a design, and talk it through with product managers and scientists before writing any code. By the afternoon you might be prototyping an idea that didn't exist yesterday, reviewing a teammate's change, or debugging something in production. Because so much here is new, you won't just pick up tickets. You'll help decide what to build, push for the approach you believe in, and see your work reach customers in weeks, not quarters. About the team Our team owns how customers discover and buy the everyday essentials they rely on — and how the brands behind those products reach them. Our mission is to make restocking the things you need effortless, and to help customers find better options along the way. Day to day you'll work with fellow engineers and partner closely with product managers, designers, and scientists, who bring the customer and data insight that shapes what we build. We're a small, fast-moving group solving open-ended problems for hundreds of millions of shoppers — a place where you own problems end to end and your ideas reach customers fast. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of non-internship design or architecture (design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and existing systems experience Experience programming with at least one software programming language Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of full software development life cycle, including coding standards, code reviews, source control management, build processes, testing, and operations experience Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers.
