jobs.title: SDE, Alexa For Shopping
jobs.description: DESCRIPTION What if you could talk to your Amazon Store? With Alexa+ on Echo Show, customers can now do exactly that. The full Amazon store is live on Echo Show 15 and 21 — a new way to shop at home that combines voice as a natural way to express needs with the product details, reviews, and videos customers rely on to make confident decisions. This product started with an ambitious question and was built from scratch — no prior version to iterate on, no existing architecture to extend, no playbook to follow. The team pioneered novel challenges including rendering the full, always-current Amazon store natively on Echo Show in real time, building visual grounding from scratch so Alexa's responses stay anchored to what the customer sees on screen, and creating a conversational commerce paradigm that lets customers skip screens entirely with natural language. We are seeking a Software Development Engineer to help build the next chapter of this experience — scaling what we've built, expanding to new surfaces and marketplaces, and pushing the boundaries of agentic, multimodal shopping. As an early-career engineer on this team, you'll design and build meaningful components alongside experienced engineers, own your work through design, implementation, testing, and livesite, and grow quickly in a high-ownership environment. This is greenfield, 01 work at the intersection of Generative AI, multimodal experiences, and conversational commerce. You will have the freedom to experiment, learn, and invent on behalf of our customers, and you'll work for a strong leadership team that optimizes for your growth and pairs you with mentors who will guide your career. Key job responsibilities As a Software Development Engineer I on this team, you will: Design, build, test, and operate features that scale and extend the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices. Write high-quality, well-tested code and participate actively in code reviews, both giving and receiving thoughtful feedback. Contribute to systems that render the Amazon store in real time, keep it in sync, and support conversational, multimodal shopping flows. Help extend the experience to new surfaces and international marketplaces, working through ambiguity where there is no existing playbook. Own your components end-to-end through livesite operations — monitoring, on-call participation, and continuous improvement of reliability and performance. Collaborate with engineering, science, product, and design partners across Alexa Shopping, including teammates in Seattle across time zones. Contribute ideas to technical designs, ask good questions, and grow your scope and autonomy over time with support from senior engineers and mentors. A day in the life Here's what a typical day might look like. You'll spend meaningful time building — designing and implementing features that scale the Amazon Store experience on Echo Show and Fire devices, whether that's improving how the store renders in real time, sharpening visual grounding, or extending the experience to a new marketplace. You'll write code, review your teammates', and get thoughtful feedback on yours. Days blend focused coding with a short standup, design conversations where your ideas are genuinely wanted, and pairing with a senior engineer or mentor when you're working through something ambiguous. Because this is 01 work, you'll often be making decisions without a playbook — and that's the fun part. You'll partner closely with engineering, science, product, and design colleagues across Alexa Shopping, many of them in Seattle, so some collaboration spans time zones. Your internal stakeholders are the product, design, and partner engineering teams shaping the Alexa+ shopping experience; your end customers are shoppers at home talking to their Echo Show, expecting it to just work. The problems you'll tackle range from "how do we keep the store always in sync and fast on-device?" to "how do we make a conversational shopping flow feel effortless?" — meaty, customer-facing problems where what you build lands in people's living rooms. About the team We're the team that taught the Amazon Store to talk back. We took an idea that didn't have a blueprint and shipped it to customers' living rooms — and now we're just getting to the fun part: making it bigger, faster, and available to shoppers around the world. Our mission is simple to say and hard to do: make shopping on Alexa feel effortless and delightful, no matter where a customer is or which device they reach for. We sit right where voice, vision, and Generative AI meet retail at Amazon scale — which means the problems we solve genuinely haven't been solved before, and the person who cracks them is often the newest engineer with a fresh idea. Culture-wise, we're builders who like ambiguity and dislike bureaucracy. We ship, we learn, we tell stories over chai, and we celebrate the wins (and the instructive failures). We hire smart people and give them room to run — you'll own real problems from day one, with experienced engineers and mentors in your corner, not looking over your shoulder. We take the work seriously and ourselves a little less so. If you like the idea of building something customers can literally talk to, you'll fit right in. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS 3+ years of non-internship professional software development experience 2+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience Experience contributing to the architecture and design (architecture, design patterns, reliability and scaling) of new and current systems PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in computer science or equivalent 3+ years of designing and developing large-scale, multi-tiered, multi-threaded, embedded or distributed software applications, tools, systems, and services using: C#, C++, Java, or Perl experience Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. jobs.description: At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. CTI MD Tech@Lilly Associate Director, CTI - Development, Clinical Dev Management Level: M1 | Job Family: Information Technology About the Organization: CTI - Development owns the digital capability that patients, sites and study teams meet first: consent and data capture, patient engagement, and the systems that get a study designed, started and set up. The portfolio spans Trial Capabilities, Clinical Experience and patient engagement, and AI & Analytics. The organization is mid-transformation, modernizing platforms and scaling AI and agentic use cases while operating under strict GxP/GCP, data integrity and inspection-readiness requirements. Job Description: The Associate Director, CTI - Development, Clinical Dev, leads a team of engineering, product and delivery professionals and owns delivery, technical direction and capability growth across the Trial Capabilities, Clinical Experience and AI & Analytics domains. The role sits where clinical process meets engineering: close enough to the build to lead a design review and challenge an architecture, fluent enough in trial execution to shape how a study team actually works. It owns the demand relationship with clinical development business owners, directs the partner teams delivering a material share of the work, manages allocated budget and contractor capacity against plan, and is expected to set the agenda for AI and agentic adoption rather than wait for direction on it. Hands-on technical experience is expected and non-negotiable: a practitioner who has built and shipped software and integrations directly, and who stays current enough to pressure-test an architecture or a build versus buy call. The role is scoped at the upper end of the band and is expected to grow into responsibility for broader teams as the portfolio expands. Core Responsibilities : Delivery Ownership Own delivery execution across the portfolio (scope, schedule, quality, dependencies, release readiness, production health) for clinical experience and patient engagement products (eConsent, ePRO/eCOA, patient portals and apps) and study start-up capabilities (site activation, study build, CTMS/eTMF integration). Run the standing delivery cadence of operational reviews, backlog grooming, planning cycles (e.g., PI Planning) and release governance as a single portfolio-wide rhythm, and apply product-management rigor to prioritization, scoring business value, technical debt, effort and risk explicitly and agreeing success measures before work starts. Define and implement the portfolio metrics framework: release predictability, defect escape, production reliability, study build and site activation cycle time, and adoption by sites, study teams and patients. Instrument it where stakeholders can see it, not inside a backlog tool. Identify and solve organizational and operational problems and technical challenges across the portfolio, from resourcing conflicts and scope ambiguity to cross-team dependencies, escalating only what falls outside established guidelines and doing so with a recommendation. Technical Direction & Engineering Standards Set and defend the technical direction of the portfolio; review architecture and design, challenge weak decisions, and own standards for APIs, data contracts, interoperability (CDISC, HL7/FHIR) and reuse across clinical platforms. Own the architecture and design decisions for the portfolio's products, approve solution and integration designs, and run a design review cadence that catches problems before a release rather than after one. Raise the engineering bar on test automation, CI/CD, observability and the deliberate reduction of technical debt. Stay personally current: spend enough time in the code, the integrations and the production systems to judge an estimate, read a pull request and ask the questions only a practitioner asks. AI & Agentic Transformation Define and land a 12 to 24 month vision for AI and agentic capability in study start-up and clinical experience: protocol and document intelligence, automated study build, site and patient-facing assistants. Make the business case for it. Find the use cases, prove them quickly at low cost, and take the ones that work through validation into production use with the evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop design that requires. Build the team's AI fluency, make AI-assisted engineering the normal way of working, and partner with business owners to redesign clinical process rather than automate around it. Resource, Budget & Vendor Management Forecast resource needs across the portfolio and manage allocated budget and contractor capacity within approved guidelines, including allocation, ramp-up and release decisions. Own vendor and partner delivery: define scope, outcomes and acceptance criteria, hold suppliers to the same engineering, quality and GxP standards as internal teams, and manage performance on predictability and quality. Own SOW/MSA follow-ups, renewals and scope amendments, shape the sourcing mix for the portfolio, and protect institutional knowledge through documentation, code ownership and cross-training. Business Stakeholder Engagement Act as the technology partner for business owners and study teams: the person they call first, and the person who tells them when an idea will not work. Represent the portfolio externally with platform vendors, sites and industry forums, influencing partner roadmaps toward Lilly's needs. Run the demand relationship: capture and challenge incoming requests, agree priorities against capacity, and keep one honest view of the roadmap and what has been traded away. Contribute to the Clinical Dev business-area plan by translating the modernization roadmap into resourced delivery cycles. Translate clinical need into technical options, and constraint, risk and cost into language a business owner can act on, with no surprises at release. People Leadership Hold management responsibility for the team, including hiring, onboarding, goal-setting and performance appraisals; hire for the capability the portfolio needs next, such as AI engineering, product thinking and clinical domain depth. Coach and develop through specific feedback, honest check-ins and a development plan each person recognises as their own; serve as career advisor and partner with HR on growth plans. Grow engineering craft, not only careers: use design and code review as teaching moments, and build shared practice across internal pods and partner teams so good patterns spread. Build bench strength and succession, remove single points of failure, and lead through senior engineers, technical leads and partner pod leads as the portfolio grows, setting direction for work executed beyond direct line management. Quality, Compliance & Process Leadership Deliver in a GxP/GCP-regulated environment covering computer system validation, 21 CFR Part 11, data integrity, inspection and audit readiness; design for security and patient data privacy from the start; own incident response and the service levels agreed with study teams. Implement and refine a standard framework for backlog management, delivery governance and execution (Agile/Kanban, PI Planning), and own the portfolio-level leadership reporting cadence. Required Skills and Expertise : 10+ years of relevant experience in technology delivery, engineering leadership or product/platform management, including 4+ years of people-leadership experience managing technical teams. Deep, current, hands-on engineering background: able to build, review and troubleshoot services, APIs and integrations, not solely credentialed from past roles. Fluency in at least one modern programming language and SQL, with working command of cloud platforms and integration patterns. Proven experience taking AI, machine learning or agentic solutions beyond proof of concept into governed production use. Experience managing vendor and contractor relationships, including SOW/MSA administration within established commercial guidelines, and forecasting resource needs against an allocated budget. Demonstrated success owning a senior business relationship: shaping demand, negotiating priorities and capacity, and holding credibility through difficult delivery news. Demonstrated experience defining delivery or product metrics frameworks that stakeholders actually use. Demonstrated success building and retaining a technical team: hiring engineers, coaching through design review, and keeping critical talent. Experience operating in regulated (GxP) environments, including computer system validation and inspection-readiness practices, with fluency in Agile/Kanban delivery and tooling (Jira, Confluence, ServiceNow or equivalent). Strong communication skills, translating technical trade-offs into business, clinical and regulatory language. Preferred Skills: 4+ years supporting clinical development technology: study start-up, site activation, patient- or site-facing systems, or clinical data capture. Experience with Veeva Vault Clinical, Medidata or comparable clinical platforms, working knowledge of clinical data standards (CDISC CDASH/SDTM, HL7/FHIR), and exposure to decentralized or hybrid trial designs. Education & Experience: Bachelor's degree in computer science, engineering or a related field (Master's preferred); Agile or PMP certification a plus. Demonstrated ownership of delivery for a portfolio or platform, shaping technical direction from direct engineering experience. jobs.title: Assistant Vice President
jobs.description: Job Description: Key Responsibilities 1. Agentic Solution Architecture & Design Authority Lead discovery and solutioning with stakeholders; translate business objectives into target-state agentic AI architectures, blueprints, and roadmaps . Own end-to-end solution design : multi-agent orchestration, tool-using agents, human-in-the-loop patterns, memory and state management, RAG and knowledge layers, and enterprise integration. Drive build vs. buy vs. partner decisions for models, agent frameworks, and solution with EXL standards. 2. Architecture Standards, Governance & Responsible AI Define and enforce reference architectures, design standards, and reusable patterns for agentic AI solutions across accounts. Embed security, privacy, compliance, and responsible AI – including agent guardrails, evaluation frameworks, and auditability – into every design. Conduct architecture and design reviews , ensuring solutions are scalable, cost-efficient, and production-grade. 3. Technical Leadership Through Delivery Guide Forward Deployment Engineers, data scientists, and delivery teams from design through production – remaining hands-on at critical points (prototyping, integration, performance tuning). De-risk delivery by resolving complex technical blockers : legacy integration, agent reliability, model performance, and latency/cost/quality trade-offs. Ensure solutions move beyond POCs to enterprise-wide adoption and value realization . 4. Stakeholder Engagement & Advisory Act as trusted technical advisor to CIOs, CDOs and enterprise architects; lead architecture workshops, design authority boards, and executive briefings. Support pre-sales and strategic deals : solution shaping, effort estimation, technical proposals, and orals. Articulate architecture decisions in business terms – value, risk, cost, and time-to-market. 5. Capability Building & Reuse Convert engagement learnings into reusable assets, accelerators, and reference implementations for EXL’s agentic AI portfolio. Mentor architects and senior engineers; raise the architecture bar across the Enterprise AI practice. Continuously track and translate emerging AI advances (Agentic AI, LLMs, autonomous systems) into EXL-ready architecture strategies. Technical & Architecture Expertise (Agentic AI) Multi-agent system design : supervisor–worker hierarchies, planner–executor and reflection loops, blackboard and swarm patterns; task decomposition, delegation, and inter-agent communication protocols; deciding when a single-agent vs. multi-agent topology is architecturally justified. Agent state, memory & context engineering : short-term vs. episodic vs. semantic memory design, checkpointing and resumability, durable execution for long-running agents; context-window budgeting, compaction/summarization strategies, and retrieval-augmented context assembly. Framework and protocol depth : LangGraph (graph state machines, interrupts, human-in-the-loop nodes), CrewAI, AutoGen/Semantic Kernel; MCP (Model Context Protocol) for tool and resource federation and A2A for agent interoperability; sound judgment on custom orchestration vs. framework adoption. Model strategy & token economics : model portfolio design and routing (frontier LLMs vs. SLMs), structured outputs and function-calling schema design, constrained decoding; fine-tuning vs. RAG vs. prompt-optimization trade-offs; prompt caching, batching, distillation, and quantization to hit latency and cost SLOs. Retrieval & knowledge architecture : hybrid retrieval (sparse + dense), rerankers, GraphRAG and knowledge graphs; chunking and embedding strategy, freshness pipelines, and access-control-aware retrieval (document/row-level security) for regulated enterprises. Evaluation architecture : golden datasets, LLM-as-judge with calibration, trajectory-level agent evals, regression harnesses wired into CI/CD gates, and online canary/A-B evaluation for continuous quality assurance. Guardrails, safety & governance : prompt-injection and jailbreak defenses, PII detection/redaction, policy engines, sandboxed tool execution, human-approval gates for high-risk actions, and full audit trails/lineage for responsible AI and regulatory compliance. Production & platform architecture : model gateways, multi-tenancy, VPC/private endpoints, HA/DR, autoscaling, rate limiting, and circuit breakers; observability via distributed tracing (OpenTelemetry), token/cost telemetry, and drift monitoring at enterprise scale. Enterprise integration : event-driven and API-led integration patterns, identity propagation (OAuth/OIDC), secrets management, and integrating agents with CRM, contact center, workflow platforms, and legacy estates. Multimodal & emerging stacks : voice agents (streaming ASR/TTS – e.g., ElevenLabs), avatar/video (HeyGen), computer-use agents; fluency with AI-native tooling (Claude Code, Cursor) and evolving OpenAI/Anthropic platform capabilities. Responsibilities: Robust, scalable agentic architectures that move engagements from POC to enterprise-wide production adoption. Reference architectures, patterns, and accelerators reused across multiple accounts – reducing time-to-value and delivery risk. Tangible business outcomes (productivity, cost, quality, revenue) enabled by sound architecture decisions. Strong security, compliance, and responsible AI posture across all designed solutions. Recognized technical credibility with CTO/CIO organizations, contributing to account growth and strategic deal wins. Qualifications: 12+ years of experience in software/solution architecture, data, or digital transformation, with 3+ years architecting AI/LLM or agentic AI solutions . Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field. Proven track record of: Architecting and delivering production AI/GenAI solutions for large enterprise clients Serving as design authority across multiple concurrent engagements or programs Operating in business-facing, consulting, or forward-deployed environments with senior stakeholders Strong understanding of: Agentic AI and LLM architectures , RAG, evaluation, and guardrails Data platforms, cloud, security, and compliance Enterprise integration and legacy modernization Experience engaging with CTOs, CIOs, enterprise architects, and executive stakeholders . Willingness to travel and work onsite at business locations as required.

Primary responsibilities include developing features for existing and new platforms, leading integrations with new businesses, and ensuring that AML & Sanctions requirements meet regulatory obligations while supporting business enablement. An understanding of the payment industry and Visa’s Compliance program is required to develop requirements for building new features. The group supports multiple products and verticals across Visa, requiring strong collaboration, relationship-building, and partnership skills with engineering, operations, product, compliance, and other internal teams. This role requires interest in payment innovation, technology, and product management, attention to detail, and the ability to achieve results within a complex setting. Technical competence in database queries, supporting large-scale platforms, troubleshooting incidents, conducting data analysis, and participating in technical and functional solution development is necessary. The position also requires familiarity with current industry developments, strong organizational abilities, written and verbal communication skills, analytical thinking, structured problem-solving, and experience in customer or partner interaction, management, and software solution delivery. Responsibilities: Essential Skills - Product Vision & Strategy: Demonstrated ability to align and work towards a clear product vision and long-term roadmap that aligns with business goals. Proven experience in supporting the development and articulation of strategic plans with leaders for new product development initiatives, along with improvement, and innovation at scale. Cross-Functional Collaboration: Skilled at collaborating across multiple teams including engineering, operations, compliance, product, analytics, and business units to deliver value. The ability to collaborate and drive initiatives in a highly matrixed environment. Guide multi-functional teams through strategic and tactical decisions, recognizing dependencies, risks, and solutions. Agile Product Management: Well-versed in Agile methodologies (Scrum, Kanban, Lean, SAFe, Design Thinking), with hands-on experience managing backlogs (user stories, epics, features), facilitating sprint planning, and utilizing tools such as JIRA and JIRA Align. Technical Expertise: Strong technical background, including experience with planning API/service design and integration, SQL, and data querying (SQL Developer, Postgres SQL), and management of large-scale, data-driven platforms. Ability to engage in technical solutioning and brainstorming discussions with architects, engineers, and QA teams, ensuring robust and scalable solutions. Ability to translate business requirements into product features and ensure adherence throughout the product lifecycle. Demonstrates strong technical expertise and can turn capabilities into long term product strategies and vision for Technology Teams. Data Analysis & Problem Solving: Advanced skills in data analysis, process mapping, impact/gap/root cause analysis, and supporting stakeholders with complex data requests. Experience in extracting actionable insights from large datasets to finalize product decisions and drive enhancements. User Acceptance Testing: Conduct thorough UAT for client integrations and new features (frontend and backend/API) in pre- and post-production by defining objectives and scope, creating timelines, developing and executing test cases, validating results, tracking defects until resolved, and supporting stakeholders throughout the process. Wireframing & UX Design: Experience in creating detailed wireframes and mockups, collaborating with stakeholders to refine user experience and interface design. User and Client Centric Mindset: Enthusiastic about improving user experience, supporting product demos, gathering feedback, and ensuring that solutions meet user needs and compliance standards. Communication Skills: Exceptional written and verbal communication abilities, capable of presenting complex topics to diverse audiences, including leaders, partners, and technical stakeholders. Strong interpersonal skills for effective partner management and alignment at all organizational levels. Incident & Issue Management: Proficiency in rapid assessment and communication of application issues, incident reporting, and coordination with development and operations to resolve incidents and minimize impact. Prioritization & Time Management: Strong organizational abilities to prioritize critical tasks, manage multiple initiatives, and coordinate deliverables across global teams and different time zones. Monitoring & Analytics: Partnering with operations and analytics to develop platform health metrics, monitor performance, and drive data-driven decision making. Adaptability & Initiative: Proactive, self-driven, and solutions-oriented—capable of thriving in fast-paced, ambiguous, and evolving environments while driving progress and innovation. Continuous Learning: Commitment to staying current with industry trends, technology advancements, and best practices in product management, compliance, and payments. Qualifications: Education & Experience: 8 or more years of relevant work experience with a bachelor’s degree or at least 6 years of experience with an Advanced Degree (e.g., Masters, MBA, JD, MD) or a minimum of 2 years of work experience with a PhD. Experience with Compliance systems and strong analytical skills. Understanding of payment processing and Visa Net/payment ecosystem a plus. Preferred Skills: Candidates with experience in Compliance, Anti-Money Laundering (AML), Sanction Screening and end-to-end Case/Alert Management are preferred. Demonstrated experience with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning solutions is considered a significant asset, highlighting the ability to innovate and enhance business processes through advanced technologies. A strong understanding of ISO 8583 and ISO 20022 standards is highly desirable, reflecting proficiency in industry protocols necessary for secure and efficient financial messaging and transactions. Support Product leadership by skillfully conducting user demonstrations, providing clear insights into product capabilities while ensuring clients’ needs and feedback are effectively addressed. Prepare and help deliver comprehensive status reports to monitor progress across multiple concurrent workstreams, facilitating transparent communication and strategic decision-making.

jobs.title: Senior Principal - EUC / MDM Platform Architect
jobs.description: Business Introduction GSK remains committed to achieving bold commercial ambitions for the future. By 2031, we aim to deliver £40 billion in annual sales, leveraging our existing strong performance momentum to significantly increase our positive impact on the health of billions of patients globally. Our Ahead Together strategy is centred on early intervention to prevent and alter the course of disease, thereby protecting people and supporting healthcare systems. Our diverse portfolio consists of vaccines, specialty medicines, and general medicines. Through continuous innovation and a dedicated focus on scientific and technical excellence, we strive to develop and launch new, groundbreaking treatments that address critical health challenges. Job Purpose Be the definitive technical authority for how 50,000+ employees across [X] countries experience and interact with their devices. This role owns the architecture, reference designs, technical standards and engineering direction for the entire end user computing estate — laptops, desktops, mobiles, tablets, virtual desktops, meeting rooms, and specialised or regulated endpoints. Where the Director owns delivery, budget and people, the Principal Architect owns what good looks like technically and holds the organisation to it. This is a hands-on-capable role: the expectation is to prototype, prove and pressure-test designs personally, not solely to review other people's slides. The Principal Architect is accountable for ensuring the estate is secure by design, cloud-native, automatable, cost-efficient and — critically — genuinely pleasant to use. They are the person who says no to architecture that will not survive contact with 50,000 users, and who can explain why in terms both engineers and executives accept. Key Responsibilities Own the target-state architecture for end user computing: platform selection, device management topology, identity integration, application delivery, security control placement and telemetry. Produce and maintain reference architectures, design patterns, technical standards and architecture decision records (ADRs) — with trade-offs made explicit rather than buried. Define the technical roadmap that underpins the EUC strategy: platform migrations, deprecations, convergence of fragmented tooling, and the sequencing that makes it deliverable. Continuously evaluate the market — modern management, AI PCs and on-device inference, cloud PC/DaaS economics, zero-trust endpoint models — and separate genuine capability from vendor narrative. Act as the design authority for all endpoint change: chair or sit on the EUC architecture review board, approve significant designs, and hold veto on standards deviation. Set and police the exception process — make the right path the easy path, and make deviations visible, time-bound and owned. Review and assure supplier and MSP technical designs; ensure partners build to the organisation's architecture rather than their own delivery convenience. Set engineering standards for configuration-as-code, packaging, testing, release management and rollback across the endpoint estate. Prototype and prove new capability in a lab before it reaches production; build the reference implementation the engineering teams then industrialise. Mentor and technically develop senior engineers and platform leads; raise the ceiling of the whole team, not just your own output. Partner with Cyber Security to embed zero-trust principles at the endpoint: device trust and attestation, conditional access, least privilege, application control, EDR and DLP placement. Architect for regulated and validated environments — GxP-qualified endpoints, computer system validation (CSV/CSA), data residency and privacy obligations, and audit/SOX ITGC evidence generation as a designed-in property rather than a manual scramble. Own the technical response to endpoint-relevant threat scenarios and drive architectural remediation of systemic vulnerabilities. Architect the digital employee experience (DEX) telemetry model: what is measured, how it is collected, where it lands, and how it drives automated remediation. Design for self-healing and self-service by default; treat every recurring ticket category as an architectural defect until proven otherwise. Translate architecture into business consequence for senior stakeholders — cost, risk, productivity, time-to-value. Represent EUC architecture in enterprise architecture forums, security governance, and vendor executive briefings. Professional Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent demonstrable professional expertise. Relevant certifications desirable (e.g., Microsoft Certified: Endpoint Administrator Expert, Azure Solutions Architect Expert, Cybersecurity Architect Expert, Jamf Certified Expert, TOGAF, CISSP or SABSA). Area of Specialisation End user computing architecture at global enterprise scale — platform selection, device management topology, identity integration, application delivery and telemetry. Modern endpoint management (Intune/MECM) and macOS management (Jamf), including co-management, hybrid-to-cloud-native migration and staged ring-based rollout. Endpoint security architecture and zero-trust design — device trust, conditional access, application control, EDR/XDR, DLP and secure baselines. Regulated and validated endpoint environments — GxP-qualified endpoints, CSV/CSA, data residency and audit/SOX ITGC evidence generation designed in. Experience Required Overall 15 years and 12+ years in IT infrastructure or end user computing, including 5+ years in a principal, lead or enterprise architect capacity with recognised design authority. Architecture ownership for an endpoint estate of 20,000+ devices across multiple countries and regulatory jurisdictions. Expert-level, hands-on-derived command of modern endpoint management (Intune/MECM) and macOS management — sufficient to build the reference implementation personally, not only to specify it. Demonstrable advanced scripting and automation portfolio; evidence of configuration-as-code applied to a production endpoint estate. Working fluency in enterprise endpoint security and zero-trust architecture, with a track record of co-designing controls alongside a Cyber Security function. Led the architecture of at least one large-scale endpoint platform migration or transformation through to production, including the failures and what was learned from them. Able to produce architecture documentation of a standard that withstands external audit and supplier scrutiny. Proven credibility with both senior engineers and executive stakeholders, in English, in a global matrixed organisation. Willingness to travel internationally, approximately [5–15]% of the time. Desirable: Experience in a regulated industry — pharmaceutical, life sciences, biotech, financial services or healthcare — with practical GxP/CSV/CSA and Annex 11 / 21 CFR Part 11 exposure. Architecture for specialised endpoints: laboratory instrument workstations, manufacturing and shop-floor devices, clinical and field devices, kiosks, shared and multi-user workstations. Leading a major platform transformation: SCCM-to-Intune migration, Windows 10 11 at scale, MSP transition, or M&A integration/divestment of an endpoint estate. Sustainability-aware design — device longevity, power management, refurbishment and Scope 3 implications of architectural choices. Accessibility and assistive technology designed into the standard build rather than bolted on. Network fundamentals relevant to endpoints — SASE/ZTNA, split tunnelling, Wi-Fi 6/7, certificate-based network access. Contribution to the wider community — open-source tooling, conference speaking, published technical writing, vendor customer advisory boards. Skills/Background Deep technical breadth across Windows and macOS internals, modern endpoint management, identity, endpoint security, application delivery, virtual desktop / cloud PC, and mobile — with the judgement to know where tenant-wide standardisation matters and where a business exception is defensible. Advanced PowerShell and at least one general-purpose language (Python, C#, Go) applied to real automation, not toy scripts. Configuration-as-code and GitOps discipline — version-controlled endpoint configuration, CI/CD for policy and package deployment, automated testing and staged ring-based rollout as the default way endpoint change is delivered. API-first integration — Microsoft Graph, ServiceNow, MDM and security tool APIs; designing integrations that survive vendor change. Telemetry and data craft — designing measurement into the estate, with competence in the query languages and platforms the data lands in (KQL, Log Analytics, Power BI or equivalent). Architectural discipline — reference designs, ADRs, HLD/LLD, and the ability to write clearly enough that others can build from it and external auditors can accept it. Trade-off reasoning — cost, risk, experience, security and operability weighed explicitly; comfortable being the person who quantifies the uncomfortable option. Scale intuition — designing for 50,000 devices, unreliable networks, disconnected users, and the long tail of exceptions that always exists. Technical leadership without authority — landing decisions across engineering, security, service delivery and vendors by credibility and evidence. Executive communication — making architecture legible and decision-ready for non-technical leadership. Constructive challenge — able to disagree with a Director, a vendor or a security architect and keep the relationship intact. Skills Cloud Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, Design Thinking, Endpoint Encryption, Endpoint Security, End User Services, Financial Operations, Jamf Pro, Network Protocols, Network Security, Zero Trust Why GSK? Uniting science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology and talent to get ahead of disease together. We aim to positively impact the health of 2.5 billion people by the end of the decade, as a successful, growing company where people can thrive. We get ahead of disease by preventing and treating it with innovation in specialty medicines and vaccines. We focus on four therapeutic areas: respiratory, immunology and inflammation; oncology; HIV; and infectious diseases – to impact health at scale. People and patients around the world count on the medicines and vaccines we make, so we’re committed to creating an environment where our people can thrive and focus on what matters most. Our culture of being ambitious for patients, accountable for impact and doing the right thing is the foundation for how, together, we deliver for patients, shareholders and our people. jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer
jobs.description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Your role Bring your specialist knowledge and experience to a company managing 50% of the world’s MIPS and play a critical role in our modernization mission. You’ll be in good company among our global community of experts leading the future of mainframe modernization. Experts who share knowledge openly and collaborate freely. In this role, you’ll design, build and maintain the high-volume business logic that runs on the mainframe. At the same time you’ll play a key role in refactoring legacy code to enable modern cloud and mobile applications to seamlessly interact with the mainframe’s core data. What you will do Maintain Performance Prevent decay and find efficiencies: Monitor the architecture and identify opportunities to optimize code to maintain and enhance mainframe performance. Debug and Test Find and fix: Debug, troubleshoot, and analyze complex system interactions to keep mission-critical applications running. Develop for the Future Bridge the gap: As an instrumental player in modernization, you’ll extract business logic from legacy systems for migration or integration with cloud-based services. Your Future at Kyndryl The career path ahead is full of exciting opportunities to grow and advance within the job family. With dedication and hard work, you can climb the ladder to higher bands, achieving coveted positions such as Principal Engineer or Vice President of Software. These roles not only offer the chance to inspire and innovate, but also bring with them a sense of pride and accomplishment for having reached the pinnacle of your career in the software industry. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required skills and experience 8+ years of experience working as a software engineer on complex software projects. Excellent coding skills and solid development experience (Java, Python, .Net etc.) with debugging and problem-solving skills. Software development methodologies, with demonstrated experience developing scalable and robust software. Experienced in relational and NoSQL databases, data mapping, XML/JSON, REST-based web services. Knowledge of architecture design - Microservices architecture, containers (Docker & k8s), messaging queues. Deep understanding of OOP and design patterns. Preferred skills and experience Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, related technical field, or equivalent practical experience. Certification in one or more of the hyperscalers (Azure, AWS, and Google GCP) - otherwise, you can obtain certifications with Kyndryl. Experience with DevOps tools and modern engineering practices. Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers. This dedication to welcoming everyone into our company means that Kyndryl gives you the ability to thrive and contribute to our culture of empathy and shared success. That’s The Kyndryl Way. What You Can Expect Your career with us isn’t just a job—it’s an adventure with purpose. We offer a dynamic, hybrid-friendly culture that supports your well-being and empowers you to grow. Our Be Well programs are thoughtfully designed to support your financial, mental, physical, and social health—because we know that when you feel your best, you do your best. From your very first day, you’ll dive into impactful work that powers the systems our customers rely on every day. You won’t just contribute—you’ll make a difference, tackling meaningful projects that sharpen your skills and fuel your growth. We’re here to champion your journey. With powerful tools to chart your career path, personalized development goals aligned with your ambitions, and continuous feedback to keep you inspired and on track, you’ll have everything you need to thrive and evolve. You’ll develop in-demand skills to grow your career and achieve your ambitions with access to cutting-edge learning opportunities—from certifications with Microsoft, Google, and Amazon to coaching and hands-on experiences. And through it all, you’ll be part of a culture that values empathy, restless learning, and a devotion to shared success. We want you to thrive here—and we’re committed to helping you do just that. Ready to make an impact? Join us and help shape what’s next. Get Referred! If you know someone that works at Kyndryl, when asked ‘How Did You Hear About Us’ during the application process, select ‘Employee Referral’ and enter your contact's Kyndryl email address.

jobs.description: About the Role: GSK’s Enterprise AI team, a highly skilled applied AI group, translates the promise of AI into measurable impact across every major group at GSK — R&D, Medical, Commercial, Supply Chain, HR, Legal, Finance, and beyond. Bionic pods — AI product managers, forward deployed engineers, full-stack engineers, data engineers, and AI agents and workers — embed directly with scientific and business teams to build AI products that change outcomes. We are hiring a Staff, AI Product Manager to own Emerging Tech and AI Tooling, the front edge of GSK’s AI platform estate. You will run structured evaluation of new AI tools and platforms, decide what graduates into a standing tower and what gets retired, and own the AI developer tooling GSK engineers use every day. It suits someone who can hold an evaluation to a decision date and retire tools the organisation is attached to. You will lead a small engineering squad and set direction a far larger estate inherits. Why This Role Exists : Every week brings a new AI tool and a stakeholder who wants it. Without a disciplined front door, evaluations never close and nothing is ever retired. This role runs that front door, and owns the developer tooling estate so the tools engineers depend on daily have a named owner rather than a shared inbox. In this role you will be the person who: Owns the evaluation portfolio for new AI tools and platforms across Enterprise AI. Decides what graduates into a standing platform tower, what holds, and what gets retired. Owns the AI developer tooling estate end to end. Hands graduated platforms over with a working operating model. How This Differs from Traditional Product Management: This is not a traditional enterprise product role managing a source system’s roadmap, releases, and backlog. As an AI Product Manager in Enterprise AI, you: Build new AI products from ambiguous, unsolved business problems. Work with probabilistic systems, defining evaluations, acceptable error, and human oversight. Help lead a bionic pod, deciding which work goes to engineers and which to AI agents and workers, and how they hand off. Prototype hands on and are measured on business outcomes. Key Responsibilities: Evaluation & Graduation: Run every evaluation to a decision. Set the hypothesis, the success bar, the comparison set, and the kill date up front. Keep a live view of what is in flight, on hold, or retired. Quantify value rigorously. Build credible adoption and retirement cases that survive finance and architecture scrutiny — engineering hours saved, licence cost avoided, capability gained, duplication removed. Tell new capability from repackaging so overlap with what GSK already runs is caught before it becomes duplicate spend. Strategic Prioritization & Portfolio Shaping: Shape the emerging tech portfolio. Keep a living view of in-flight, queued, and retired evaluations with the rationale for each call, and feed it into the AI Platforms & Tools portfolio. Make the graduate, retire, or hold call. Decide which tower receives a graduating platform, and hold the decision date when the organisation would rather extend it. Protect the estate from sprawl. Say no, with evidence, to tools that look attractive but do not change what the organisation can actually do. Engineering Partnership & Enablement: Lead the Emerging Tech and AI Tooling squad. Run conversations that turn vendor enthusiasm into a testable hypothesis with a decision date. Build sponsor coalitions that secure evaluation funding, pilot cohorts, and the air cover to retire tools people are attached to. Communicate impact clearly in language that connects tooling investment to engineering throughput and enterprise outcomes. jobs.title: Senior Technical Architect
jobs.description: Job Summary Job Description — AI/ML Engineer (Codibix Assistant) Location: Chennai Experience level: Senior — 8–12+ years Summary Owns the conversational Assistant end-to-end — a standalone Python/Node service, deliberately separate from the Java/Spring Boot core, that authors and validates knowledge-repository entries through a multi-agent architecture. This is the one genuinely novel, non-boilerplate part of the platform: not a CRUD app Claude can generate wholesale, but a governed agent system where every AI-drafted output must stay clearly distinguishable from human-authored content until a Reviewer approves it. Key Responsibilities Design and build the multi-agent architecture: Orchestrator/Router, Retrieval/Grounding (RAG), Authoring, Validation/Schema, and Explainer/Audit agents — each with a narrow, explicit job, not one do-everything LLM call Enforce the core guardrail in code, not just in the prompt: the Authoring agent drafts only, never auto-publishes — every AI-suggested entry must render visibly distinct from human-authored ones Build the tool-calling contract per agent (e.g., Authoring agent can call draft_entry() but never publish_entry()) — RBAC boundaries enforced at the tool layer, not hoped for in the system prompt Own the retrieval layer: embedding strategy, chunking, and query design against the shared PostgreSQL/pgvector store so drafts don't duplicate or contradict existing repository content Build and maintain the model-agnostic integration layer — the abstraction that makes "swap the underlying model, keep the same agent behavior" actually true in code, not just a slide claim Own the REST/gRPC API contract this service exposes to the Java core (owned jointly with the Solution Architect, who owns the consuming side of that same contract) Define and monitor agent-quality metrics — hallucination rate on drafted entries, retrieval relevance, false-approval risk on the Validation agent Partner with Domain Architects to validate that agent-drafted entries actually reflect real domain judgment, not plausible-sounding text Skill Requirements 5–8 years in ML/AI engineering, with direct experience building production LLM-based agent systems, not just prototype chatbots Hands-on experience with an agent orchestration framework (e.g., LangGraph, LangChain, or equivalent) and a clear point of view on why a graph/state-machine approach beats a single unstructured agent loop for governed use cases Strong Python or Node.js (matches whichever the Assistant service is ultimately built in) Experience with retrieval-augmented generation: embeddings, vector search (pgvector or equivalent), chunking strategy trade-offs Demonstrated ability to design guardrails that are structurally enforced, not prompt-only — this is the single most important skill for this role, given the platform's audit-trail requirements Comfortable owning a service boundary/API contract with a team building in a different language (Java) — this role does not need Java fluency, but does need to design a contract a Java consumer can integrate against cleanly Experience evaluating LLM output quality in production (not just offline benchmarks) — hallucination detection, relevance scoring, human-feedback loop design Must Have Skill Python,Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG),Vector Databases,Generative Artificial Intelligence,Machine Learning,Agentic AI Good to Have Skill Other Requirements Preferred Prior experience in a regulated or compliance-sensitive domain where AI output requires traceability back to source Familiarity with Spring AI or LangChain4j (useful context for the API contract, even though this role doesn't build in Java) Experience building a correction/feedback loop that feeds structured signal back into a knowledge base, not just a thumbs-up/down Success Metrics Draft-to-approval rate (how often Reviewers accept vs. reject/heavily edit AI-drafted entries) — the most direct signal of whether the Assistant is actually helping Retrieval relevance (drafts genuinely grounded in existing repository content, not duplicated or contradicted)

jobs.description: Job Summary AWS Cloud Engineer / Cloud Developer We are seeking a highly skilled and passionate AWS Native Application Developer to join our growing engineering team. In this role, you will be responsible for designing, coding, and implementing cloud-native applications utilizing AWS serverless and native service architectures. Unlike traditional cloud infrastructure or DevOps roles, your primary focus will be on writing application code, building APIs, crafting business logic, and orchestrating serverless workflows. You will work closely with our product and design teams to translate business requirements into highly scalable, secure, and resilient application code running directly on AWS native services. What This Role Is (and Is Not) This IS a Software Engineering Role: You will spend the majority of your time writing application code (Node.js, Python, or Go), designing data schemas, writing Lambda functions, and building APIs. This IS NOT an Infrastructure / DevOps Role: You will not be responsible for provisioning VPCs, configuring routing tables, maintaining Kubernetes/EKS clusters, or managing firewalls. We have a dedicated Cloud Infrastructure team that handles platform-level operations. Your focus is purely on the software application layer. Key Responsibilities Application Development: Design and develop robust application backends, microservices, and event-driven architecture utilizing AWS native services. Serverless Engineering: Build and maintain scalable APIs using AWS Lambda, Amazon API Gateway, and AWS AppSync (GraphQL). Workflow Orchestration: Design complex business workflows and state machines using AWS Step Functions. Database Integration: Write application code interacting with NoSQL databases like Amazon DynamoDB (including single-table design concepts) and relational engines like Amazon Aurora Serverless. Messaging & Event-Driven Flows: Implement asynchronous communication using Amazon SQS, Amazon SNS, and Amazon EventBridge. Identity & Security: Integrate application-level authentication and authorization workflows utilizing Amazon Cognito and AWS IAM service roles. Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for Developers: Write and maintain developer-focused IaC templates using AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) or AWS SAM (Serverless Application Model) to deploy your application resources. Performance Tuning: Optimize application performance, cold-start times, and database query patterns to ensure low-latency responses and cost-efficiency. Testing & CI/CD: Write unit and integration tests for serverless components and collaborate with the DevOps team to integrate application builds into CI/CD pipelines. Skill Requirements Required Technical Skills & Experience Programming Proficiency: Strong software development background with deep production experience in at least one modern programming language (e.g., Python, Node.js/TypeScript, or Go). AWS SDK Expertise: Proven experience utilizing the AWS SDK to write applications that programmatically interact with AWS services. Serverless Development: Minimum of 5+ years of experience building, deploying, and debugging serverless applications using AWS Lambda. Database Skills: Deep understanding of NoSQL database design principles, specifically Amazon DynamoDB (data modeling, indexes, partition keys, and query optimization). API Development: Strong experience designing and implementing RESTful APIs or GraphQL endpoints. Asynchronous Design: Practical knowledge of building event-driven architectures and message queuing patterns. Developer Tooling: Experience using developer tools such as AWS SAM, Serverless Framework, or AWS CDK. Preferred Qualifications AWS Certification: AWS Certified Developer – Associate or AWS Certified DevOps Engineer – Professional. Front-End Familiarity: Basic understanding of integrating cloud backends with modern frontend frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, or Vue). Performance Monitoring: Experience with AWS X-Ray, CloudWatch Logs, or third-party monitoring tools to trace and optimize distributed transactions. Must Have Skill Amazon Web Services (AWS) Good to Have Skill Other Requirements Soft Skills & Working Style Product-Minded Developer: Ability to think about the end-user experience and align technical application choices with product goals. Collaborative: Comfortable working alongside dedicated UI/UX designers, product managers, and cloud infrastructure engineers. Self-Starter: Passionate about learning new cloud design patterns and staying up to date with the latest AWS native feature releases.

jobs.title: SDET Senior Test Lead
jobs.description: Job Summary We are looking for an experienced QA Engineer with a strong background in both functional and automated testing, and a working understanding of AI and machine learning concepts. This role is central to ensuring the quality, reliability, and trustworthiness of enterprise-grade AI solutions — spanning traditional ML models, Generative AI applications, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and the data pipelines that power them. This is not a generic QA role. The ideal candidate understands how AI systems behave differently from traditional software — where outputs are probabilistic rather than deterministic, where correctness is contextual, and where testing strategies must account for model drift, hallucination, retrieval quality, and data integrity. You will work alongside AI Engineers, data engineers, and architects to define test strategies, build validation frameworks, and deliver clear, actionable quality reports to technical and non-technical stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Functional Testing • Design, execute, and maintain comprehensive test plans and test cases for AI/ML solutions, Generative AI applications, RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and supporting REST APIs. • Validate end-to-end functional behaviour of AI and its integrated solutions against defined acceptance criteria and business requirements. • Test ML model outputs for correctness, consistency, and alignment with expected behaviour — including classification results, predictions, anomaly flags, and recommendations. • Evaluate RAG pipeline quality: validate retrieval relevance, chunking effectiveness, reranking behaviour, hybrid search results, and the accuracy of LLM-generated responses against source documents. • Test agentic AI workflows for correct tool/function invocation, reasoning logic, multi-step task completion, and appropriate handling of edge cases and failures. • Conduct API testing to validate request/response behaviour, error handling, authentication, input validation, and performance under load. Official Use Only • Perform data pipeline testing: validate data ingestion, transformation, cleansing, and output quality across batch and streaming workflows. • Execute regression testing following model updates, pipeline changes, or infrastructure modifications. • Test non-functional requirements including latency, throughput, scalability, and resilience. • Conduct exploratory testing to surface unexpected or emergent behaviours in AI systems — particularly in agentic and LLM-based solutions. Test Automation • Design and implement automated test frameworks and suites for AI solutions, APIs, and data pipelines. • Build reusable, maintainable automation scripts in Python, integrating with testing frameworks such as pytest, Robot Framework, or equivalent. • Develop automated regression suites that can be integrated into CI/CD pipelines to enable continuous quality validation. • Implement automated evaluation pipelines for Generative AI outputs — including LLM-as-judge scoring, semantic similarity checks, factual grounding validation, and response consistency testing. • Automate data quality checks within Databricks or equivalent pipeline environments to validate schema, completeness, referential integrity, and statistical distributions. • Integrate test automation with monitoring and alerting tools to detect quality degradation in deployed AI solutions. AI-Specific Validation • Evaluate LLM outputs for hallucination, factual accuracy, relevance, coherence, and adherence to safety and content guidelines. • Validate embedding quality, vector search precision/recall, and metadata filtering behaviour in RAG architectures. • Test model fairness, consistency, and robustness across diverse inputs, including adversarial and edge-case scenarios. • Validate that responsible AI principles — including content safety filters, guardrails, and bias mitigations — are functioning as designed. Official Use Only • Support model drift monitoring by defining baseline benchmarks and alerting thresholds for deployed ML models. Reporting & Stakeholder Communication • Produce clear, well-structured test reports summarizing test coverage, results, defect trends, quality risks, and recommendations — tailored for both technical and non-technical audiences. • Maintain dashboards and metrics that provide ongoing visibility into solution quality, test execution progress, and open defects. • Document defects clearly, with reproducible steps, expected vs. actual behavior, severity assessment, and supporting evidence (logs, screenshots, sample data). Skill Requirements Functional Testing Proven experience in functional, integration, regression, and exploratory testing of complex software systems. Strong ability to analyse requirements, design test strategies, and write high-quality test cases with clear pass/fail criteria. Experience testing REST APIs using tools such as Postman, REST Assured, or equivalent. Familiarity with testing data-intensive applications, including validation of pipeline outputs and structured/unstructured data quality. Experience working in Agile/Scrum delivery environments, including sprint-based test planning and execution. Test Automation Hands-on experience building and maintaining automated test suites using Python-based frameworks (pytest preferred). Official Use Only Experience integrating test automation into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, or equivalent). Ability to write clean, maintainable automation code following good software engineering practices. Experience with API test automation and data validation automation. AI & Domain Knowledge Working knowledge of AI and ML concepts: understanding of how models are trained, evaluated, and deployed — and the implications for testing strategies. Familiarity with Generative AI concepts: LLMs, RAG pipelines, embeddings, vector search, chunking, reranking, and agentic workflows. Ability to evaluate LLM output quality, including identifying hallucinations, factual errors, relevance gaps, and unsafe content. Understanding of AI non-determinism and how to design testing approaches that account for probabilistic outputs (e.g., semantic equivalence checks rather than exact string matching). Awareness of responsible AI principles: content safety, bias, fairness, and transparency. Reporting & Communication Strong written communication skills, with the ability to produce clear, professional test reports and defect documentation. Ability to distil technical quality findings into concise summaries suitable for non-technical stakeholders. Experience maintaining test metrics and quality dashboards — using tools such as Azure DevOps, Jira, Confluence, or equivalent. Comfortable presenting quality status and risks in team meetings and sprint ceremonies. Tools & Platform Familiarity Familiarity with Azure cloud services relevant to AI solutions: Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, Azure Databricks, and ADLS — sufficient to understand system architecture and design targeted test scenarios. Experience with version control (Git) and collaborative development workflows. Familiarity with logging and observability tools (e.g., Azure Application Insights) to support defect investigation and root cause analysis. Must Have Skill API Testing,Selenium,Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) Good to Have Skill Other Requirements Nice to Have Hands-on experience with LLM evaluation frameworks such as RAGAS, DeepEval, or LLM-as-judge implementations. Experience with performance/load testing tools (e.g., Locust, k6, or Azure Load Testing). Exposure to Databricks notebooks or PySpark for data pipeline validation. Experience testing ML model fairness and bias using tools such as Fairlearn or equivalent. ISTQB certification or equivalent formal QA qualification. Experience in a data engineering or AI engineering adjacent role — providing deeper empathy for the systems being tested.

jobs.title: Senior Data Science Specialist
jobs.description: Job Summary We are a team of nerds dedicated to collect other nerds that happen to be the best in their respective fields in the broadly understood IT service and analytics. Together, we create IT and Analytical Hubs that bring together the best experts from the IT world to help our partners become truly data-driven entities. Currently, we are looking for a Data Scientist as we support our partner in developing a Global Analytics Unit —a global, centralized team with the ambition to strengthen data-driven decision-making and the development of smart data products for day-to-day operations. The team is designed to foster a data-driven entrepreneurial culture by acting as an incubator to turn ideas into action: creating smart data products across various business domains like sales, marketing, purchasing, logistics, and beyond. The team has the autonomy to shape their approach, especially in terms of tools, technology, and introducing new concepts and solutions. Data Scientist We are searching for a Data Scientist to join our team of top-tier specialists, responsible for applying their expertise in machine learning , data mining , and information retrieval to design, prototype, and build next-generation analytics engines and services. If you want to: Take part in developing and implementing complex smart data solutions. Work on bleeding-edge projects with a chance to see your visions come to life. Collaborate with world-class IT professionals. Work on projects addressing real business challenges in a global and diverse team. Have real impact on the projects and environment you work in. Propose innovative solutions and initiatives. Moreover, if you like: Flexible working hours and a casual, non-corporate environment. Access to benefits such as Multisport, private medical care, and a modern office in the center of Warsaw with good transport links. Remote work options as much as you prefer. A relaxed atmosphere at work where your passion and commitment are appreciated. Vast opportunities for self-development through online courses, certifications, and global knowledge-sharing. Key Responsibilities Your Responsibilities: Understanding business problems and designing smart data products. Developing complex models and algorithms to drive innovation within the organization. Conducting advanced statistical analysis to provide actionable insights, identify trends, and measure performance. Collaborating with data engineers to implement and deploy scalable solutions. Working closely with business teams to clarify ambiguous projects into concrete requirements. Designing and implementing time-series forecasting, anomaly detection, and demand-sensing solutions for business domains such as sales, marketing, pricing, supply chain, and logistics. Partnering with software and full-stack engineering teams to expose models through APIs, dashboards, and scalable user-facing applications that support day-to-day business decisions. Skill Requirements We Expect: MS or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Mathematics, Artificial Intelligence, Physics, or a related technical discipline. At least 5 years of experience in a statistical and/or data science role. Expertise in Python (experience with languages like R, MATLAB, Scala is a plus). 2+ years of hands-on Python ML Production experience (not just POC), with proficiency in deploying models to real-world systems. 3+ years of professional experience as a Data Scientist , with a focus on applying machine learning models to business problems. Strong software engineering skills, including unit testing , object-oriented programming , and familiarity with best practices like PEP8 and tools like Black . Familiarity with Azure Machine Learning (1+ year of experience) and building cloud-based ML solutions. Experience in Bayesian modeling (1+ year) and the application of probabilistic models. Fluency in the NumFOCUS stack : pandas, scikit-learn, Matplotlib, and SciPy. Experience working with large datasets using tools like Spark and RDBMs. Experience with version control systems (e.g., Git) and knowledge of DevOps tools (Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD pipelines). Proven ability to deploy models to production and plan products, considering the broader technical landscape. Professional attitude and service orientation. Team player with the ability to work autonomously on complex projects. Fluent English, as you will communicate primarily in English. Hands-on experience with time-series algorithms and forecasting methods such as ARIMA, SARIMA, SARIMAX, Exponential Smoothing, Prophet, VAR, and state-space models, along with modern machine learning and deep learning approaches such as XGBoost, LightGBM, LSTM, GRU, and Transformer-based forecasting. Strong understanding of time-series feature engineering, trend and seasonality decomposition, lag-based modeling, anomaly detection, model backtesting, and forecast evaluation using metrics such as MAE, RMSE, MAPE, sMAPE, and WAPE. Good full-stack engineering experience, including building and consuming REST APIs using FastAPI or Flask, integrating analytical services into microservice-based architectures, and collaborating on frontend applications built with frameworks such as React or Angular. Experience in delivering end-to-end data products with SQL/NoSQL databases, containerized deployments, cloud services, orchestration, observability, and secure production practices for business-facing analytical applications. Experience with Azure stack would be a plus. Must Have Skill AI/ML Tools - Others,Gen AI,Python,Foundation models and API Integration Good to Have Skill Other Requirements Why Join Heineken: Be part of a globally recognized brand with a commitment to innovation and sustainability. Collaborate with a diverse and multicultural team. Drive business growth through data-driven insights and optimization. Enjoy a competitive compensation and benefits package . If you're a Data Scientist passionate about production-level machine learning, time-series forecasting, Bayesian modeling, and building end-to-end data products that connect models with real business applications, we invite you to join the Heineken team and be part of our journey to create unforgettable moments through great beer and data-driven insights. jobs.title: Platform Security Architect
jobs.description: Who We Are At Kyndryl, we run and reimagine the mission-critical technology systems that drive advantage for the world’s leading businesses. We are at the heart of progress; with proven expertise and a continuous flow of AI-powered insight, enabling smarter decisions, faster innovation, and a lasting competitive edge. For our people—Kyndryls—that means doing purposeful work that powers human progress. Join us and experience a flexible, supportive environment where your well-being is prioritized and your potential can thrive. The Role Your Role We are seeking a Platform Security Architect to serve as a trusted advisor, shaping how security is embedded into modern private cloud and platform engineering environments. This role sits at the intersection of platform engineering, DevSecOps, and developer experience, with a strong emphasis on advisory, architecture definition, and governance. You will bring deep real-world delivery experience to ensure that recommendations are practical, scalable, and proven in production. You will support Consult-led opportunities across the full lifecycle (pre- and post-sale), working with clients on first-of-a-kind private cloud migration and modernization initiatives, including navigating sovereignty requirements and evolving regulatory landscapes. To our clients, you are the subject matter expert—engaging early, shaping the solution, defining architecture, and ultimately leading technical delivery. What you will do The Platform Security Architect is responsible for advising clients on the design and security of modern private cloud and platform engineering environments by defining target-state architectures, enforceable standards, and non-bypassable security guardrails. This includes shaping secure Internal Developer Platforms (IDPs), embedding policy-as-code governance, and establishing repeatable "golden paths" that enforce secure-by-default patterns across applications, Kubernetes, and infrastructure. The role also addresses the emerging threat of AI-accelerated vulnerability exploitation (informed by frameworks such as Mythos / Project Glasswing), defining architecture and controls that close the gaps adversaries can find and weaponize faster using AI — including accelerated vulnerability discovery, automated exploit chaining, and compressed attack timelines — so that platform defenses are hardened against machine-speed threats rather than human-speed ones. A key focus is reducing configuration variability, minimizing attack surfaces, and ensuring that security is inherently built into platform design rather than applied reactively. In addition, the role drives end-to-end DevSecOps and runtime security transformation by integrating security controls into CI/CD pipelines, identity and access architectures, secrets management, and software and AI/ML supply chains. This includes architecting developer-facing tooling and testing capabilities that keep pace with today's AI-accelerated vulnerability landscape — enabling developers to identify, validate, and remediate exploitable weaknesses at the speed adversaries now operate at, rather than relying on traditional review cycles that assume human-speed attack timelines. The role further defines control frameworks, embeds continuous compliance, enables behavior-based runtime detection, and integrates real-time security feedback into developer workflows to maintain velocity without compromising governance. The architect also leads client engagements across pre- and post-sale phases—shaping solutions, guiding large-scale private cloud modernization programs (including sovereignty and regulatory requirements), and supporting go-to-market efforts through workshops, pilots, and thought leadership that advance Kyndryl's platform security and AI-risk mitigation capabilities. Your future at Kyndryl This role opens the door to many career paths, both vertical and horizontal, and there may be opportunity to travel. It’s a great chance for database administrators or other techs to break into the cloud. It’s also a solid path to become enterprise or chief architect or a distinguished engineer! Whatever you see for yourself, you’ll find the opportunity here. Who You Are You’re good at what you do and possess the required experience to prove it. However, equally as important – you have a growth mindset; keen to drive your own personal and professional development. You are customer-focused – someone who prioritizes customer success in their work. And finally, you’re open and borderless – naturally inclusive in how you work with others. Required Technical and Professional Expertise 8+ years in platform architecture, platform engineering, or security engineering, with a strong advisory focus Demonstrated experience designing and guiding platform transformations, not just implementing them Deep expertise in DevSecOps practices, secure software delivery, and CI/CD pipeline security integration Strong background in Kubernetes security and platform design principles Experience defining policy-as-code, governance models, and security frameworks Hands-on experience with identity, access control, and secrets management, informing advisory credibility Experience addressing AI-accelerated attack patterns or advising on emerging AI-driven threat models, including architecting defenses and developer tooling that close vulnerability windows at machine speed Preferred Technical and Professional Experience Experience advising on VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF), NSX, vDefend or other private cloud platforms Exposure to AI-enabled security tooling and modern threat response models Experience with Internal Developer Platforms (e.g., Backstage) in design or advisory contexts Experience with behavior-based or runtime detection capabilities Experience supporting pre-sales or client advisory engagements, including workshops, pilots, and solution shaping Familiarity with sovereignty and regulatory requirements in large-scale cloud modernization programs Being You The “Kyn” in Kyndryl means kinship, which represents the strong bonds we have with each other, our customers and our communities. We focus on ensuring all Kyndryls feel included and we welcome people of all cultures, backgrounds, and experiences. Even if you don’t meet every requirement, we encourage you to apply. We believe in growth, and we’re excited to see what you can bring. At Kyndryl, employee feedback has told us that our number one driver of employee engagement is belonging. That sense of belonging — being a valued, respected, trusted member of the team — is fundamental to our culture and fueling great experiences for our customers.
